roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.reason: Locked in as the top overall fantasy QB — top-9 in passing yards 5 of the last 6 years, top-7 in passing TDs every year, with real rushing/scramble equity on top. Historic Week 2 Thursday-night performance in a 41-31 win over Detroit: 317 total yards and 5 total TDs (3 pass, 2 rush), over 40 fantasy points — per ESPN, only the 3rd player in NFL history with 9 total TDs and 0 turnovers through a team's first 2 games (Mahomes 2018, Manning 2013 the others). NEW: banged up late in Week 3's win over the Chargers — took a helmet to the outside of his left knee in the 4th quarter and was seen favoring the leg postgame. No formal diagnosis announced, but medical analysts (Dr. David Chao) describe him as "more hurt than injured," floating a possible grade 1-2 MCL sprain that could range from full Week 4 availability to a 1-3 week absence (Buffalo Rumblings, SI, Yahoo Sports, 9/28-29). Officially Questionable entering Week 4 vs. New England and likely limited in practice early in the week — worth checking the Friday injury report before locking him in. UPDATE (9/30): the left knee scare from Week 3 is a non-issue — Allen practiced in full Wednesday with no brace or visible limitation, and HC Joe Brady said "I'm not concerned with Josh." He is NOT listed on the Week 4 injury report at all ahead of Sunday's game vs. New England (Buffalo Rumblings, CBS Sports, RotoWire, 9/30). Week 4 final (10/4): the knee was a total non-issue, but Buffalo lost its first game of the season, 29-26 at home to New England (fell to 3-1). Allen went 23/33 for 253 yards and 1 passing TD (34-yd to Keon Coleman) plus 5 carries for 4 yards and a rushing TD -- but threw a game-sealing INT with 1:14 left. He also became Buffalo's all-time TD leader on the score. No health concerns entering Week 5 (ESPN, Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 10/4).

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.reason: Widely projected as the 2026 fantasy #1 overall pick — back-to-back 1,400+ rush-yard seasons plus 60+ catches gives him a McCaffrey-type dual-threat ceiling. The camp hold-in is fully resolved: signed a 3-year, $75M extension ($51M guaranteed) with Atlanta in early August 2026, ending the contract-driven absence before the season started (NFL.com). Backed up the elite billing with a dominant Thursday-night Week 3 performance in the 35-14 win over Green Bay: 29 carries for 194 yards and 2 rushing TDs, plus 2 catches for 19 yards — 213 total yards from scrimmage (CBS Sports, 9/24).

roster.name: Chase Brown
roster.reason: Top-5, arguably top-3 PPR RB potential — posted 7 top-12 weekly finishes even through Burrow's 2025 absence; Samaje Perine remains mild committee/handcuff risk. Backed up a strong Week 1 with 20 carries for 80 yards plus 3 catches on 5 targets in Cincinnati's 20-6 win over Houston in Week 2 — 42-of-60 snaps, 36 carries and 11 targets through two games confirms bell-cow usage (Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports).

roster.name: Christian Watson
roster.reason: No PUP/injury drama to open 2026 — signed a 4-year, $110.5M extension in June and entered the season atop Green Bay's WR depth chart, fully healthy. Delivered as the Packers' clear outside WR1 in the Week 1 win at Minnesota: 6 catches for 147 yards and 2 TDs on 8 targets, well ahead of Matthew Golden in target share. Kept it up in Thursday night's Week 3 loss at Atlanta (35-14): led the team with 7 catches on 10 targets for 96 yards and a TD (4-yard grab that opened the scoring) — remains Green Bay's clear top target earner even in a blowout loss (RotoWire/CBS Sports, 9/24). NEW (10/23): Watson was listed with an ankle injury and was a limited practice participant Wednesday 10/21 ahead of Sunday's Week 7 game at Detroit (Packers' injury report via TheFantasyFootballers, 10/21) -- Green Bay's first injury blemish of the season for him after three clean weeks as the clear WR1. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending Friday's final status; no report yet that he'll miss time. CLEARED (10/25): carries no injury designation into today's Week 7 game at Detroit -- the ankle issue that popped up last week (limited practice Wed 10/21), Green Bay's first injury blemish of the season for him, resolved cleanly. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. Week 7 result (10/29): played through the previously-cleared ankle issue with no setback in Sunday's Week 7 loss at Detroit (10/25) -- exact catch/yard line could not be independently confirmed via box score as of this update, but the team's own tracker credits him 10.7 fantasy points for the game. Remains Healthy; no new injury-report concern heading into Week 8. NEW -- BROKEN RIB (10/31): suffered a broken rib (plus a chest injury that had him coughing up blood) during Thursday night's 27-19 win over Carolina (10/29) and was taken to a hospital by ambulance for precautionary testing -- X-rays confirmed the fracture but a CT scan and bloodwork showed no internal bleeding or further damage, and he dramatically returned to the game in the 3rd quarter to keep playing (Yahoo Sports, NFL.com, Packers.com, Bleacher Report, 10/29-30). Carries a QUESTIONABLE tag into Green Bay's Week 9 game at New England (Sun 11/8) -- no outlet has reported a specific return timeline yet, and it's not yet clear whether more than one rib is involved, so treat the timeline as genuinely unresolved rather than guessing a duration. Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty; recommend confirming practice participation reports next week before locking him into a Week 9 lineup. CLEARED TO PLAY (11/4-8): progressed from a limited Wednesday practice to practicing in pads Thursday on the broken rib/chest injury suffered in the Week 8 Thursday-night win over Carolina (10/29) -- our roster feed shows him cleared to Active for today's road game at New England with no new setback reported. No official diagnosis update beyond the original fracture; downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Health Watch given the clearance, though a fresh rib fracture carries real re-injury risk worth monitoring in-game. CLEARED, RESOLVED (11/8-10): carried no injury designation into Sunday's Week 9 road game at New England and played -- the broken rib/chest injury from the 10/29 hospitalization has fully healed with no setback reported. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. Stat line not independently confirmable via search as of this update.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.reason: Missed Week 1 (meniscus trim surgery in early September) and Week 2 at the Chargers, then came down to a Sunday game-time call for Week 3 vs. New Orleans. CLEARED AND DELIVERED: officially active roughly 2 hours before kickoff and made a monstrous 2026 season debut in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Saints — 10 catches on 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown (CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 9/27), instantly re-establishing himself as Las Vegas' clear top receiving option. No re-aggravation reported after the workload; Michael Mayer moves back to a clear TE2 role now that Bowers has cleared and produced in the same game. UPDATE (10/8): Bowers has carried a QUESTIONABLE tag in each of the last two weeks -- an illness (not his earlier knee issue) was the reported cause ahead of Week 4 vs. Kansas City, and the Raiders expected him to play (ESPN's Adam Schefter, 10/4); he's QUESTIONABLE again for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. New England, though the specific reason behind this week's tag hadn't been reported by beat writers as of Wednesday. CLEARED (10/8): upgraded from limited to a full practice participant Thursday on the knee, trending toward playing Sunday's Week 5 game vs. New England -- no setback reported from the illness-related QUESTIONABLE tag he carried into Week 4 (Yahoo Sports/Raiders beat, 10/8). NEW DESIGNATION (10/16): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag for the first time this week, but it's the same knee the Raiders have been proactively managing in practice all season, not a new injury -- limited Wednesday, upgraded to a full practice Thursday (10/14-10/15). FantasyPros projects him at 94% to play Sunday vs. Buffalo (10/18); this matches his standard early-week rest pattern rather than a real setback. CLEARED (10/17): logged back-to-back full practices Thursday and Friday and carries NO injury designation into Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Buffalo -- officially off the injury report entirely (NBC Sports, 10/16). Remains the overall TE1 play this week. NEW (10/23): the knee has been a weekly practice-management issue all season since September's meniscus trim, with a limited-Wednesday-then-clears pattern repeating most weeks. That pattern looks to be repeating into Week 7 vs. the Rams (Sunday 10/25, home) behind today's QUESTIONABLE tag; he has cleared every prior 'limited' designation to play since early October and remains Las Vegas' clear top receiving weapon (NBC Sports/Rotoworld, FanDuel Research). Recommend confirming Friday's official designation directly. Keeping Health Watch given the chronic-but-played-through pattern. CLEARED (10/24): per our roster feed, the knee-management flag resolved again and he carries no designation into Sunday's Week 7 home game vs. the Rams -- the same pattern he's cleared nearly every week since the September meniscus trim. Remains Las Vegas' clear top receiving weapon; keeping Health Watch given the chronic (though consistently played-through) nature of the knee management. WEEK 7 RESULT (10/30): the Rams beat the Raiders 35-21 on 10/25 at Allegiant Stadium; Bowers had carried a pre-game QUESTIONABLE tag (knee) per a Fox Sports preview, but his actual catch/yard/TD line from that game could not be confirmed via box score search. Las Vegas's Week 8 opponent is the Jets (Sun. 11/1, MetLife Stadium); no Week 8-specific report found yet for the chronic knee-management pattern. Keeping Health Watch given the season-long played-through pattern. CLEARED (10/31): this week's practice-management flag was a calf issue (not the chronic knee) -- limited Wednesday, then back-to-back full practices Thursday and Friday, and off Las Vegas's Week 8 injury report entirely heading into Sunday's game at the Jets (11/1) (Yahoo Sports/USA Today, Raiders.com, 10/30). Keeping Health Watch given the recurring in-season management pattern, but no setback and no missed-game risk this week.

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.reason: The groin injury was fully resolved for Week 1 — played through it with no setback, catching all 5 targets for 63 yards vs. Carolina. UPDATE: caught an 8-yard TD from Case Keenum in Chicago's 27-7 Week 3 upset of Philadelphia (Monday Night, 9/28) — his first score of the season, with Keenum starting in place of the injured Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent. BIG GAME, THEN FADED (10/22): exploded for 4 catches, 130 yards and a TD in the first half of Thursday's 30-24 win over New England, then was held without a catch in the second half as Rome Odunze took over down the stretch (CBS Sports, 10/22-23). First real explosive game of the season -- adding Breakout Watch alongside Healthy. NEW QUESTIONABLE TAG (11/10): picked up a fresh QUESTIONABLE designation for Week 10 after previously being fully cleared (Healthy) -- specific new injury/practice report not independently confirmed via search as of this update. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending more detail. NEW QUESTIONABLE TAG (11/9-10): picked up a QUESTIONABLE designation this week with no fresh injury report confirmed via search as of this update -- treating this as a likely weekly placeholder reset pending confirmation rather than a new setback.

roster.name: Jalen Coker
roster.reason: Caught 8-of-9 targets in EACH of Carolina's first two games (Week 1: 8/138 yds/2 TD vs. Chicago; Week 2: 8/66 yds vs. Atlanta) with Bryce Young — became just the 3rd undrafted player since 1967 to reach 15+ catches, 200+ receiving yards and 2+ TDs through a team's first two games (Yahoo Sports/Heavy, 9/23). No longer just a presumptive WR2 behind McMillan — now viewed as a legitimate 1A/1B. UPDATE: played through the ankle issue that had triggered a Week 3 Questionable tag, but exited Sunday's 21-18 loss to Cleveland early with a new quad strain, finishing limited to 2 catches for 18 yards. Monday follow-up tests found nothing overly significant on the quad — described as a relatively minor strain. He's Questionable for Week 4 vs. Detroit, with his Wednesday-Friday practice activity set to determine availability (SI/OnSI, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 9/28-29). Downgrading tag from a standalone injury tier to Health Watch given the "relatively minor" framing and no ruled-out signal yet. WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/5): downgraded from QUESTIONABLE to OUT today -- the quad strain suffered vs. Cleveland in Week 3 (originally called "relatively minor" by Ian Rapoport) has not resolved on the Wed-Fri practice ramp-up as hoped. No multi-week timeline has been disclosed, but Carolina has an IR transaction history on this same quad earlier in the season, raising some risk the team manages it conservatively. Bumping tag from Health Watch to standard Injury given the confirmed missed game and recurrence on the same body part. REVISED TO LONG-TERM, CORRECTED (10/7): Carolina placed Coker on IR, and ESPN's David Newton reported an expected 4-to-6 game absence -- HC Dave Canales called it a "serious quad strain," a firmer and worse timeline than the earlier "relatively minor" read. Revising tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury given the confirmed 4+ game IR window. IMPORTANT CONTEXT: the Panthers are on their Week 5 BYE, so there is no Week 5 game/opponent for him either way -- today's QUESTIONABLE roster status is a placeholder, not a game-week designation. He's now inside his 21-day practice window (eligible to return from IR) but has not yet been designated to return; realistic target is Week 6 or later, post-bye. CLEARED (10/16): practiced in full Wednesday (10/14) with no designation on Carolina's injury report, ending the IR stint -- HC Dave Canales called him "on track" to play Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Philadelphia (10/18) (NBC Sports/Sharp Football, 10/13-14). Softening tag from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch; expect his workload eased in his first game back before he reclaims a full target share. NEW (10/28): A new shoulder injury (unrelated to the earlier quad strain) surfaced on Carolina's short-week injury report ahead of Thursday night's game at Green Bay (10/29) -- limited Monday (10/26), upgraded to full practice Tuesday (10/27) per Panthers.com/NBC Sports. No formal game-status designation attached as of Tuesday; trending toward playing Thursday. WEEK 8 FINAL (10/30): Carolina fell 19-27 to Green Bay in Thursday Night Football (10/29), dropping to 3-4; no individual box-score line for Coker's targets/catches/yards could be confirmed via search as of this update -- flagging as unconfirmed rather than inventing a stat.

roster.name: Jakobi Meyers
roster.reason: NEW PROFILE: acquired via trade from the Raiders at the 2025 deadline, now extended through 2028 -- projected as Jacksonville's No. 2/3 target behind Brian Thomas Jr., sharing the WR room with Travis Hunter and Parker Washington. Season totals through Week 7: 28 targets, 20 catches, 285 yards, 2 TDs -- a steady but modest floor piece rather than a clear volume lock, with some reports noting Parker Washington has out-snapped him in recent weeks. NEW (10/30): carries a QUESTIONABLE tag for Sunday's Week 8 home game vs. Indianapolis. He has dealt with a recurring thumb injury off and on since August/September, but no specific October practice report could be confirmed via search as of this update -- treat this week's tag cautiously rather than attach a specific cause. Keeping Committee role expectations; recommend confirming Friday's designation. CONFIRMED (11/3): active and played through the hamstring/ankle issue in Jacksonville's lopsided 42-7 Week 8 win over Indianapolis (11/1) -- Trevor Lawrence threw 3 TD passes (one to Brian Thomas Jr.) and Bhayshul Tuten ran for 104 yards and a score as the Jaguars improved to 5-2 and took control of the AFC South (ESPN, Yahoo Sports, Jaguars.com, 11/1). Meyers' individual catch line could not be independently confirmed via search as of this update, but no new injury concern was reported. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. NEW (11/2-3): back on Jacksonville's injury report with hamstring and ankle issues, limited both Monday and Tuesday ahead of Thursday night's short-week game at Baltimore -- officially TBD for Week 9 as of Wednesday. He played through a similar hamstring/ankle issue in Week 8's blowout win over Indianapolis and led the team in targets that game, so this looks like managed maintenance rather than a new setback, but worth confirming he clears Wednesday's final practice. Downgrading from Healthy to Health Watch pending that (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, 11/2-3). CLEARED (11/6): the hamstring/ankle TBD tag from this week's short-week report resolved -- carries no game-status designation after Jacksonville's 33-10 road blowout of Baltimore (TNF, 11/5), which improved the Jaguars to 6-2 (CBS Sports, NBC Sports, Jaguars.com, 11/5). Individual catch/target line unconfirmed via box score as of this update. Upgrading tag from Health Watch back to Healthy.

No specific beneficiary (DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir) has been reported if he sits. Monitor Monday's final game-day call. CLEARED (11/9): back to an ACTIVE designation on our roster feed ahead of Buffalo's Week 9 Monday Night Football game at Minnesota, after being limited in practice Thursday and Friday with the shoulder issue -- Bills beat coverage (SI Bills Central) had already called it 'not overly serious,' and the clean roster status confirms he's good to go. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.reason: Clear backup, not a starter — Breece Hall re-signed and remains the workhorse; Allen competes with Isaiah Davis for change-of-pace touches. UPDATE (9/30): Breece Hall (thigh/quad) will not play Week 4, and Allen is set to start in his place — he flashed in relief during Week 3's loss to Detroit (4 carries for 14 yards and a TD) after Hall exited. Treat as the clear lead-back option for as long as Hall is out (CBS Sports, NBC Sports, SI/OnSI, 9/28). Week 4 final (10/4): took every single Jets RB carry in the 23-12 loss to Chicago -- 14 carries for 59 yards (4.2 YPC) plus 2 catches for 8 yards. Volume was capped by the Jets' anemic 32 offensive plays, not a snap-share concern. With Breece Hall still out (see his note, remains week-to-week with no firm return date), Allen looks like the clear every-down back rather than a committee piece -- upgrading tag from Depth Chart Battle to Depth Chart Secured (NBC Sports, NYJets.com, CBS Sports, 10/4-5). Week 5 final (10/11): career-best game with Breece Hall again out -- 24 carries for 116 yards (4.8 YPC) and the game-winning 22-yard TD run on 3rd down in a 17-12 win over Cleveland, playing 60 of 70 snaps (85.7%). Added 1 catch on 4 targets for 0 yards. Remains the clear lead back as long as Hall is out. NEW (10/30): limited at Wednesday's Week 8 practice (The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt, 10/28) ahead of Sunday's home game vs. the Raiders -- body part not clearly confirmed (one outlet says ankle, another lists it as undisclosed). More notably, Breece Hall (quad) also returned to limited practice that same day after missing 4 straight games -- a real signal he's trending toward a Week 8 return, which would cut into Allen's workload. No final Friday designation found for either back. Adding Health Watch; monitor Hall's snap share Sunday. CLEARED, BUT WATCH HALL (10/31): Allen's own ankle issue (limited Wednesday) resolved with no game designation for Sunday's home game vs. the Raiders (11/1); upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. Bigger storyline for his workload: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in practice all three days this week and is listed QUESTIONABLE -- a real game-time decision after missing four straight games -- per HC Aaron Glenn and the Jets' official injury report (NBC Sports, 10/30). If Hall is active Sunday, expect him to cut into Allen's touches for the first time since Week 3; if Hall sits again, Allen remains the clear starter.

roster.name: David Montgomery
roster.reason: Trade acquisition from DET leads the Houston backfield, and Joe Mixon's release clears out the only other real competition — but Woody Marks still holds real passing-down/receiving touches, so it remains a genuine committee, not a clear lead back. NEW (10/13): suffered a groin injury early in the 2nd quarter of Sunday's Week 5 win over Tennessee (26-3), exiting after just 5 carries for 11 yards (Houston Chronicle, RotoWire, ESPN, 10/11-12). HC DeMeco Ryans called it "week-to-week" Monday with no hard return date, matching today's flip to DOUBTFUL -- picking the standard Injury tier given the genuinely uncertain timeline. Woody Marks (see his note) took over as the lead back the rest of the game and is confirmed to handle the workload if Montgomery sits further; Ryans said Marks "will carry the load for us." UPDATE (10/15): no fresher practice-report confirmation found beyond HC DeMeco Ryans' Monday (10/12) "week-to-week" comments -- no official Wed/Thu Week 6 designation located via search yet. 4for4's analysis says he's "very likely" to miss Week 6, and flags that Houston's upcoming bye week could extend the absence further before a firm return estimate emerges. Woody Marks (see his note) is confirmed as the Week 6 lead back regardless. CONFIRMED OUT (10/16): officially ruled out for Sunday's Week 6 game at Jacksonville in London (10/18) with the groin injury suffered late in the Week 5 win over Tennessee, after zero practice reps Wednesday or Thursday. HC DeMeco Ryans calls it "week-to-week," with reporting (NBC Sports, National Football Post) pointing to a Week 7 vs. the Giants target return -- Houston's bye isn't until Week 8, so there's no extra cushion this week. Upgrading tag to Short-Term Injury given the firm ~1-week target; Woody Marks remains the clear lead back in the meantime. UPDATE (10/22): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip lines up with the new Week 7 practice-report cycle (Houston hosts the Giants Sun 10/25), but no independent beat reporting confirming his actual Wednesday practice participation was found as of this update -- one outlet speculates he could target a Week 7 return but explicitly flags that as unconfirmed, not an official report. Keeping the Short-Term Injury tier from last week's ~1-week target rather than overclaiming a confirmed recovery; recheck Thursday/Friday's report. Woody Marks remains the lead back in the meantime. WORSENED, TIMELINE WALKED BACK (10/23-24): the original ~1-week target has now slipped -- multiple outlets (NFL.com, Sportsbook Review, NBC Sports' Aaron Wilson) report Montgomery has not practiced since the Week 5 groin injury and is not expected to play Sunday's Week 7 home game vs. the Giants, which would be a second straight missed game; our roster feed's QUESTIONABLE-to-DOUBTFUL flip matches this. No new 4+ game/IR signal, so not yet Long-Term, but the firm short-term framing from two weeks ago hasn't held up. Revising tag from Short-Term Injury back to the standard Injury tier. Woody Marks remains Houston's clear lead back regardless. CONFIRMED OUT (10/25): officially ruled out for today's Week 7 home game vs. the Giants, confirming yesterday's note -- still hasn't practiced since the Week 5 groin injury, a second straight missed game. Woody Marks remains Houston's clear lead back. Keeping the standard Injury tier. NO CHANGE (10/28): Status flip to QUESTIONABLE is a false signal -- the Texans are on their Week 8 bye (no game 10/29-11/2), so there's no new practice or game report possible this week. Last real status stands: groin injury since Week 5, OUT again for Week 7 (10/25 vs. the Giants, a 27-21 OT loss), Woody Marks remains Houston's clear lead back. Watch his actual Week 9 (at the Chargers, 11/8) injury report for the real signal. ESCALATING, REVISED TO LONG-TERM (11/6): ruled OUT again for Sunday's Week 9 game at the Chargers -- HC DeMeco Ryans said Monday he had "no significant update" on the groin injury first suffered Week 5 (10/11) (per The Fantasy Footballers/4for4 Week 9 coverage, 11/2-4). This will be a third missed game (Weeks 6-7, now 9, plus the Week 8 bye) with no practice logged since the original injury nearly a month ago and no firm return date given -- revising the tag from the standard Injury tier to Long-Term Injury given the real, reported month-plus absence, up from the original 1-2 week framing. Woody Marks remains Houston's clear lead back in the meantime. QUESTIONABLE FLIP LOOKS PREMATURE, KEEP LONG-TERM (11/9-11): HC DeMeco Ryans told KPRC2's Aaron Wilson (11/9) he's 'hopeful' to get Montgomery back to practicing this week or next -- notably a practice-return hope, not a game-return claim, and he still hasn't practiced since the original Oct. 11 groin injury. The QUESTIONABLE flip for Week 10 (vs. Cleveland, Sun. 11/15) has no corroborating medical news behind it. Keeping Long-Term Injury; Woody Marks remains Houston's clear lead back. STILL OUT, GROIN UNCHANGED (11/11-13): sat out Wednesday's practice again with the Week 5 groin injury ahead of Sunday's Week 10 road game at Cleveland -- Sharp Football Analysis has him Limited Thursday with SI's preview listing him Questionable, but our roster feed already shows OUT, consistent with the pattern of this injury never clearing a practice session since October. No fresh diagnosis or timeline beyond HC DeMeco Ryans' 'hopeful' comment from 11/9. Woody Marks (see his note) remains Houston's lead back. Keeping Long-Term Injury. DATA/REALITY CONFLICT, STILL LIKELY OUT (11/13-14): roster feed flips him from OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 10 road game at Cleveland, but real reporting doesn't support a clearance -- as of this week's coverage he still hadn't been seen back at practice since the original Week 5 groin injury, and RotoWire's Week 10 analysis says he's 'likely, but not certain' to miss another game, adding he needs to resume practicing before fantasy managers can seriously consider starting him. Treating the QUESTIONABLE flip as a probable data lag, consistent with the pattern this injury has shown since October. Woody Marks remains Houston's clear lead back. Keeping Long-Term Injury.

roster.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
roster.reason: Wasn't the clear lead back in Week 2 — White out-snapped him 36-23 in the Dallas loss (9/20) as the Commanders leaned on White's receiving in a trailing game script. Treat this as a genuine 2-man committee rather than a locked-in CM1 role, even after his confirmed Week 1 lead-back role vs. Philadelphia. NEW (10/8): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag in this week's injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants; specific injury type was not confirmed by beat writers as of Wednesday -- recheck once Washington's Thursday/Friday reports post. Still working as part of a 2-man committee with Rachaad White. CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants -- no setback reported from this week's unspecified issue. Still in a backfield mix with Rachaad White (also cleared, see his note); Washington waived depth piece Kaytron Allen this week, slightly simplifying the committee (RotoBaller, 10/8-9). Dropping the Health Watch tag now that he's cleared. NEW (10/15-16): a groin injury (recurring from Week 5) kept him off the practice field entirely both Thursday and Friday ahead of Monday night's Week 6 game at San Francisco (10/19) -- ESPN's John Keim flagged the Thursday absence as a real watch item. Re-adding the Health Watch tag given the back-to-back DNPs; no severity or ruled-out/doubtful designation confirmed yet, recheck Saturday's report. Rachaad White would see the bulk of the backfield work if he sits. CONFIRMED OUT (10/18, final): HC Dan Quinn confirmed Saturday that Croskey-Merritt is out for tonight's Monday Night Football Week 6 game at San Francisco (10/19) with the same recurring groin injury -- he did not practice at all this week (SI/Yahoo Sports Commanders injury reports, 10/17-18). Rachaad White (shoulder, cleared) and Austin Ekeler (chest, cleared) are set to handle the bulk of Washington's backfield work in his absence -- see White's note. PLACED ON IR (10/19-21): officially moved to injured reserve with a groin reinjury (first hurt in preseason, reaggravated in the Week 5 tie vs. the Giants) -- HC Dan Quinn called it a reinjury, and per Ian Rapoport he's out at least through Week 10 (NFL Network, RotoBaller, TSN, 10/19). Across 5 games this season he had 67 carries for 239 yards and 2 TDs in a committee with Rachaad White. Washington's backfield now projects as a White/Austin Ekeler/Jeremy McNichols (activated off IR Monday) committee in his absence. Upgrading tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury given the official IR move and the ~4-game minimum absence.

roster.name: Tyreek Hill
roster.reason: Suffered a severe left knee injury (dislocation with torn ACL/MCL/PCL and patella damage) on Sept 29, 2025 vs. New England, requiring surgery; Miami released him in February 2026 as expected. Remains an unsigned free agent as of Sept 2026 — has not retired, but has also not signed with any team. Publicly says his recovery "timeline looking real good" but has also said he still has "no power" in the left leg; agent Drew Rosenhaus has indicated doctors want to hold off on a comeback attempt until at least October 2026. Not rostered by any NFL team — unplayable/bench for now; monitor for a signing or workout announcement. UPDATE (10/13): still unsigned -- agent Drew Rosenhaus called the free-agency situation "fluid," telling reporters "I think a deal could happen anytime" and naming the Chiefs as a plausible contender fit given Hill's stated preference to sign only with a Super Bowl-caliber team needing WR help (RotoBaller, CBS Sports, 10/13). No team has signed him as of this update. Today's in-system flip from OUT to QUESTIONABLE does not correspond to any real NFL game-status designation since he isn't on any team's roster -- treat it as a data artifact, not real news. Remains unplayable/bench.

roster.name: Joe Burrow
roster.reason: Played through the back tightness as expected — active and started Cincinnati's 20-6 win over Houston (Sun 9/20), going 20/31 for 207 yards and 2 TDs (both to Ja'Marr Chase, from 32 and 18 yards) with no INTs, though he did take 5 sacks. Confirms the back issue was minor/day-to-day as reported all week — no setback, no in-game re-aggravation reported, and no new limitation entering Week 3 prep. Elite passing-volume QB1 when right — the profile concern remains price/ADP more than health at this point.

roster.name: Kenneth Walker III
roster.reason: Immediately looks like the lead back in Kansas City's backfield after the free-agent signing (3yr/$43.05M) — leads the NFL with 47 carries (56 touches) through 2 games, backing up a Week 1 explosion (23-173-1 rush, 2 total TDs vs. Denver) with a Week 2 workhorse outing (24-117 rush, 6 catches/61 yds vs. Indianapolis). CONFIRMED: despite HC Andy Reid's talk of "balance" with rookie Emmett Johnson, Walker's Week 3 role barely budged — 78% of the RB snaps and 20 of 23 RB carry opportunities before the final drive, extending his streak to three straight weeks with a 70%+ snap share and 20+ PPR points in a 24-10 win over Miami. Dolphins did hold him to just 16 yards from scrimmage after halftime, worth monitoring, but the workhorse role itself is unchanged (Arrowhead Pride, RotoWire, 9/28).

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.reason: Led Buffalo's backfield as expected in the opener vs. Houston: 13 carries for 57 yards and 3 catches for 12 yards, though he didn't find the end zone in a game the Bills controlled on the ground. Signed a 4-year, $48M extension (up to $30M guaranteed) in August 2025, locking him in through 2029.

roster.name: Justin Jefferson
roster.reason: Down year by his own standard in 2025 (WR30 overall) but still finished 6th league-wide in target share (28.5%) — new QB Kyler Murray has a track record of feeding elite WR1s. Left Sunday's Week 3 win over Tampa Bay (23-16) early in the 1st quarter with a left ankle injury after a defender landed on it during a 10-yard screen reception, and did not return. NEW: Monday's MRI (9/28) revealed a clean ankle sprain with no structural/long-term damage — a real relief given the initial fear of a high-ankle or deltoid-ligament issue. HC Kevin O'Connell called the outlook positive and said the team will manage his practice reps through the week to gauge Week 4 availability vs. Miami; there's a real chance he plays (ESPN, NBC Sports, Bleacher Report, Athlon, 9/28-29). Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch given the clean imaging and plausible Week 4 clearance. WORSENED (10/2-3): despite the clean MRI and earlier optimism, Jefferson was officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. Miami (CBS Sports' Week 4 injury report, PrizePicks, 10/2-3) -- the ankle sprain needed more than a week of management after all. Bumping tag from Health Watch to Injury; no multi-week timeline reported, so treat as a week-to-week absence for now rather than Short/Long-Term. TRENDING UP (10/7): QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at New Orleans. HC Kevin O'Connell said as of 10/3-4 that Jefferson has made "great progress" on the ankle, though it's "too early to say" definitively if he plays (ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, Fox9, NBC Sports). No setback reported since last week's OUT designation -- keeping the Injury tag for now given he's not yet confirmed to play, but this reads as a real step toward a Week 5 return rather than a new concern. UPDATE (10/8): was a limited practice participant to begin Week 5 prep (Wednesday, 10/7) for Sunday's game at New Orleans -- a step up from last week's OUT designation, though not yet confirmation he plays. Final designation comes Friday. CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/12): played a full workload in Sunday's Week 5 win at New Orleans (Vikings won 23-13 to improve to 5-0 and head into their bye) with no setback from the ankle -- 6 catches for 79 yards and a touchdown (a 15-yard TD from Kyler Murray in the 3rd quarter), his first score since Week 1. Upgrading tag from Injury to Healthy given the clean workload and no re-aggravation. NEW (10/23): Flip to QUESTIONABLE is tied to the same surgically-clean left ankle from Week 3 -- Jefferson was a limited practice participant Wednesday 10/21 ahead of Sunday's Week 7 home game vs. Indianapolis (Vikings' official injury report via RotoBaller, 4for4, 10/21-22). No new setback reported; HC Kevin O'Connell may simply be managing his in-season reps coming off the bye rather than a real flare-up, and he could still upgrade off the report by Friday. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending final Friday designation -- treat as likely-to-play barring a Friday downgrade. WEEK 7 RESULT (10/30): Minnesota beat Indianapolis 16-10 (10/25) -- Jefferson caught 4 of 7 targets for 44 yards, a quiet game by his standard but with no new injury concern reported (The Fantasy Footballers Week 7 recap). Minnesota's Week 8 opponent is a road trip to Detroit (Sun. 11/1).

roster.name: Tee Higgins
roster.reason: Played through a heel contusion in Week 1, catching 3 of 6 targets for 59 yards. NEW (9/30): ruled OUT for Thursday's Week 4 game at Jacksonville with a shoulder injury, after not practicing Wednesday (CBS Sports, FantasyPros, RotoWire, 9/30). Reporting doesn't yet specify when the shoulder issue arose or a return timeline — flagging this as fresh news since our own roster tracker's status field hasn't yet caught up to the OUT designation. S Jessie Bates III (neck) is also out for Cincinnati Thursday. Ja'Marr Chase remains the clear top target in his absence. UPDATE (10/5): missed a second straight game with the shoulder injury in Thursday's Week 4 loss to Jacksonville, never practicing that week (CBS Sports, National Football Post, Sportskeeda, 10/1-2). Today's flip from OUT back to QUESTIONABLE suggests real practice-field progress toward a return -- HC Zac Taylor has called him "on the right trajectory to play" -- but no firm return date has been reported yet, so keeping the standard Injury tier rather than Short-Term. Ja'Marr Chase remains Cincinnati's clear top target in his continued absence. CORRECTION (10/8): previous notes describing a 'shoulder' injury that kept Higgins out of the Jacksonville game were inaccurate. The real story: Higgins played in Week 4's 22-17 loss to Jacksonville and had a big game (11 catches for 157 yards on 16 targets) before hurting his adductor on a late sideline catch, leaving briefly and managing one final-drive snap. HC Zac Taylor called him day-to-day Monday and did not rule him out for Sunday's Week 5 game at Miami, alongside Ja'Marr Chase's concussion situation (FieldLevelMedia, RotoBaller, 4for4, 10/5). Downgrading tag from Injury to Health Watch given the day-to-day framing and that he already played through it once. CLEARED (10/12): played through the adductor injury with no setback reported in Sunday's Week 5 win at Miami (Bengals won 31-24, now 3-2); specific catch/yardage totals for Higgins could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update. Ja'Marr Chase (see his note) also cleared concussion protocol and had a big game in the same contest.

roster.name: Sam LaPorta
roster.reason: The hip flare-up was a non-issue once games started — produced in both Week 1 (9.8 fantasy pts, opener vs. New Orleans) and Week 2 (17.2 fantasy pts in Thursday night's win over Buffalo), with no re-aggravation reported.

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.reason: Elite volume floor even coming off a down 2025 — earned a 30%+ target share early last season and has topped 23% every year of his career. NEW (11/4-5): in the concussion protocol, a non-participant at Wednesday's practice ahead of Sunday's Week 9 home game vs. Kansas City -- officially Questionable, with HC Aaron Glenn and the team not yet confirming he's cleared (Yahoo Sports, bet365 News, 11/4). Genuinely uncertain given the protocol has to be cleared day-by-day; adding the standard Injury tag given the real risk he's held out. Breece Hall (quad) is separately trending toward a return the same week -- see his note. CONFIRMED OUT (11/6-7): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 9 home game vs. Kansas City after a third straight non-participant practice day (Wed/Thu/Fri) in the concussion protocol -- per the Jets' official Friday injury report and AP wire coverage. HC Aaron Glenn has called him day-to-day; no clearance date reported. No confirmed beneficiary named by beat reporters as of this update. STILL IN PROTOCOL, UNCERTAIN FOR WEEK 10 (11/9-11): remains in the concussion protocol from the Week 8 hit vs. the Raiders -- missed Week 9 vs. Kansas City entirely and was unable to practice at all that week. The Jets are hoping he returns for Week 10 vs. Buffalo, but he still has to clear practice/protocol stages day-by-day, which is not guaranteed (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, Jets official site, JetNation, 11/4-11/9). Keeping the standard Injury tier given the genuine uncertainty; the QUESTIONABLE flip reflects hope more than confirmed clearance.

roster.name: Lions D/ST
roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Andre Szmyt
roster.reason: Added off waivers. Cleveland's unquestioned starting kicker for a second straight season after returning on an exclusive-rights tender signed in March 2026; no competition on the Browns' depth chart. 14-of-16 on field goals and 11-of-12 on PATs this season per our stats database -- a standard low-variance K1 role.

roster.name: Jonah Coleman
roster.reason: With both RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins banged up, Coleman led Denver's backfield in Week 2 snap share (42.4%), touches (13) and total yards (58 plus a TD) in the win over Jacksonville — his first career rushing TD. Named a top Week 3 waiver-wire target by NFL.com (9/24). REVISED (from the earlier "minor, shouldn't affect gameday status" framing, then from last update's "short absence" framing): the ankle is a high ankle sprain, and Denver placed Coleman on injured reserve Saturday (9/26) rather than just ruling him out week-to-week — he's expected back no sooner than Oct. 25 vs. Arizona (first eligible date), meaning at least 4 additional games missed on top of Week 3 (ESPN, NFL.com, Denver Gazette, CBS Sports, 9/26). Upgrading the tag from Short-Term to Long-Term Injury to reflect the real, IR-confirmed absence. The good news for Denver: both J.K. Dobbins (hip) and RJ Harvey (hamstring) escaped the injury report with no designation and are expected to play Week 3 — the backfield rotation should run through them for the next several weeks with Coleman on IR. UPDATE (10/5): remains on IR with the Week 2 high-ankle sprain, first eligible to return Week 7 (no change to the previously reported Oct. 25 vs. Arizona target). Denver lost Week 4 to the Chargers; in that game J.K. Dobbins clearly won the early-down split over RJ Harvey -- 11 carries for 83 yards and a TD plus a catch, vs. just 2 carries for 2 yards and 3 catches for 14 yards for Harvey (CBS Sports/RotoWire). Dobbins looks like the stronger side of Denver's committee right now while Coleman remains out. ACTIVATED & LED BACKFIELD (10/25): activated off IR and immediately out-touched both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey in Denver's 30-16 win over Arizona -- 9 carries for 54 yards plus 2 catches for 15 yards, vs. 6 carries/23 yards+a TD for Dobbins and just 3 carries/6 yards for Harvey (Harvey's fantasy value came via a 52-yard TD catch on a screen pass, not a carry). Dobbins reportedly left the locker room frustrated afterward, telling reporters 'I'm unavailable' and declining interviews (Yahoo Sports, Athlon, PredominantlyOrange, 10/25) -- a real signal Coleman could be climbing the pecking order in a muddled three-way committee. Downgrading tag from Long-Term Injury to reflect the activation; keeping Breakout Watch and Depth Chart Battle given the unsettled backfield hierarchy. CLEARED, Week 8 (10/27): carries no injury designation this week after Sunday's (10/25) activation and lead-role usage vs. Arizona -- officially ACTIVE with no setback reported. Denver's three-way RB committee (with J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey) remains unsettled; keeping Breakout Watch and Depth Chart Battle. UPDATE (10/31-11/1): RJ Harvey has been placed on injured reserve (knee, minimum 4 games -- see his note), leaving Denver's backfield as a two-man Coleman/J.K. Dobbins arrangement rather than the muddled three-way committee of recent weeks. Reporting frames Coleman as the lead back in the new arrangement, with Dobbins as the secondary option and Cody Schrader elevated as depth. Keeping Breakout Watch and Depth Chart Battle given Dobbins is still in the mix.

roster.name: Germie Bernard
roster.reason: NEW (10/23): Exploded for a Steelers franchise rookie-record 11 catches on 12 targets for 87 yards and his first career TD -- the OT game-winner -- in Pittsburgh's 26-19 win over Tampa Bay in Week 6, topping JuJu Smith-Schuster's 2017 rookie mark of 9 catches. NEW (10/23): Role is legit, not a one-off -- he also went 6/9/80 in Week 5. Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are both on IR, and Bernard has stepped into the slot (61% snap share, 28% target share Week 6), making him a priority add if available.

roster.name: Denzel Boston
roster.reason: 2026 second-round rookie (No. 39 overall, Washington) who opened the season in Cleveland's starting WR2 spot alongside Jerry Jeudy. Broke out in Week 2 vs. Tampa Bay with 5 catches for 95 yards and a 55-yard TD, earning an NFL Rookie of the Week nomination. NEW (10/16): picked up a foot injury this week -- logged back-to-back limited practices Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15), which is why he's carrying a QUESTIONABLE tag for the first time this season ahead of Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Baltimore (10/18). Beat writers (NBC Sports, CBS Sports) still expect him to play without real restriction. CLEARED (10/18): carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Baltimore after logging back-to-back limited practices Wednesday/Thursday -- beat reporting (NBC Sports, The Fantasy Footballers) had already expected him to play without real restriction. Dropping the Health Watch tag now that the foot issue produced no game-status designation. VERIFIED (10/23): Confirmed via independent search that Boston's real NFL team is the Cleveland Browns, matching our roster data -- no Seattle/Seahawks connection beyond his college ties to the Seattle area. NEW (10/23): Same lingering foot injury from Week 6, not a new one -- despite last week's clearance, Boston was again a limited practice participant Wednesday 10/21 (Akron Beacon Journal, via NBC Sports/TheFantasyFootballers) ahead of Sunday's Week 7 road game at Tennessee. Beat reporting says he should handle his usual workload (90%+ snaps last week) if his practice level holds or improves -- reads as minor and expected-to-play. Keeping Health Watch tag. WEEK 7 RESULT (10/30): Cleveland beat Tennessee 27-24 on the road (10/25) -- Boston was held relatively quiet with 3 catches on 8 targets for 27 yards (season totals through Week 7: 20 catches, 372 yards, 3 TDs). Fellow rookie KC Concepcion had the bigger day in that same game (8 catches, 129 yards -- see his note). No new injury reported; the foot issue that limited him in practice the past two weeks produced no setback. NEW (11/6): back to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 9 road game at New Orleans. No specific fresh practice report confirmed via search as of this update -- likely a recurrence of the lingering foot issue that has had him on and off Cleveland's injury report since Week 6, which he's played through without missing a game so far. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending Friday's report. NEW BODY PART (11/4-8): Wednesday's Week 9 injury report listed Boston as limited with a calf injury -- a different issue from the lingering foot problem that has dogged him since Week 6 (Chronicle-Telegram/Scott Petrak via RotoBaller, NBC Sports, 11/4). No Thursday/Friday practice update or final designation could be independently confirmed, but our roster feed shows him cleared to Active for today's game at New Orleans. Keeping Health Watch pending firmer confirmation. Separately: Browns QB Deshaun Watson is reportedly in concussion protocol and trending to sit today, with rookie Shedeur Sanders in line to start (SportsLine, The Fantasy Footballers, On3, 11/4-6) -- worth monitoring Boston's target quality under a new QB. POST-GAME CONFIRMATION (11/8-10): played Sunday's Week 9 game at New Orleans -- carried no final designation on the calf issue flagged earlier in the week. Stat line not independently confirmable via search as of this update; no setback reported. NEW FLIP, UNCONFIRMED CAUSE (11/12): back to QUESTIONABLE today ahead of Sunday's Week 10 home game vs. Miami, continuing the pattern of recurring lower-body issues (foot since Week 6, calf since Week 9) that have dogged him all season without costing him a game. No specific fresh practice report or beat-writer confirmation found via search as of this update -- treating as a likely recurrence of one of the existing issues rather than a new injury. Keeping Health Watch; recheck Friday's report.

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.reason: Rookie hype exceeds his current role — projected ~250 att/1,125 yds, but likely won't clear 70% snap share with Mitchell handling passing downs. High-variance breakout, not a lock.

roster.name: Mike Washington Jr.
roster.reason: NEWLY ROSTERED (10/10): Raiders 4th-round rookie RB (drafted 122nd overall, trading up from Atlanta; $5.36M rookie deal, $1.1M guaranteed), added as a depth/handcuff piece behind Ashton Jeanty. Has not seen a meaningful role through Week 4 with Jeanty healthy and the clear lead back (see Jeanty's note) -- this is purely a handcuff stash given Jeanty's recent ankle/foot practice-report flags, not a standalone volume play.

roster.name: Emmett Johnson
roster.reason: NEW TO NOTES (11/6): rookie 5th-round pick (Nebraska) newly added to a FantasyGoblins roster this week. Profiles as Kansas City's clear No. 2 running back behind Kenneth Walker III, with HC Andy Reid praising his pass-catching ability -- real standalone value only if Walker misses time, but a credible Chiefs backfield handcuff (RotoBaller, PlayerProfiler, AtoZ Sports).

roster.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
roster.reason: Diagnosed with a deltoid ligament sprain in his left ankle (not an Achilles issue — HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed the Achilles is intact) after leaving the Sept 10 opener vs. the Rams early without a target. Underwent ankle surgery Wednesday (Sept 16) after the injury proved worse than initially believed, and was officially placed on injured reserve — revised from the earlier ~1-month outlook to a firmer ~10-week absence per Shanahan's post-surgery update. Drop-and-stash-if-needed territory in shallow leagues for the next couple of months. Still a real deep-league breakout stash for whenever SF's WR room opens back up.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.reason: Dislocated his left (non-throwing) elbow — the same joint's 2nd dislocation within under a year — late in the first half of Washington's 37-20 Week 2 loss to Dallas (Sun 9/20); X-rays showed no fracture. Ruled out for Week 3 vs. Seattle, with Marcus Mariota named starting QB (Dan Quinn, 9/22 presser). NEW (AP, ~9/23): imaging and multiple specialist opinions found NO ligament damage, and Daniels will NOT need surgery; the Commanders are not placing him on IR "for now" (FOX Sports/AP, NBC Sports/PFT, ProFootballRumors) — a real upgrade from Tuesday's total-uncertainty read. Still no firm return timetable — HC Dan Quinn has declined to commit to one, with re-evaluation expected to continue toward Washington's Week 7 bye. Mariota remains the starter in the interim, and the recurring nature of the injury (2nd dislocation of the same elbow in <1 year) keeps real season-long variance in play even without surgery. UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Week 4 (in London vs. Indianapolis). He returned to practice this week and traveled with the team, and per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz told teammates he's foregoing surgery and felt he "owed it to them" to return as fast as possible (RotoWire, Washington Times, Hogs Haven, 9/28). HC Dan Quinn said he isn't sure yet if Daniels plays "in six days" but that he "isn't far off" and will practice "in some form" this week. Read this as soft/early-stage QUESTIONABLE, not a real lean toward playing — nearly every outlet still has Marcus Mariota as the presumptive Week 4 starter pending how practice reps go Wed-Fri. CONFIRMED OUT (10/2-3): ruled out for Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Colts in London -- ESPN's Adam Schefter does not believe Daniels will be active despite making the trip and practicing in some form. Marcus Mariota remains the favorite to start unless Daniels takes the bulk of first-team reps, which hasn't happened (CBS Sports, RotoBaller, Commanders.com, 10/1-3). No surgery still planned this season; recurring elbow dislocation keeps real multi-week variance in play. CONFIRMED (10/5): did not play Week 4 vs. the Colts in London; Marcus Mariota started for a second straight game and Washington won 17-16 (Colts.com). Per Adam Schefter, Daniels will "eventually need surgery" on the elbow (this is the THIRD dislocation of the same non-throwing elbow within under a year) but is deferring it to the offseason and will likely play in a brace whenever he returns -- no practice/return timeline has been given as of 10/5 (NBC Sports). Given the recurring nature of the injury and no near-term surgical or return plan, upgrading tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury; Mariota remains the starter indefinitely. IMPROVING, REVISED (10/7): real progress this week -- HC Dan Quinn said Daniels is set for a full Wed-Thu-Fri practice week with the goal of starting Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants, wearing the elbow brace (ESPN, TSN). Added urgency: backup Marcus Mariota suffered his own MCL sprain vs. the Colts, making 7th-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis the emergency option if Daniels can't go. Some practice-report aggregators still show a "limited" tag, so treat this as a real but not fully resolved Questionable rather than a lock. Revising tag down from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch given the firm full-practice/start-Sunday trajectory -- no longer an open-ended absence. CLEARED (10/8): officially flipped from Questionable to Active ahead of Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants after a full Wednesday practice; per Jay Glazer, Washington plans to start Daniels in the elbow brace, and Tom Pelissero reports the team remains hopeful he returns to the starting role (ESPN, CBS Sports, 10/7-8). Backup situation is in flux -- Marcus Mariota aggravated the same MCL he had surgically repaired in 2022 and is doubtful/out, which only reinforces that Washington needs Daniels back now. CONFIRMED HEALTHY RETURN (10/12): started Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants in the elbow brace and delivered a big dual-threat performance in a 27-27 overtime tie -- 17-of-25 passing for 199 yards with no interceptions (despite 5 sacks), plus 103 rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns on 9 carries. No setback to the surgically-pending elbow reported. Washington lost a late chance to win in OT after a Daniels scramble ran out the clock instead of spiking it. WEEK 10 TNF RESULT (11/12-13): threw two interceptions on back-to-back fourth-quarter possessions in Thursday night's game at the Giants, but engineered a game-winning final drive capped by a 32-yard TD pass to Stefon Diggs with under a minute left, lifting Washington to a 24-21 win and keeping the Commanders' (3-5-1) playoff hopes alive. No injury reported.

roster.name: Bhayshul Tuten
roster.reason: Illness that sent him home from a Sept 2 practice was a non-issue by kickoff — logged a full workload in Jacksonville's Week 1 win over Cleveland with 15 carries for 66 yards plus a catch for 22 yards. UPDATE: posted a season-high 73 yards on 15 touches with 5 broken tackles in Jacksonville's 35-6 rout of New England in Week 3 (9/27) — a clear positive trendline heading into Week 4 (Jaguars.com, SI/OnSI). NEW (11/4): popped up on Jacksonville's Week 9 injury report with ankle and foot issues, sitting out Monday and Tuesday's practices ahead of Thursday night's road game at Baltimore -- officially Questionable/TBD as of Wednesday, with Wednesday his last practice before the short week forces a game-status call. Chris Rodriguez Jr. (himself limited with a hand injury) would be the top complementary back if Tuten sits. Dropping the Depth Chart Battle tag -- he's been Jacksonville's clear lead back for weeks now, this is purely a health question (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, Heavy.com, 11/2-3). WEEK 9 RESULT (11/6): the ankle/foot Questionable/TBD tag from this week's short-week Thursday report resolved with no issue -- played and scored a rushing touchdown in Jacksonville's 33-10 road blowout of Baltimore (TNF, 11/5), which improved the Jaguars to 6-2. Lamar Jackson did not play for Baltimore (rookie Joe Fagnano started). Exact carry/yardage total unconfirmed via box score as of this update. Upgrading tag from Health Watch back to Healthy; remains Jacksonville's clear lead back. NEW -- ANKLE/FOOT, REAL DOUBT (11/11-13): did not practice Wednesday or Thursday with the same ankle/foot issue that popped up earlier this season, putting Sunday's Week 10 road game at Tennessee genuinely in question -- one preview (bet365) explicitly notes that another DNP Friday would likely mean he sits (Yahoo Sports, Black and Teal, bet365, 11/11-12). This is a tougher sign than last week's short-week TBD that resolved fine. Chris Rodriguez Jr. (hand, limited) is the next-man-up if Tuten can't go. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch; will confirm Friday's final designation.

roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.reason: Led the NFL with 323 carries in 2025 — 1,585 yds, 18 rush TD, RB1 overall. New contract extension cements him as the Colts' offensive centerpiece; staff may trim touches slightly to manage wear, but role security is elite. New extension (announced Aug 6, 2026): 2 years, $44M ($39M guaranteed, up to $47M) — the 2nd-highest-paid RB in the NFL by AAV. TRADE WATCH (10/28): Speculation around Taylor has intensified after the Colts fired GM Chris Ballard (week of 10/22), with ESPN and Field Level Media reporting Green Bay, Seattle, Denver and Minnesota among potential suitors ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. No deal has been made, and Indianapolis reportedly wants to see more games before deciding; Taylor himself says he hasn't considered it. Monitor closely through the deadline -- a trade would warrant a New Team tag if it happens. TRADE BUZZ ESCALATING (11/3-5): speculation intensified after Indianapolis traded away G Quenton Nelson and DT DeForest Buckner (week of 10/27), which multiple outlets frame as "opening the door" to also moving Taylor ahead of Tuesday's (11/10) trade deadline -- the Giants and Vikings are now reported as the current frontrunners, with Green Bay and Denver also mentioned. No deal has been made as of this update, and Indianapolis reportedly wants to see more game action before deciding; Taylor himself says he hasn't considered it. Would warrant a New Team tag if a trade is finalized before the deadline.

roster.name: Malik Nabers
roster.reason: CLEARED: the shoulder that "popped out" (and back in) during Week 2's loss at the Rams came back with clean X-rays; Nabers was a full practice participant that Thursday and the ESPN status flipped from Questionable to Active ahead of Week 3 at Tennessee. Told reporters: "Good result. I'm smiling, I'm out there, playing, catching the ball, so good results... I'll be fine" (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Giants.com, 9/24). UPDATE: played Week 3 and led the Giants with 5 catches on 6 targets for 26 yards (27% target share) in a 12-7 win over Tennessee — a quiet, low-yardage line but with no ill effects reported from the shoulder (NBC Sports, CBS Sports/RotoWire, 9/27-28). The bigger Week 4 storyline is the QB change, not the shoulder: starter Jaxson Dart is out with a knee injury and Jameis Winston is set to start at QB going forward, which beat writers flag as a likelier drag on Nabers' target quality/fantasy ceiling than the now-resolved shoulder issue (CBS Sports, 9/29-30). NEW (10/8): flipped to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington after not practicing Wednesday with a knee issue (Giants' official injury report, giants.com, 10/7) -- notable given his 2025 season ended with a torn ACL/meniscus in the same knee, though no beat writer has reported a new tear or setback. Treat as a practice-report flag to watch through Friday, not a confirmed re-injury. CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington -- no setback reported from the knee soreness that had him DNP Wednesday (the knee is the same one that ended his 2025 season with a torn ACL/meniscus, but no new tear or setback has been reported). HC/beat coverage from the Giants was cautiously upbeat all week (bolavip, Newsweek, 10/7-9). BIG GAME (10/28): Caught 7 passes for 111 yards in the Giants' 27-21 OT win over Houston (10/25), maintaining his role as the clear top target through New York's QB shuffle (Winston/McCarthy). No health concerns reported since his early-October knee scare resolved; upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy and reflecting his locked-in role with WR1 Lock. NEW (11/6-7): added to the Giants' injury report with a knee issue -- a non-participant Thursday, full participant Friday, and no final game-status designation heading into Sunday's Week 9 game at Philadelphia. New Giants HC John Harbaugh (hired this past offseason, replacing Brian Daboll, who was fired back in November 2025 -- correcting a stale "Daboll" reference in an earlier Giants-related note) called it "an in-season type thing" and said Nabers will be full-go; Nabers told reporters he'd "be good" for Sunday. No outlet has described this as a re-aggravation of his 2025 ACL/meniscus injury (CBS Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, Rotowire, Big Blue View, 11/5-6). Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch out of caution given the knee history, but current reporting points to a minor, managed issue. CLEARED (11/6-7): missed Thursday's practice with the knee issue but was a full participant Friday and carries no game designation for today's Week 9 home game vs. Philadelphia -- HC John Harbaugh confirmed Nabers will be "full-go" (Heavy.com, SI.com/OnSI, 11/6). Resolves the in-season knee flare with no indication of a new ACL/meniscus setback. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. POST-GAME CONFIRMATION (11/8-10): played Sunday's Week 9 game at Philadelphia as expected after clearing the knee issue -- final stat line not independently confirmable via search as of this update. No setback reported. Remains Healthy.

roster.name: Carnell Tate
roster.reason: Took a hard hit in Monday practice and missed Wednesday's session with dizziness/stiffness — evaluated but not diagnosed with a concussion, has since returned to practice with no Week 1 concern. Rookie WR with rising fantasy stock as the direct beneficiary any time Wan'Dale Robinson is banged up. 2026 1st-round pick (No. 4 overall, Ohio State) — Tennessee's top rookie weapon for Cam Ward alongside slot man Wan'Dale Robinson. NEW (10/8): added to Tennessee's injury report Thursday with a back issue, downgraded to limited after a full practice Wednesday -- a new ailment unrelated to the August practice-collision stiffness. Comes right after his best game of the season (9 catches, 145 yards in the Week 4 loss at Baltimore), so a limited Sunday vs. Houston would be a real hit to Cam Ward's passing game (Yahoo Sports/Titans beat, 10/8). NEW (10/23): QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 7 home game vs. Arizona with a chest injury -- limited at Wednesday's (10/21) practice, per Broncos.com's Aric DiLalla; his status will be watched closely as the weekend approaches (CBS Sports, 10/21-22). Nothing severe reported; downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch. Denver (coming off a Week 6 bye) remains a run-first offense that hasn't consistently fed Waddle target volume even when healthy. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; Volume Regression Watch stands given Denver's run-first offense still hasn't fed him consistent target volume even when fully healthy. CONFIRMED (11/3): played through the chest injury in Sunday's Week 8 win at Kansas City -- caught a 1-yard TD pass from Bo Nix (plus the 2-pt conversion) and finished with 3 catches for 39 yards as Denver rallied from a 24-13 fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Chiefs 28-24, improving to 6-2 and taking first place in the AFC West (ESPN, Arrowhead Pride, Mile High Report, 11/1-2). No setback reported. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; Volume Regression Watch stands given the modest target share even in a scoring game. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending more detail. Brown (knee) ruled inactive, helping power New England's 24-19 comeback win at Miami -- his specific carry/catch total could not be independently confirmed via search as of this update. roster.reason: Consensus QB2 for 2026, but coming off a down 2025 (16.5 PPG, career-low 349 rush yds) due to hamstring/back injuries — real risk, though his efficiency on throws past the sticks remains elite. On track to start Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Tennessee as normal (Yahoo Sports, 10/1-2). UPDATE (10/5): HC John Harbaugh said Monday that an MRI on the back injury showed only a "significant contusion" with nothing structural -- "I don't want to minimize the severity and pain level of that because it's legit" -- supporting a day-to-day designation rather than a serious new issue (NFL.com, ESPN, Ravens.com). Context: Baltimore lost Week 4 28-12 to Tennessee and Jackson had a rough game by his standards (2 INTs, a fumble, sacked 4 times), which plausibly explains the soreness behind today's QUESTIONABLE tag. Keeping Health Watch given the clean imaging. CORRECTION (10/6): yesterday's note describing a back contusion and a 28-12 Week 4 loss to Tennessee was inaccurate -- the real story: Baltimore beat Tennessee 24-18 on 10/4 (Titans fell to 0-4), and Jackson's ankle rolled awkwardly under a Tennessee defender late in the 2nd quarter; he left the game and did not return (the Ravens scored nothing after that point -- all 24 points came in the first half). His current Week 5 QUESTIONABLE tag is for this ankle injury, not a back issue. No official practice report has posted yet as of today (Monday); the first real signal will be Wednesday's Week 5 injury report. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Injury given the confirmed in-game injury and no "expected to play" signal so far. UPDATE (10/8): per multiple reports (10/4-5), Jackson was seen leaving in a walking boot after the ankle injury and underwent an MRI Monday; HC Jesse Minter said results weren't in yet and the team wouldn't update his status until Wednesday. Sources disagree on severity -- Ian Rapoport frames it as day-to-day, while PFT's Mike Florio called it 'week-to-week' -- but Minter said the injury 'isn't expected to be long-term.' Tyler Huntley would start if Jackson sits Sunday vs. Atlanta; no official Wednesday practice report had posted as of this search, so recheck Thursday/Friday. CONFIRMED (10/10): officially ruled OUT for Sunday night's Week 5 game vs. Atlanta with the ankle sprain suffered vs. Tennessee in Week 4 -- did not practice all week, and Tyler Huntley will make the start in his place (NBC Sports, Newsweek, TSN reporting through 10/7-9). HC John Harbaugh has called the injury not long-term and not expected to require surgery, but no firm return date has been attached yet. Downgrade expectations for Mark Andrews and Zay Flowers in the passing game with Huntley at QB. CORRECTION (10/13): earlier notes misattributed Ravens head-coach comments to a "Jesse Minter" -- Baltimore's actual head coach is John Harbaugh (Jesse Minter is a defensive assistant, not the HC); correcting the record here. Jackson did sit out Week 5 at Atlanta as expected with Huntley starting. TRENDING TO RETURN (10/28): Ankle sprain (since 10/4 vs. Tennessee) kept Jackson out a third straight game in Week 7 vs. Cincinnati (10/25); Baltimore is not on a bye and visits Buffalo in Week 8 (Sun 11/1), which multiple outlets now frame as his real return target after an encouraging practice ramp-up the week of 10/19-23. CLEARED, ENDS 3-GAME ABSENCE (10/30): HC Jesse Minter confirmed Friday that Jackson is off the injury report and will start today's Week 8 game vs. Buffalo, back from the ankle sprain suffered 10/4 vs. Tennessee that cost him Weeks 5-7. Jackson said the pain is "bearable" (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report, SI, 10/30). Tyler Huntley reverts to backup. SEASON-THREATENING SETBACK (11/3): suffered a right thumb injury on Baltimore's very first offensive snap of Sunday's Week 8 game at Buffalo and did not return; HC Jesse Minter confirmed after the 36-10 loss that Jackson will need surgery and will go on injured reserve, and said "we'll see" when asked if it's season-ending (Forbes, Bleacher Report, CBS Sports, 11/1-2). IR MOVE AND BACKUP SITUATION (11/5-7): no follow-up report confirms the thumb surgery has actually been completed or that IR paperwork was formally filed, but HC Jesse Minter's original Nov. 1-2 comments ("That'll be a surgery deal. He'll go to IR") remain the operative plan, with CBS Sports noting the IR stint is a minimum of 4 games -- making Week 14 at home vs. Tampa Bay (Dec. 13) the earliest possible return. roster.name: Josh Jacobs
roster.reason: Pleaded no contest Sept 10 to misdemeanor battery and criminal-damage charges from the May incident — fined $1,000 plus costs, with the damage charge to be dismissed after a 12-month deferred agreement. The legal resolution does NOT end his NFL absence: he remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List (can't practice, play, or be on the 53-man roster, though he's paid and can attend meetings/individual workouts) while a separate personal-conduct-policy review continues. Sources still peg the likely suspension range at 4-6 games once announced, with games missed on the exempt list expected to count toward it. Pleaded no contest Sept 10 in Brown County to the misdemeanor battery charge (found guilty, $1,000 fine + costs) with a 12-month deferred-judgment agreement on the property-damage charge. As of 9/26, the NFL STILL has not announced an official suspension length — reporting indicates the league is navigating legal barriers (a court-ordered bar on releasing video evidence) before finalizing discipline, with the standard 6-game domestic-violence-related baseline still the working estimate (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, ProFootballRumors, 9/24-26). Green Bay has already hedged, trading a 2028 6th-round pick to Pittsburgh for RB Kaleb Johnson as depth-chart insurance — a real sign the team isn't banking on a quick Jacobs return. Treat him as unplayable/bench for now. UPDATE (10/6): still no change -- the NFL has NOT announced an official suspension length. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List (confirmed still inactive for Green Bay's Week 4 game vs. Tampa Bay on 10/4). Speculation on the eventual suspension length now ranges from 4-6 games (ESPN's Jeremy Fowler) up to as many as 8 games (NFL Network's Ian Rapoport), still unconfirmed either way. The video-evidence dispute delaying the league's review is still unresolved -- a judge recently declined to permanently seal the incident video on procedural grounds (NBC Sports/PFT, ~10/1-2) -- and Jacobs' next court hearing isn't until Nov. 17, well past several more game weeks. Any time already spent on the Exempt List would count toward an eventual suspension. Green Bay's Kaleb Johnson depth-chart plan is unchanged; still unplayable/bench. UPDATE (10/13): still no official suspension length announced. HC Matt LaFleur said ahead of Green Bay's Week 6 game at Dallas that he has no word from the league on timing. Reporting still pegs a likely 4-6 game range (6-game baseline for a first battery offense, reducible for mitigating factors), with exempt-list time possibly counting toward it (ProFootballRumors, Yahoo Sports, 10/9-10). Still unplayable/bench. This remains a Personal Conduct Policy matter (a no-contest plea to misdemeanor battery/criminal damage to property stemming from a May domestic incident), not a PED case. A court fight over releasing police video/records from that incident is reportedly ongoing and may be delaying the league's final ruling (Rolling Out, 10/14). He'll miss a 6th straight game Sunday vs. Dallas. Green Bay's backfield without him: MarShawn Lloyd leads with 40 carries/112 yards/2 TD this season, with Kaleb Johnson (27/106) and Chris Brooks also involved -- Green Bay's run game ranks last in the NFL in his absence. UPDATE (10/16): filed a civil suit Wednesday (10/15) seeking to restrict public access to records tied to the May incident, as the Commissioner's Exempt List review continues -- no suspension length has been announced yet, and this remains a Personal Conduct Policy matter, not a physical injury (our roster feed's "DAY_TO_DAY" status field reflects the exempt-list/legal situation, not an actual injury). Still unplayable/bench; MarShawn Lloyd remains Green Bay's lead back for Sunday Night Football vs. Dallas (10/18). The Personal Conduct Policy investigation into his misdemeanor battery/property-damage case continues separately, and the league has not ruled out an eventual suspension, but for now he is expected to be available to the Packers (AP, Newsweek, NY1, 10/16-19). MarShawn Lloyd has been Green Bay's lead back in his absence and figures to continue sharing work even once Jacobs is back; still a wait-and-see Depth Chart Battle until he actually suits up. SEASON DEBUT IMMINENT (10/25): the Commissioner's Exempt List review ended Monday (10/19), clearing him to practice and play starting with today's Week 7 game at Detroit (4:25pm ET) -- HC Matt LaFleur said this week Jacobs got a full week of practice and 'we feel he's in a pretty good spot,' though the team stopped short of guaranteeing the season debut outright. NFL Network's Tom Pelissero separately reported Jacobs will immediately return as Green Bay's starting RB. The Personal Conduct Policy review into the underlying misdemeanor battery case continues separately and an eventual suspension hasn't been ruled out, but for today he's expected to play for the first time all season after missing the first six games. MarShawn Lloyd, who has led Green Bay's backfield all year, remains in the mix regardless. Dropping the Health-Watch mislabel now that this is squarely a workload/role story rather than a physical injury; adding Bounce-Back Watch for the long-awaited debut and keeping Depth Chart Battle. A meaningful role but not a workhorse share of the carries in his first game back after missing the first six games on the Commissioner's Exempt List; keep an eye on next week's split with MarShawn Lloyd to see how the touches settle. Keeping Depth Chart Battle and Bounce-Back Watch. WEEK 8 FINAL (10/30): Green Bay beat Carolina 27-19 in Thursday Night Football at Lambeau (10/29) to improve to 5-3; Jacobs scored twice on the ground (CBS Sports), but his exact carry/yardage total could not be independently confirmed via a full box score as of this update. Jordan Love threw 3 TD passes in the win (see his note). NEW QUESTIONABLE TAG (11/10): picked up a fresh QUESTIONABLE designation for Week 10 after Sunday's Week 9 road game at New England (11/8) -- specific injury/practice report not independently confirmed via search as of this update. Adding Health Watch as a flag to track. NEW QUESTIONABLE TAG (11/9-10): picked up a QUESTIONABLE designation this week with no fresh injury report confirmed via search as of this update -- most likely the standard weekly placeholder reset rather than new medical news, consistent with a pattern seen repeatedly with other players on this roster. No tag change pending confirmation. CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reports a max ceiling of about 3 weeks, but HC Matt LaFleur called Week 10 (vs. Minnesota) availability 'uncertain' and did not rule out an IR stint (CBS Sports, The Fantasy Footballers, 4for4, TSN, 11/9-11). Return-timeline reporting is unchanged: Rapoport projects 2-3 weeks, Zenitz says no more than 3, with a possible Week 11 (vs. the Rams) return. Treating the QUESTIONABLE flip as a likely data lag rather than real medical news; keeping the standard Injury tier. CONFIRMED OUT, HAD SURGERY (11/12-14): the QUESTIONABLE-to-OUT flip (and yesterday's flagged 'data lag' suspicion) is resolved -- Jacobs underwent surgery on the fractured right ring finger suffered in the Week 9 win over New England, and HC Matt LaFleur said he's out indefinitely with an IR move possible, per NFL Network's Tom Pelissero. CBS Sports' timeline is 2-3 weeks, which would have him miss Week 10 (at Minnesota) and target a Week 12 return (Green Bay has a Week 11 bye, which may limit the real games missed). Kaleb Johnson is in line to lead Green Bay's backfield in his absence (see Johnson's note). Keeping the standard Injury tier pending an official IR decision.

roster.name: Bryce Young
roster.reason: Legitimate early-season breakout: 6 total TDs (passing) against just 1 INT through two 2026 games, averaging 8.9 yards per attempt, with a 34-3 Week 2 rout of Atlanta headlined by a 23-of-36, 287-yard, 3-TD, 0-INT line (116.3 rating). Worth monitoring for regression given a small sample and the difficulty of NFL defenses adjusting, but two clean, efficient starts is a real signal after a rocky first three pro seasons (ESPN, Yahoo Sports).

No new return timeline reported; Week 6 vs. Atlanta remains the target, keeping the standard Injury tier. UPDATE (10/13): real progress -- returned to a limited practice Friday (10/9) after resuming throwing drills, and The Athletic's Dan Wiederer reports Chicago never placed him on IR, keeping Week 6 vs. Atlanta (10/18) live as his target. He's still building back to full-speed running, and HC Ben Johnson is calling his return "to be determined"/benchmark-based rather than confirming he plays -- Rapoport/Pelissero flagged Week 6 or the following week (10/22 vs. NE) as the likely activation window, with no hard date set (NBC Sports, Bleacher Nation, 10/9-10).
