HC Ben Johnson has NOT guaranteed it, saying only that Williams would be "close." The Chicago Sun-Times (10/11) floated the team instead targeting the following week (Oct 22 vs. New England) given the short Thu turnaround after a Sunday game, calling the decision "to be determined." Keeping the standard Injury tier until an actual designation/practice grade confirms he's playing. UPGRADE (10/14): took a full practice Wednesday, per HC Ben Johnson (Yahoo Sports/SI, BleacherNation) -- a real step up from last week's limited/estimated sessions. Johnson still won't commit to naming him the starter until closer to Sunday's game at Atlanta, but a full practice week is a strong signal he plays. Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Health Watch given the clean practice participation. UPDATE (10/16): a full practice participant Wednesday (10/14) after missing three straight games with a Grade 2 hamstring strain -- NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports "all signs point" to Williams returning Sunday vs. Atlanta (10/18), and the Bears have moved to roughly 3-point favorites, suggesting the market expects him back. HC Ben Johnson hasn't confirmed the start, calling it "still fluid." RETURNED AND DOMINANT (10/18): made his return from the 3-game hamstring absence in Sunday's 31-23 win at Atlanta with zero lingering effects -- went 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a TD to Colston Loveland, including a 12-of-12 start before his first incompletion. Chicago held off a 24-point Atlanta rally attempt to improve to 4-2; D'Andre Swift ran for 2 TDs (see his note). Williams said afterward his body felt great but that managing it will be "a weekly thing" (ESPN, CBS Chicago, Yahoo Sports, 10/18). Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Healthy given the clean, full-workload return; Chicago is back in action Thursday vs. New England on a short week, worth checking his practice reps given the quick turnaround. WEEK 7 ACTUAL (10/22): backed up his return with another strong outing in the 30-24 TNF win over New England -- 22-of-33 for 308 yards and 2 TD (incl. a 12-yard TD to Colston Loveland), zero interceptions, no hamstring setback through back-to-back full workloads. Also hit Rome Odunze on a key 3rd-and-9 conversion late that set up Odunze's own game-sealing onside-kick recovery (Boston Globe, Bleacher Nation, NFL.com, 10/22-23).

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.reason: Chicago's clear RB1 in Ben Johnson's scheme. The Sept 3 practice scare was cramping, not a leg injury, and it showed no lingering effect — torched Carolina for 18 carries, 124 yards and 3 TDs (plus a catch) in Sunday's 59-37 win, arguably his best game as a Bear. The Week 2 knee/ankle concern is resolved — logged a full practice Friday (9/18) and was removed from Chicago's injury report entirely, carrying no designation into Sunday's game at Minnesota (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, 9/18). NEW (10/1-2): popped up on Chicago's Week 4 injury report as a non-participant Thursday with a knee injury — a new issue, not a recurrence of the earlier cramping/knee-ankle scares. He was off the Wednesday walkthrough report and had just carried 20 times for 84 yards in Chicago's prior game, so beat writers flagged the sudden Thursday DNP as worth watching; no designation confirmed yet pending Friday's report, with hope he's a full go Sunday vs. the Jets (Chicago Sun-Times, Bleacher Nation, 10/1-2). CLEARED (10/3): the Thursday DNP knee scare did not linger -- Swift practiced fully later in the week and carries no designation into Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Jets, remaining Chicago's unquestioned RB1. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. NEW (10/4): fumbled in the 3rd quarter of Chicago's 23-12 Week 4 win over the Jets and did not return, finishing with 15 carries for 58 yards and 2 catches for 16 yards; was seen limping postgame with soreness in the same knee that had been a minor pregame concern. HC Ben Johnson did not frame it as a benching. Kyle Monangai (see his note) took over and torched the Jets for 146 yards/2 TD on 30 carries in relief. No official injury designation or severity reported yet as of 10/5-6 -- downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending clarity; Chicago's Week 5 backfield split is worth watching since both backs picked up bumps in the same game (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Bleacher Nation, Heavy.com, 10/4). CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Green Bay -- the hip/knee issue that kept him out of Wednesday's practice resolved by Friday. Remains Chicago's lead back; downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. WEEK 6 + WEEK 7 ACTUAL (10/18, 10/22): stayed Chicago's clear lead back through both games. Week 6 at Atlanta (31-23 win, 10/18): 16 carries for 44 yards (2.8 YPC) and 4-of-5 targets for 26 yards -- backup Roschon Johnson actually out-gained him on the ground that day (13 car/51 yds/TD). Week 7 TNF vs. New England (30-24 win, 10/22): bounced back as a true workhorse, 86% of offensive snaps -- 22 carries for 78 yards and Chicago's first TD of the game (4-yard run), per Rotowire's usage breakdown and CBS Sports. Monangai still out; no threat to Swift's role.

roster.name: Stefon Diggs
roster.reason: Turns 33 in November, but 2025 metrics (9.9 YPT, top-7 YPRR) show no real decline — his route-running game tends to age gracefully. Signed 1yr/$12M as Washington's presumed WR2 behind Terry McLaurin, throwing to Jayden Daniels. NEW (10/8): did not practice Wednesday with a hamstring injury and is QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants (Commanders' official injury report, 10/7) -- first hamstring concern of the season. With Terry McLaurin (hamstring) also out of Wednesday's practice, a Diggs absence would be a real hit to Washington's receiving corps; watch Thursday/Friday participation. WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/10): flipped from QUESTIONABLE to OUT for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. the Giants with the hamstring injury -- was a non-participant in back-to-back Wednesday/Thursday practices. Teammate Terry McLaurin is also dealing with a separate hamstring/core-muscle issue and remains Questionable (see his note); with both of Washington's top two receivers banged up, rookie Antonio Williams is in line for a bigger role Sunday. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Injury given the confirmed missed game; no return timeline reported yet. UPDATE (10/14): no Week 6 practice report has surfaced yet for the hamstring that kept him out of Week 5 vs. the Giants -- Washington's next game is at San Francisco on Monday Night Football (10/19). Today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip could not be corroborated with any fresh beat-writer reporting either way, so treat it cautiously rather than as confirmed progress; recheck Thursday/Friday. Teammate Terry McLaurin did return and play through his own hamstring/core issue in the Week 5 OT tie vs. the Giants with no setback reported, and is ahead of Diggs in recovery. UPDATE (10/15): still no fresh Wed/Thu practice report found for the hamstring that kept him out of Week 5 -- Washington's Week 6 game is at San Francisco on Monday Night Football (10/19), so the team has extra practice days before any decision; nothing new to report yet. Recheck Thursday/Friday coverage closer to the Monday game. UPDATE (10/16): still no practice Thursday (10/14-10/15) for the hamstring that cost him Week 5, per the Commanders' own beat reporter -- no game designation assigned yet despite the extra prep time before Monday night's game at San Francisco (10/19). Teammate Terry McLaurin is further along in his own hamstring recovery. CLEARED AND PLAYED (10/19-21): was upgraded to Questionable and played through the hamstring injury that cost him Week 5 in Monday night's 23-17 loss at San Francisco (10/19), posting 16.4 fantasy points per our tracker with no re-aggravation or setback reported. Washington is now on its Week 7 bye, and today's flip to ACTIVE simply reflects there being no game this week. Downgrading tag from Injury to Healthy given the clean return. NEW (10/30): QUESTIONABLE again ahead of Sunday Night Football's Week 8 home game vs. Philadelphia (11/1) -- carrying the same-side hamstring concern that cost him Week 5, with one report adding a hand issue this week as well (not independently verified as of this update). HC Dan Quinn has said he's hopeful Diggs gets more practice reps later in the week; no Thursday/Friday update found yet. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Injury given the genuine uncertainty -- recommend confirming before kickoff. CLEARED (10/31): the hand/hamstring/rest designation that held him out of Wednesday's practice resolved with back-to-back full practices Thursday and Friday -- off Washington's final Week 8 injury report and active for Sunday Night Football vs. Philadelphia (11/1) (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, 10/30). Upgrading tag from Injury to Healthy. Context: teammate Terry McLaurin is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon (see his note); HC Dan Quinn said he doesn't expect Diggs to see a materially larger target share as a result, but he remains Washington's clear top healthy receiver regardless. GAME-WINNING CATCH (11/12-13): caught a 32-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels with under a minute left to give Washington a 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday Night Football (Week 10) -- the Commanders (3-5-1) kept their playoff hopes alive. No injury concern; a clean, clutch performance.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.reason: Rough 2025: a 3-game suspension to start the year, only 17.4% target share (Jefferson had 28.2%), finished WR43. QB upgrade to Kyler Murray helps, but MIN also signed WR Jauan Jennings — adds competition rather than clearing it. Profiles more WR3/bench right now. NEW (10/8): sidelined at Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury and carries a QUESTIONABLE tag (per the Vikings' own injury report) into Sunday's Week 5 game at New Orleans -- though one outlet flagged a conflicting Minnesota listing, so confirm Friday's final designation. First hamstring concern of the season, and it comes while he's already fighting for target share behind Justin Jefferson (himself limited this week with an ankle issue). CONFIRMED (10/12): inactive for Sunday's Week 5 game at New Orleans with the hamstring injury after a true game-time call (only two limited practices during the week). Minnesota (5-0) now has its Week 6 bye, so Addison's next chance to play isn't until Oct. 25 vs. the Colts -- effectively a two-week break to heal rather than a sign of a longer-term issue. Justin Jefferson (see his note) returned and played a full workload in the same game. NON-EVENT (10/14): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip is a procedural reset, not real news -- Minnesota is on its Week 6 bye (confirmed via Vikings.com/FoxSports league bye list), so there's no game for Addison to be questionable for. He remains on track to return Week 7 (Oct 25) vs. the Colts per last week's report; no new hamstring details surfaced. CLEARED (10/23): Addison's hamstring is resolved -- he was a full practice participant Wednesday 10/21 (first Week 7 practice off the Week 6 bye) and multiple outlets (RotoBaller, TheFantasyFootballers, 10/21) expect him back in Minnesota's starting lineup for Sunday's Week 7 home game vs. Indianapolis. His role could still be squeezed if Justin Jefferson (ankle, limited Wednesday -- see his note) ends up out. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

roster.name: Mike Evans
roster.reason: Monday (9/21) update: Shanahan said the hip "will have to be managed this week" and Evans would likely miss some practice time. Turns 33 in August — an aging watch item independent of any single-week injury. UPDATE: exited Week 3's loss to Arizona early in the 2nd quarter with a rib injury after a hard hit from S Budda Baker on a middle-of-the-field catch — was carted off and did not return, finishing with 3 catches for 34 yards and a TD before leaving (ESPN, CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/27-28). Downgrading tag from Aging-Watch-only injury risk to Health Watch: Evans returned to practice Friday and is officially Questionable for Week 4 vs. Denver, with HC Kyle Shanahan indicating optimism that he'll play (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Last Word on Sports, 9/26-29). Treat as a game-time-decision-caliber Questionable, not a real absence risk at this point. CLEARED (10/5): the rib strain suffered vs. Arizona in Week 3 is behind him -- today's status flip from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE confirms he's cleared the issue that had him day-to-day. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to reflect no current injury; turns 33 in August remains a standalone long-term watch item (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Last Word on Sports). UPDATE (10/8): the Week 3 rib injury remains a recurring game-status item -- Evans played through it in Week 4 (76 yards, NBC Sports, 10/4) and is again QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Denver; Forbes' fantasy injury roundup (10/7) described it as 'not overly serious' at this point, consistent with his pattern of limited practice reps but suiting up. CORRECTION + CLEARED (10/10): last week's note misstated San Francisco's Week 5 opponent as Denver -- the 49ers actually play Seattle in Week 5. Evans was upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's game vs. the Seahawks; he was limited in Wednesday's practice with the recurring rib issue (NBC Sports Fantasy, 10/7) but cleared by Friday, continuing the pattern of playing through this injury each of the last two weeks. DELIVERED (10/13): no setback from the rib -- caught 7 passes for 113 yards and a TD, plus a 2-point conversion, in San Francisco's 32-29 win over Seattle on Sunday 10/11, pushing the 49ers to 5-0 (ESPN box score, gameId 401872992). Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean workload and no re-aggravation; remains SF's clear top receiving weapon alongside Deebo Samuel (who left the same game with a hamstring injury -- see his note). NEW (10/15-16): HC Kyle Shanahan said Evans will not practice Thursday due to Achilles soreness, on top of the recurring rib issue he's played through in recent weeks; his status for Monday night's Week 6 home game vs. Washington (10/19) is in question. With Deebo Samuel Sr. also out (hamstring, see his note), Jacob Cowing, Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins would see larger roles if Evans sits too. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch given the fresh soreness and missed practice; no multi-week framing reported, treat as day-to-day pending Friday's practice report. EXITED (10/19): left Monday night's 23-17 win over Washington before halftime with right Achilles soreness after leading all receivers with 3 catches for 94 yards; did not return. HC Kyle Shanahan described it as Achilles tendonitis and said he didn't believe further imaging was needed, and beat reporter Jennifer Lee Chan reports the tendon is intact -- he's expected to miss "a little time," with speculation his return could line up around San Francisco's Week 8 bye (ESPN, NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, 10/19-20). Revising tag from Health Watch to Short-Term Injury given the relatively optimistic, tendon-intact framing, but his Sunday vs. Atlanta status is unconfirmed as of this update -- some analysts expect SF to rest him given the upcoming bye. Deebo Samuel Sr. remains out separately (hamstring, see his note), so a Niners WR room already thin would thin further if Evans also sits. CONFIRMED OUT (10/25): ruled out for today's Week 7 game at Atlanta with the recurring Achilles tendinitis that flared up in last week's win over Washington -- HC Kyle Shanahan has said he doesn't believe it's a long-term issue and doesn't think further imaging is needed, and San Francisco's Week 8 bye sets up a plausible Week 9 return. Keeping the Short-Term Injury tier given that framing, though some reports suggest the Niners may simply be resting him into the bye rather than treating this as a hard multi-week absence. NO CHANGE (10/28): Evans was ruled OUT again for Week 7 at Atlanta (10/25) with the Achilles tendinitis dating to the Week 6 MNF aggravation; no new Shanahan comment or practice update found. SF's Week 8 bye (no game this week) remains the expected target for a Week 9 return vs. the Raiders (11/8) -- today's QUESTIONABLE flip is almost certainly the standard bye-week placeholder reset rather than new medical news. REVISED FROM SHORT-TERM TO STANDARD INJURY (11/5-8): the Achilles tendinitis that cost him the second half of Week 6, all of Week 7, and the Week 8 bye is now also costing him today's Week 9 home game vs. the Raiders -- 49ers GM John Lynch told KNBR (11/5-6) the team is being "extra cautious" and called it an "easy decision" to sit him again; Evans did not practice Thursday. No new severity report, but the original short-term (1-2 week) framing from mid-October has clearly been exceeded with no firm return date given. Revising tag from Short-Term Injury to the standard Injury tier to reflect the longer, still-open-ended timeline. RULED OUT AGAIN, CONFIRMED (11/8-10): missed Sunday's Week 9 home game vs. Las Vegas as expected, with both the rib injury and the recurring Achilles tendinitis in play per Niners Wire's final report (11/6) -- that's two games missed in the three SF has played since Week 6 (Week 7 and now Week 9, with the Week 8 bye between), with no firm 'back by X' timeline found in search as of this update. Keeping the standard Injury tier. QUESTIONABLE AT BEST FOR WEEK 10 (11/11): Mike Garafolo reports Evans is 'questionable at best' to play Sunday vs. Dallas, with no confirmed Shanahan 'won't be ready' quote but also no clearance -- genuinely uncertain, leaning toward sitting again (per Garafolo, 11/11). No new severity report beyond the existing Achilles tendinitis/rib combination. Keeping the standard Injury tier.

roster.name: Makai Lemon
roster.reason: NEW TO NOTES (10/31): rookie Eagles WR newly added to a FantasyGoblins roster. With both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) out of Philadelphia's Week 8 38-21 loss to Dallas, Lemon drew a flagged priority-waiver bump as the next man up for targets (RotoBaller, 10/26), though his season-long target share behind Smith/A.J. Brown has otherwise been thin (3 catches on 6 targets in the Week 4 loss to the Rams). Treat as a depth-chart-battle add pending Smith/Wicks' Week 9 availability. UPDATE (11/1): DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) are both OUT again for tonight's Week 8 SNF at Washington -- the same beneficiary situation flagged after Week 7 continues into this week, keeping Lemon in a bigger offensive role for Philadelphia behind Tanner McKee. Still unproven on a snap-share basis; treat as a depth-chart-battle add pending Smith/Wicks' eventual return. ROLE SOLIDIFIES (11/6-8): with DeVonta Smith now officially on injured reserve (see Smith's note) and Dontayvion Wicks also unavailable, Lemon is framed by multiple previews (bet365, RotoBaller) as Philadelphia's presumptive top perimeter target alongside TE Dallas Goedert for today's Week 9 home game vs. the Giants. Still unproven on a snap-share basis, but the opportunity is real now that Smith's IR move removes any near-term competition for targets.

roster.name: Romeo Doubs
roster.reason: Signed in free agency; profiles as a high-volume slot piece similar to Diggs' old role now that Diggs is gone. PLACED ON IR (10/19-20): dove for a 42-yard go-ahead TD catch from Drake Maye in the 1st quarter of Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets and landed hard on his shoulder, first questionable to return before being ruled out; the Patriots officially placed him on injured reserve Monday (10/19), which rules him out a minimum of four games under NFL IR rules (ESPN, NBC Sports, Boston.com, Heavy.com, 10/19). No surgery has been announced and a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler the injury isn't expected to keep him out long-term -- he's hopeful to return around New England's bye in late November, with one outlet pegging Week 12 vs. the Chargers as an earliest-return target. Upgrading tag from Breakout Watch to Long-Term Injury per the official IR designation (our fixed tiering rule treats any IR stint as Long-Term regardless of the softer verbal outlook); Mack Hollins and DeMario Douglas are set to see expanded roles in New England's receiver room in the meantime.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.reason: Ranked QB11 for 2026 — with Etienne now gone to New Orleans, more of the offense funnels through Lawrence's arm and legs; expected to throw 30+ TDs for the first time. UPDATE: threw 3 TD passes (including to Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers) in Jacksonville's 35-6 rout of New England in Week 3 (9/27) — a strong bounce-back performance for the passing game (Jaguars.com, SI/OnSI).

roster.name: Ashton Jeanty
roster.reason: The Aug 23 ankle sprain was a non-issue for the Sept 13 opener — Jeanty was off the injury report entirely and delivered a workhorse Week 1 in Las Vegas' game vs. Miami: 23 carries for 102 yards plus 6 catches for 45 yards and 2 receiving TDs (27 touches, 2 total TDs). Confirmed as the clear lead back over rookie Mike Washington Jr., who saw no meaningful role in Week 1. Reaffirmed the workhorse role with 25 total touches (21 carries/48 yards, 4-of-7 targets/15 yards) in the Raiders' 26-14 upset of the Chargers in Week 2, but had a late-game injury scare (returned to finish the game) and dropped 3 passes — worth a brief watch, not yet a designation change (CBS Sports, NBC Sports). NEW (10/8): downgraded to a limited practice participant Thursday with a foot issue layered on top of the ankle he's been managing since exiting Week 4's loss to Kansas City (hobbled off in the 3rd quarter, returned in the 4th). Raiders haven't signaled real concern about Sunday's game vs. New England and one outlet still expects him active, but worth tracking given the back-to-back-day downgrade (CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, Newsweek, 10/8). CLEARED (10/12): played through the ankle/foot combo with no reported setback in Sunday's Week 5 loss at New England (Patriots won 45-17); specific carry/yardage totals for the game could not be confirmed via search at the time of this update. Remains the clear lead back in Las Vegas' (now 3-2) backfield.

roster.name: Blake Corum
roster.reason: RB2 behind Kyren Williams in a ~65:35 split that has been fluid through camp. Carried a near-even Monday-night workload alongside Kyren Williams (combined 164 rush yards) in the win over the Giants — the split continues to run closer to 50/50 than a clean Williams-lead role (CBS Sports/RotoWire).

roster.name: Matthew Golden
roster.reason: The early skepticism has faded fast — Golden has been a real Week 2-3 riser: 9.8 fantasy pts in Week 2, then 5 catches for 100 yards and a TD (15-yard grab, plus a 45-yard catch that set up Green Bay's first score) in Thursday night's Week 3 loss at Atlanta, playing like a true No. 1 WR and called the Packers' "lone bright spot" by multiple outlets (RotoWire/CBS/Yahoo, 9/24). 253 receiving yards and 15 catches through 3 games — trending toward a real featured role opposite Watson rather than the depth-chart battle framing from earlier in camp. NEW (10/23): First injury concern of his breakout season -- Golden was listed with a shoulder issue and was a limited practice participant Wednesday 10/21 ahead of Sunday's Week 7 game at Detroit (Packers' injury report via TheFantasyFootballers, 10/21). No severity details or beat-writer swing-game concern surfaced yet; adding Health Watch tag alongside Breakout Watch pending Friday's designation. CLEARED (10/25): carries no injury designation into today's Week 7 game at Detroit (4:25pm ET) -- the shoulder issue that popped up last week (limited practice Wed 10/21) resolved with no setback reported. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy. NO CHANGE (10/28): Today's QUESTIONABLE flip has no injury report behind it -- the mid-October shoulder issue is fully resolved (LaFleur said "no concern" ~10/22) and Golden played Week 7 at Detroit with no designation. Green Bay's Week 8 game is Thursday night (10/29) vs. Carolina, a short week that commonly produces leaguewide placeholder tags; treat this as procedural. Remaining Healthy. WEEK 8 FINAL (10/31): played through the shoulder/foot QUESTIONABLE tag in Thursday night's 27-19 win over Carolina (10/29) with no setback reported -- his exact catch/yard line from the game could not be independently confirmed via box score as of this update, but there's no indication he left the game or missed any snaps. Carries no injury designation (status reset to ACTIVE) heading toward Week 9 at New England (11/8). Remaining Healthy; the real story out of Thursday's game is teammate Christian Watson's broken rib (see his note).

roster.name: Tetairoa McMillan
roster.reason: 2025 AP Offensive Rookie of the Year (70/1,014/7); profiles as a safe WR2 (~WR18-20) capped by Carolina's low-volume passing offense, with Jalen Coker now adding real target competition.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.reason: 2025: 126 rec/1,239 yds/11 TD, led all TEs in target share (25.4%). New Cardinals staff invested heavily in the run game (drafted RB Jeremiyah Love 3rd overall, signed Tyler Allgeier) — his 683-route workload likely won't repeat. Still a top-2 TE, just not a top-15-overall ceiling. NEW (9/30): suffered a concussion on a head-on hit from Lions S Brian Branch in Week 3 (3 catches, 25 yards before exiting) and is ruled OUT for Week 4 vs. Washington (Bleacher Report, ClutchPoints, AZCardinals.com, 9/28). Worth tracking as a protocol case — no set return timeline until he clears the steps, but concussions can also clear quickly. He'd been out-targeting Marvin Harrison Jr. 23-4 through two games, so his absence is a meaningful hit to Arizona's passing-game volume for at least this week. UPDATE (10/5): remains in the concussion protocol after the head-on hit from Lions S Brian Branch in Week 3; did not practice that week and was ruled out for Arizona's following game, with Elijah Higgins, Tip Reiman and Travis Vokolek filling in at TE (azcardinals.com, CBS Sports, NBC Sports). Note: several injury-report sources mislabeled that game as "vs. Washington"; Arizona's actual Week 4 opponent was the New York Giants -- an indexing error in those sources, not a real schedule conflict. Team-sourced reporting says he "should have a good chance to clear protocol in time for Week 5" -- a short, routine absence. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Short-Term Injury given that fairly firm timeline.

roster.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
roster.reason: Two straight down seasons (sub-12 PPG each) with the worst YPRR marks of his career and a shrinking red-zone role. Back in SF on a 1-year “reunion” deal — real chance 2026 is his last fantasy-relevant year. NEW (10/13): strained his hamstring late in the 3rd quarter of Sunday's 32-29 Week 5 win over Seattle, fumbling on the play before being ruled out for the rest of the game (CBS Sports, FantasyPros, 10/11-12). HC Kyle Shanahan said Monday he's expected to miss "at least a couple of weeks" and is not currently being considered for IR (NBC Sports, SF Chronicle, Yardbarker, 10/12). He has a history of this hamstring flaring up and recurring on return per Shanahan's own comments about 2025, so treat the couple-week estimate as the real risk, not a floor. Picking Short-Term Injury given the reported ~2-week timeline; Mike Evans (see his note) is SF's clear top option in the meantime. REVISED FROM SHORT-TERM TO STANDARD INJURY (10/14): HC Kyle Shanahan's full Monday (10/12) comments walk back last cycle's ~2-week framing -- he said Samuel is "going to miss some time," specifically "at least the next couple of games and likely a bit longer," which is a real extension beyond the firm 1-2-week Short-Term framing (ABC7/ABC30, NBC Sports Bay Area, ClutchPoints via Ian Rapoport). Not on IR as of this update. Expect him to miss SF's Week 6 game at Washington (MNF 10/19) and likely Week 7 at Atlanta too, with San Francisco's Week 8 bye potentially extending the absence further before a real return estimate firms up. Mike Evans (7/113/1 in the Week 5 win over Seattle) and Brandin Cooks/Jacob Cowing are the clear beneficiaries in the meantime. NO CHANGE (10/28): Status flip to QUESTIONABLE is a feed artifact -- the 49ers are on their Week 8 bye (no game 10/29-11/2) after Sunday's Week 7 loss at Atlanta ended SF's unbeaten start. Samuel was again ruled OUT for that game with the hamstring injury dating to Week 5; no new timeline or Shanahan comment found. The bye remains the expected evaluation window before a possible Week 9 return at home vs. the Raiders (11/8). STILL OUT, TRENDING LONGER (11/5-8): 49ers GM John Lynch told KNBR's "Murph & Mack" (11/5-6) that both Samuel and Mike Evans are "unlikely" to be available for today's Week 9 home game vs. the Raiders -- Samuel was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, continuing a stretch dating to the original Week 5 hamstring strain (10/11) that's now cost him Weeks 6, 7, the Week 8 bye, and apparently Week 9. No official multi-week number or IR move has been reported, so keeping the standard Injury tier rather than escalating to Long-Term, but this is now a real extended absence worth watching closely for a possible IR move. RULED OUT AGAIN, NO NEW TIMELINE (11/8-10): missed Sunday's Week 9 home game vs. Las Vegas as GM John Lynch had signaled -- his third missed game of the five SF has played since the Week 5 hamstring strain (Weeks 6, 7, and 9, with the Week 8 bye in between). No fresh Shanahan comment or revised multi-week number turned up in search as of this update; a 'likely to miss remainder of the season' headline that surfaced in search traces to an unrelated 2020 Samuel injury, not this one, and is being disregarded. Keeping the standard Injury tier for now, but a 4th-straight missed game next week would support a move to Long-Term Injury. TRENDING TO RETURN (11/11): practicing again Wednesday after missing Weeks 6, 7, and 9 (bye in 8) with the hamstring strain -- SI reports his 'next chance to play will be Week 10 against the Dallas Cowboys' (SFStandard's David Lombardi via The Fantasy Footballers, SI, 11/11). No final designation yet since it's only Wednesday, but this is the most positive signal since the original Week 5 injury. Keeping the standard Injury tier rather than upgrading to Long-Term given the real chance he plays this week; would reconsider if he's held out again.

roster.reason: Established starter, no flags

roster.name: Jordan Love
roster.reason: Played Thursday night's Week 3 loss at Atlanta (Falcons won 35-14) with no recurrence of the Week 2 elbow/hand-numbness scare — a clean non-issue as expected. Final line: 28/53, 312 yards, 2 TD (Christian Watson 4-yard, Matthew Golden 15-yard), 1 INT, 75.4 rating, took only 1 sack. Note the yardage was inflated by heavy garbage-time volume (53 attempts) after Green Bay fell behind 27 unanswered points — treat this as a middling real performance dressed up by a big raw stat line (RotoWire/CBS Sports, Heavy.com, 9/24-25). Team-level concern: RT Zach Bako-Bewele's season-ending torn patellar tendon remains an O-line issue worth monitoring for Love's protection going forward. NEW (10/23): New issue, not a recurrence of the Week 2 elbow/hand scare -- Love was listed with a back injury and was a limited practice participant Wednesday 10/21 ahead of Sunday's Week 7 game at Detroit (Packers' injury report via The Athletic's Matt Schneidman, 10/21). Beat reporting frames his inclusion on the first Week 7 report as possibly precautionary but says it 'bears watching.' Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending Friday's final call. CLEARED (10/24): per our roster feed, the back flag resolved with no designation heading into Sunday's Week 7 game at Detroit -- independent beat confirmation of the Thursday/Friday practice detail wasn't available via search as of this update, but no setback has been reported anywhere, consistent with the earlier 'possibly precautionary' framing. Upgrading tag from Health Watch back to Healthy. CONFIRMED (10/27): the back flag was a non-issue -- played Sunday's Week 7 game at Detroit as expected with no setback, posting 16.96 fantasy points per our stats database (Green Bay fell 20-17; see Josh Jacobs' note for his side of that game). No new injury concern heading into Week 8.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.reason: CORRECTION + WEEK 7 RESULT (10/30): the previous update's reference to a "home game vs. Philadelphia" was wrong -- Minnesota's actual Week 7 opponent was Indianapolis (16-10 home win, 10/25), not the Eagles. Hockenson caught 4 of 5 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in that win, with no setback reported (NBC Sports). Minnesota's Week 8 opponent is a road trip to Detroit (Sun. 11/1). NEW -- WRIST/CHEST (11/11-13): picked up wrist and chest issues and did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (an estimated Wednesday report since Minnesota didn't hold a padded practice) ahead of Sunday's Week 10 game at Green Bay -- played 81% of the Week 9 snaps at Buffalo before this surfaced, so it's a new issue rather than an aggravation. No game-status designation attached yet as of Thursday; sources list it as TBD rather than a confirmed Questionable (Vikings.com, Star Tribune, Sharp Football Analysis, 11/11-12). Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending Friday's report.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.reason: The camp toe sprain didn't cost him any time — played through it in the Week 1 opener vs. Cincinnati, catching 5 of 6 targets for 63 yards. Locked in as Tampa Bay's WR1 with Mike Evans gone to SF. UPDATE (10/13-14): has fully taken over as Tampa Bay's clear top receiver amid the WR room's injuries -- 25 catches, 445 yards and 5 TD through 5 games. With Chris Godwin (fibula) and Bucky Irving (foot/shoulder) both ruled out for Week 6 vs. San Francisco (see their notes), Egbuka's target share should only grow further this week. Dontayvion Wicks (now himself cleared, see his note) projects for a season-high role in his absence. Keeping the standard Injury tier; recheck Friday's final practice report before trusting the "chance to return" framing from earlier in the week. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller are the direct backfield beneficiaries in the meantime; treat Etienne as a stash-only dynasty/IR piece for roughly a month.

roster.name: Alec Pierce
roster.reason: CONFIRMED: officially placed on injured reserve Wednesday 9/23 (HC Shane Steichen) after aggravating his surgically-repaired left heel late in Sunday's loss at Kansas City — couldn't put weight on it and left on crutches in a boot. ESPN sources report Pierce plans to rehab rather than undergo a second surgery; he and the club are "hopeful" for roughly a 4-6 week absence after a second opinion, with return targeted for midseason — IR guarantees a minimum 4 games missed, and the exact timeline remains rehab-dependent/unconfirmed. Colts signed veteran WR Darius Slayton (agreed to terms 9/22) as a direct replacement. Pierce had led the NFL in yards/catch among qualified WRs the past two seasons; expect targets to spread toward Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, Slayton, and TE Tyler Warren.

roster.name: Christian McCaffrey
roster.reason: Full workhorse usage in the opener with no ill effects from the calf scare: 10 carries for 68 yards plus 5 catches for 20 yards in the win over the Rams. Held out of the end zone, but the touch volume is exactly what you want to see after last year's injury history. HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed this week the Week 1 split with rookie Kaelon Black (who out-carried him 14-10, 44% of snaps) was a deliberate plan to lighten McCaffrey's load: "That was the goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more... love taking some off Christian." Total touches were even (15-15), but expect Black to keep chipping into the carry share. NEW (10/28): McCaffrey left Sunday's Week 7 loss at Atlanta (10/25) with a hip/thigh injury (reports differ on the exact body part) in the 2nd quarter, briefly replaced by rookie Kaelon Black, but returned and finished the game. No Shanahan severity comment found, and SF is on its Week 8 bye so there's no practice report to clarify further until Week 9 prep. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch out of caution; not treating this as a significant injury based on current information since he played through it the same day. CORRECTION + CLEARED (11/6-8): the Week 7 injury (10/25) that briefly pulled him from that game is a mild/Grade-1 hamstring strain, not a hip injury as an earlier note stated -- Kyle Shanahan explicitly described it as a hamstring strain after McCaffrey returned to finish that game with 7 carries/39 yards/TD plus 6 catches/61 yards. SF was "pretty optimistic" it wouldn't cost him time and targeted a return after the Week 8 bye; he was present for Thursday's practice this week and carries no designation for today's Week 9 home game vs. the Raiders. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; keeping Depth Chart Battle given rookie Kaelon Black's continued share of early-down work. POST-GAME CONFIRMATION (11/8-10): played Sunday's Week 9 home game vs. Las Vegas after being cleared on the mild/Grade-1 hamstring strain -- no setback reported. Stat line not independently confirmable via search as of this update. Remains Healthy.

roster.name: Parker Washington

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.reason: Missed Week 2 vs. New Orleans with the recurring hamstring injury (first tweaked in a Week 1 TD catch-and-run, aggravated further in that same game). CLEARED AND DELIVERED: active and effective in Sunday's Week 3 win over Dallas in Rio — 5 catches on 6 targets for 84 yards plus a 20-yard carry, turning half his touches into 20+ yard gains, including a 27-yard catch with time expiring that set up the game-winning field goal (NBC Sports, 9/27). No re-aggravation reported; the hamstring concern appears fully resolved with a full workload back in hand — Flowers projects back into his lead-receiver role for Baltimore. NEW (9/30): flipped back to a game-status designation (limited practice) as Baltimore continues managing the same hamstring that had him on a "pitch count" through Week 3's 5-catch, 84-yard game. HC Jesse Minter said Monday he expects Flowers to carry a full workload Week 4 vs. Tennessee; FantasyPros projects him roughly 79% likely to play with no new setback reported (NBC Sports, RotoWire, FantasyPros, 9/29-30). CLEARED (10/1-2): upgraded from limited to a full practice participant Thursday, officially shaking the hamstring designation ahead of Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Tennessee — full workload expected as Baltimore's lead receiver (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, 10/1-2). NEW DESIGNATION (10/2-3): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag again this week, but this reads as routine hamstring management rather than a new setback -- HC Jesse Minter said Flowers is "coming out of this thing really ready to push to be back in there closer to full time," and multiple outlets (RotoBaller, FantasyPros) are calling him a must-start WR1 Sunday vs. the 0-3 Titans if there's no in-week change. Watch Friday's final report, but treat this as a likely-to-play Questionable, not a real doubt. Entered Week 4 off a full Thursday practice with no setback, and OC/staff expected him to carry a full workload vs. Tennessee after Baltimore's win (team reports, 10/1). No new injury or designation has surfaced since; treating the hamstring issue as resolved and upgrading tag to Healthy as Baltimore's lead receiver. (Exact Week 4 box-score line could not be independently confirmed via search -- sourcing on the Ravens-Titans final was inconsistent.) UPDATE (10/8): the recurring hamstring issue produced another QUESTIONABLE tag -- Flowers was downgraded in Baltimore's final Week 4 injury report (questionable vs. Tennessee) and now carries the same designation into Sunday's Week 5 game at Atlanta as the team continues managing his workload week to week. No new injury or setback reported, just the same ongoing hamstring maintenance pattern. UPDATE (10/13): flipped from QUESTIONABLE back to ACTIVE. Pregame reporting had him questionable with a foot issue (distinct wording from the recurring hamstring, possibly just reporting inconsistency) but ESPN's Adam Schefter said he was expected to play Sunday night at Atlanta; Lamar Jackson (ankle) was out for that game with Tyler Huntley starting (see Jackson's note). Could not independently confirm the final score or Flowers' box-score line for that game via search as of this update -- treating today's ACTIVE flip as a likely no-new-designation reset for Week 6 rather than confirmed proof the hamstring is fully behind him. Recheck next cycle for the actual Week 5 result. Week 5 final (10/11): quiet by his standards but heavy volume -- 8 catches on 9 targets for 53 yards plus a 13-yard carry in Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win over Atlanta (Tyler Huntley started for the injured Lamar Jackson and scored the winning TD). No touchdown, and his longest catch went for just 12 yards -- a 26-yard grab on the late game-tying drive was wiped out by a defensive pass-interference penalty drawn in his favor. No new injury reported. NEW (10/15-16): added to Baltimore's Week 6 injury report with a toe injury, limited in both Thursday and Friday practice -- but no game designation on the final report, so he's good to play Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. Cleveland (10/18) per NBC Sports (10/16). Lamar Jackson's ankle (see his note) remains the bigger question mark for the Baltimore offense. CONFIRMED (10/18): today's QUESTIONABLE-to-ACTIVE flip matches what was already being reported -- the toe injury produced no game designation on Baltimore's final Week 6 report (NBC Sports, 10/16), so he's playing Sunday's home game vs. Cleveland at full workload as Baltimore's lead receiver. Lamar Jackson (ankle) is the bigger question for the passing game, now officially OUT (see his note) with Tyler Huntley starting.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.reason: Played in the opener as expected off Achilles recovery, but usage was light (2 catches, 12 yards on 5 targets, 46.2% of snaps) — matches Shanahan's stated plan to manage his snap count. The Achilles maintenance plan wrapped up clean — upgraded to a full practice Friday (9/18) and removed from the injury report entirely, with no designation for Sunday vs. Miami; Wed/Thu limited reps were confirmed as planned workload management, not a new setback (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, 9/18).

roster.name: Tony Pollard
roster.reason: Entrenched starter chasing a 5th straight 1,000-yard season — hit 1,000 rushing yards in each of the past 4 years. CLEARED: returned to a full practice Friday (9/25) and is off the final Week 3 injury report entirely — no designation for Sunday vs. the Giants (RotoWire, FantasyPros, NBC Sports, 9/25). Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (ankle) remains Questionable — if Spears is limited or sits, Pollard is positioned for an even bigger workload bump on top of his already-larger carry share (53.4% snap share to Spears' 42.7% through two weeks, with roughly double Spears' carries). NEW (9/30): a new foot injury (distinct from the ankle issue referenced earlier) — Pollard was a non-participant in Wednesday's Week 4 practice. HC Mike Vrabel's staff said they are "not overly concerned about Sunday" for Pollard and don't believe it will affect his Week 4 availability vs. Baltimore; backfield mate Tyjae Spears also sat out Wednesday with an ankle issue (CBS Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, Newsweek, 9/30). CLEARED (10/1-2): the foot issue that held him out of Wednesday's practice did not linger — Pollard returned to a full practice Thursday and carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Baltimore. Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (ankle) remains limited/Questionable, keeping Pollard's bell-cow workload intact (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 10/1-2). Week 4 final (10/4): the foot issue was a non-factor -- went for 16 carries, 48 yards and a 3-yard rushing TD plus 2 catches for 2 yards in a 24-18 loss to Baltimore that dropped Tennessee to 0-4. Backfield mate Tyjae Spears was marginal (2 carries, 7 yards), confirming Pollard as the clear lead back even in a lost season. Worth watching: with Tennessee winless, ESPN's Adam Schefter floated Pollard as a potential trade-deadline candidate -- no deal reported yet, just speculation (NBC Sports, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports, 10/4). NEW (10/8): did not practice Wednesday with a foot injury and is QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Houston; beat coverage describes it as a possible maintenance/veteran rest day rather than a new injury, consistent with how Tennessee has handled him in past weeks (10/7). CLEARED (10/8): back to a full practice participant Thursday after sitting out Wednesday with the foot issue -- on track to play Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Houston, continuing the pattern of maintenance-related absences that haven't cost him game time all season (Yahoo Sports/Titans beat, 10/8). Week 5 final (10/13): the foot was a non-issue and he played the full workload, but the game itself was ugly -- Houston routed Tennessee 26-3 (ESPN gameId 401872984, Titans.com, PFF), dropping the Titans to 0-5 (not 0-4 as noted last week; the winless streak continued, it did not end). Pollard carried 14 times for 52 yards with no catches or TDs reported (Yahoo Sports, RotoWire, FantasyPros). No new injury flagged out of the game; still Tennessee's clear lead back on a team now shopping for answers at 0-5. BIG GAME (10/29): erupted for an estimated ~129 rushing yards on a season-high ~25 carries and accounted for all 3 Tennessee touchdowns in a 27-24 loss to Cleveland in Week 7 (10/25) -- named a Week 7 fantasy MVP by at least one outlet with 36.5 total fantasy points, the league's top score for the week (Wolfsports, Fantasy Football Calculator). Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (knee) was inactive, clearing the way for a near-every-down workload. No new injury flagged; the earlier-season foot/maintenance issues have not recurred in weeks. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean recent run. NEW QUESTIONABLE FLIP (11/13-14): picked up a fresh QUESTIONABLE designation for Sunday's Week 10 home game vs. Jacksonville. No specific new injury type or practice-participation detail could be independently confirmed via search as of this update -- Tennessee's Week 10 injury coverage found several other starters (Anthony Hill Jr., Cody Barton, Peter Skoronski) and backfield mate Tyjae Spears tagged Questionable, but no corroborating Pollard-specific report. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch out of caution pending Friday's final word; recheck before treating this as a real absence risk.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.reason: Played through the previously undisclosed issue with no setback and led Pittsburgh's offense with 10 targets, turning them into 4 catches for 40 yards in the opener vs. Atlanta — the target volume was there even if the per-catch efficiency wasn't. Traded from Seattle to Pittsburgh in 2025 (Steelers sent a 2nd- and 7th-rounder, got back a 6th) and signed a 5-year, $150M extension there. UPDATE: named Steelers' Player of the Week after his Week 4 performance, remaining Pittsburgh's clear top target earner (Steelers.com, early week of 10/5). NEW (10/18): added to Pittsburgh's injury report Friday with an illness (not an injury) after missing practice -- RotoBaller reports he wasn't on the Wednesday/Thursday report, suggesting he started feeling sick late in the week. Steelers' WR room is thin behind him (Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek both out), so Germie Bernard would see a bigger role if Metcalf can't go Sunday vs. Tampa Bay. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch given the swift, late-week designation; illness-driven Questionable tags often clear on gameday, so recheck the final inactive list. CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/18): removed from Pittsburgh's injury report Saturday, ending the late-week illness scare, then delivered a big game in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over Tampa Bay -- 11 catches for 93 yards, tied with Germie Bernard (also 11 catches) for Pittsburgh's team high in receptions (Yahoo Sports, Behind the Steel Curtain, 10/18-19). Teammate Pat Freiermuth (calf) also carried a late QUESTIONABLE tag into the same game -- see his note. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean, productive game.

roster.name: A.J. Brown
roster.reason: Left his Patriots debut early in the 3rd quarter of the Sept 9 NFL Kickoff Game (a 13-10 loss to Seattle) with a right ankle injury after Seahawks CB Nehemiah Pritchett's knee landed on his ankle; had 3 catches for 26 yds on 4 targets before exiting. Thursday's (Sept 10) MRI confirmed a high-ankle sprain (Tuesday-night X-rays had been negative). Confirmed Sept 11 (AP): Patriots are placing him on injured reserve, officially ruling him out a minimum of four games under IR roster rules — New England is also signing DT DaQuan Jones as a separate roster move. Treat him as unplayable through at least Week 4. Arrived via trade from PHI (Patriots sent Philadelphia a 2028 1st-round pick and a 2027 5th-round pick); signed for up to $112.75M with $32.75M guaranteed. Was stepping into a wide-open target share atop New England's WR room before the injury. ACTIVATED AND RETURNED (10/18): activated off injured reserve and made his Patriots home debut in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets, ending a 4-game absence with the high-ankle sprain suffered in his Sept. 9 Patriots debut. The return was rusty -- just 3 catches for 27 yards on 9 targets with multiple drops, plus a muffed-onside-kick mishap his teammates covered for (Boston Globe, NESN, 10/18-19). Drake Maye (3 TD passes, 0 INT) carried New England's offense in the win; expect Brown's role/rapport to build gradually. Downgrading tag from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch now that he's actually back on the field. MANAGED, NOT A SETBACK (10/20-21): limited at Monday's walkthrough and Tuesday's practice with the same high-ankle sprain he returned from last week, but this reads as short-week load management rather than a new issue -- Brown told reporters he's "absolutely" ready for Thursday night's Week 7 game at the Bears, and HC Mike Vrabel and Brown himself both describe the ankle as not a lingering concern (ESPN's Mike Reiss, Heavy.com, Athlon, 10/20). Keeping Health Watch; today's QUESTIONABLE game-status flip is expected to clear by Thursday's kickoff. WEEK 7 ACTUAL (10/22): played the whole game at Chicago with the ankle fully behind him -- removed from the injury report entirely with no designation heading into Thursday, then finished 3-for-6 for 48 yards in the 30-24 loss, his second quiet game in as many weeks since returning (3-for-10 in Week 6 vs. the Jets, with multiple drops). Ankle is no longer a health question -- downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; remaining inefficiency looks like QB-WR rust/chemistry, not a physical issue (RotoBaller, TSN, 10/22-23). NEW (10/30): picked up a QUESTIONABLE tag again this week ahead of New England's Week 8 road game at Miami (Sun. 11/1) -- no fresh beat-writer report tying this to a new or worsening ankle issue could be confirmed via search as of this update. Treat cautiously as a possible placeholder reset rather than a confirmed setback; downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending Friday's official word. RULED INACTIVE, SURPRISE SCRATCH (11/1-2): despite being a full practice participant all week, Brown was held out of Sunday's Week 8 game at Miami -- multiple outlets (Patriots.com, NESN, Yahoo Sports/SI) confirm he was a surprise inactive, with reporting split between a newly-flared-up knee issue and the previously-managed ankle as the driver. No firm diagnosis or return timeline has been reported. New England also lost Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins to inactives, and TE Hunter Henry left in the 2nd quarter with a new foot injury (see his note), but still rallied from a 10-point halftime deficit for a 24-19 comeback win behind Drake Maye; Stefon Diggs, Kayshon Boutte, and DeMario Douglas absorbed the extra targets. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the real missed game and lack of a confirmed timeline. STILL UNRESOLVED (11/2-4): the knee issue behind last week's surprise Week 8 inactive remains up in the air for Sunday's Week 9 home game vs. Green Bay -- HC Mike Vrabel said "we'll see" when asked Monday if Brown would even practice this week, and no Wednesday practice designation had surfaced as of this update. Still tracking alongside the separate ankle injury that cost him New England's first four games this season (Yahoo Sports, ESPN, Bleacher Report, 11/2-3). STILL OUT, SECOND STRAIGHT WEEK (11/5-8): missed practice again Thursday (knee, stacked on the earlier ankle sprain) and is ruled OUT for today's Week 9 home game vs. Green Bay -- a second straight missed game. HC Mike Vrabel had said "we'll see" on 11/2 about whether Brown would even practice this week; no outlet has yet named a specific diagnosis or return timeline for the knee. Keeping the standard Injury tier given the continued uncertainty. REVISED FROM INJURY TO LONG-TERM INJURY (11/5-10): officially missed a second straight game Sunday vs. Green Bay with the knee -- Adam Schefter confirmed (11/5) the issue is specifically the knee (not the earlier-healed ankle), and NFL Network's Tom Pelissero reports the Patriots are 'optimistic' Brown can return only after New England's Week 11 bye. That projects to a four-game-plus absence (Weeks 8-10 plus the bye) before a possible Week 12 return, which crosses the Long-Term Injury threshold -- upgrading the tag accordingly. This is a separate issue from the Week 1 high-ankle sprain that already cost him four games earlier this season. QUESTIONABLE FLIP LOOKS LIKE A PLACEHOLDER, NOT A REAL CLEARANCE (11/11): the roster tracker flipped him from OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Week 10, but extensive search turned up no new reporting beyond the 11/5-7 line (Pelissero/Boston.com) that the Patriots are 'optimistic' he returns only after New England's Week 11 bye -- i.e., a projected Week 12 return, not Week 10. No corroborating practice report or coach comment supports an actual clearance. Keeping Long-Term Injury; treating the QUESTIONABLE tag as a likely system placeholder rather than real medical news, and will recheck as the week progresses. BACK AT PRACTICE, SOONER THAN PROJECTED (11/11-13): after missing two straight games with the knee issue and an earlier 11/5-7 report that projected a return only after New England's Week 11 bye (i.e., Week 12), Brown has actually returned to practice this week -- limited both Wednesday and Thursday ahead of Sunday's Week 10 game at Detroit (Munich, Germany). No official game-status designation has been attached yet. This is a genuinely positive development versus the prior projection, but he hasn't been given a game-status clearance yet, so keeping Long-Term Injury until he's actually active for a game; will revisit immediately if he's cleared to play Sunday.

roster.name: Woody Marks
roster.reason: Was Houston's clear passing-down/receiving-work back behind David Montgomery through the first several weeks, holding real standalone value even in a committee. NEW (10/13): took over as Houston's lead back after David Montgomery exited Sunday's Week 5 win over Tennessee (26-3) with a groin injury -- finished with a season-high 15 carries for 62 yards plus 4 catches, reportedly logging roughly 85% of the Texans' backfield snaps once Montgomery left (FantasyPros, Athlon Sports, SI/OnSI, 10/12). With Montgomery now DOUBTFUL/week-to-week (see his note), Marks projects as Houston's clear lead back for as long as that lasts. UPDATE (10/13): confirmed to keep the expanded lead-back role for Week 6 in Montgomery's continued absence, replicating his Week 5 workload (15 carries/62 yards, 4 catches) -- per FantasyFootballers and CBS Sports (~10/13). Jawhar Jordan and practice-squad RB Deuce Vaughn are the depth pieces behind him if needed. NEW -- KNEE (11/11-13): picked up a knee injury this week, limited at Wednesday's Texans practice ahead of Sunday's Week 10 road game at Cleveland; one outlet (Battle Red Blog) has him as a Thursday non-participant instead, so the trend is unclear -- worth confirming Friday's report. Still Houston's clear lead-role back when healthy alongside David Montgomery's continued absence (see his note). Adding Health Watch given the real uncertainty.

roster.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
roster.reason: Finished 2025 as the No. 2 fantasy TE in PPR and was projected top-5 again in 2026 as one of Penix's top two targets alongside London, but the profile hasn't shown up in the box score through 3 games. NEW: just 1 catch on 2 targets for 5 yards in Thursday night's Week 3 win over Green Bay (35-14) — his line through 3 games is now just 2 catches for 20 yards on 6 targets. QB Michael Penix Jr. is clearly funneling the passing game elsewhere (London had a 9/194 day the same game); worth downgrading expectations until target share shows up (RotoWire/NBC Sports, 9/24).

roster.name: Matthew Stafford
roster.reason: Reigning NFL MVP — led the league in passing yards (4,707) and TD passes (46) in 2025; real regression risk since his 2025 leaned on unsustainable red-zone efficiency. Went 22-of-31 for 327 yards, 4 TD, 1 INT in Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants; his 426th career passing touchdown moved him past Philip Rivers into 6th all-time (NFL.com, Yahoo Sports). NEW (11/2-4): added to the Rams' injury report with arm/elbow soreness -- reports conflict on whether it's the throwing arm broadly or specifically the elbow. HC Sean McVay called it day-to-day soreness rather than a clear structural injury and said he'll defer to Stafford on how he's feeling; officially TBD/Questionable for Sunday's Week 9 game at Washington. Monitor Friday's report (CBS Sports, DraftKings, RotoWire, 11/2-3). CLEARED (11/6): the arm/elbow soreness that had him TBD/Questionable earlier this week produced no game-status designation -- carries no injury flag into Sunday's Week 9 game at Washington. No specific Friday practice report was independently confirmed via search as of this update, but the clean designation itself is a real signal; upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

roster.name: Ollie Gordon II
roster.reason: Stepped in after De'Von Achane tore his ACL in Week 3 vs. Kansas City (season-ending) — 17 carries for 41 yards and a TD, plus 3 catches for 14 yards on 3 targets in relief (Yahoo Sports, Bleacher Report, 9/27-28). Miami's backfield is now a committee with Jaylen Wright (trending back healthy for Week 4) — analysts project roughly a 60/40 split favoring Wright, with Gordon getting goal-line/early-down work. One of the top Week 4 waiver adds league-wide given the timeshare upside (SI/OnSI, Yahoo Sports). Week 4 final (10/4): dominated the Miami backfield in the 15-10 loss to Minnesota -- 9 carries for 100 yards and a TD plus 2 targets on 22 snaps, clearly outplaying Jaylen Wright (5 carries/7 yards, 12 snaps -- see his note). With De'Von Achane out for the season, Gordon now looks like the favorite for lead-back work in Miami's backfield heading into Week 5, not just a 50/50 committee piece (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Heavy.com, 10/4).

roster.name: Quinshon Judkins
roster.reason: Moved to the unambiguous RB1 spot on Cleveland's depth chart, ahead of Sampson and Sanders. Battling a minor "nagging" injury that cost him two camp practices, but coaches aren't concerned — remains Cleveland's clear lead back over Dylan Sampson, Raheim Sanders, and Ahmani Marshall. 2025 2nd-round pick (36th overall, Ohio State), acquired via a Day 1 trade with Jacksonville. Handled 12 of Cleveland's 15 RB carries plus 5 catches (17 touches, 48 total yards) in the Week 2 win over Tampa Bay, confirming him as the clear #1 back even in a tough matchup (CBS Sports, RotoWire). NEW (10/13): picked up a new right ankle "tweak" in Sunday's Week 5 loss to the Jets (10/11); HC Kevin Stefanski called it day-to-day and said he'll "have a chance to play" Week 6 vs. Baltimore (RotoWire, NBC Sports, 10/12). Worth watching closely -- it's the same ankle/fibula area he surgically repaired after a dislocation/fracture last season, which has some beat writers flagging it even though team language is cautiously optimistic (Yahoo Sports/Heavy, Dawg Pound Daily, 10/12). No official Wed/Thu/Fri practice grade confirmed yet -- recheck before Week 6. If he sits, Raheim Sanders would be next in line, though Sanders himself left the same game with a hip injury and his own availability is a wrinkle (ESPN). UPDATE (10/14): did NOT practice Wednesday with the ankle, per NBC Sports/RotoWire -- he was seen in the locker room without the walking boot he'd worn postgame Sunday, a mildly positive visual sign, but no Thursday/Friday practice grade had posted as of this update; his Week 6 call vs. Baltimore still hinges on the rest of the week's practice participation. Correction: the "day-to-day, has a chance to play" comment is attributed by multiple outlets to OC Todd Monken, not HC Kevin Stefanski as previously framed -- flagging since the original Stefanski attribution could not be verified. Separately, backup Raheim Sanders (hip, same Week 5 game) was placed on IR Tuesday (10/13), so he will NOT be available if Judkins sits -- Cleveland signed RB Audric Estime off Minnesota's practice squad as added depth, with Jaleel McLaughlin also in the mix. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty and Wednesday DNP. UPDATE (10/16): did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the ankle, though he was seen without his walking boot. Beat writers still frame him as "day-to-day" without a firm ruling, but Cleveland signed RB Audric Estime off Minnesota's practice squad this week as insurance, and Dawg Pound Daily reports the trend points toward Jaleel McLaughlin as Sunday's lead back vs. Baltimore (10/18) if Judkins sits. CONFIRMED OUT (10/18): did not play in Cleveland's 13-10 win over Baltimore -- tested in pregame warmups on the ankle he tweaked in Week 5 (the same surgically-repaired ankle/fibula from last season) before being held out (USA Today/Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 10/18). Jaleel McLaughlin (9 carries/41 yards) and Audric Estime (9 carries/19 yards, including the game-tying 2-yard TD) split the backfield work in his absence. No firm return timeline has been reported yet for Week 7; recheck Wednesday's practice report. Keeping the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty and the injury's proximity to last year's more serious ankle/fibula fracture. UPDATE (10/22): upgraded to a LIMITED practice participant Wednesday (10/21) -- a real step up from last week's DNP -- with Dylan Sampson also absent from Cleveland's non-participant list, per the Akron Beacon Journal's Chris Easterling. OC Todd Monken said he's "optimistic" about Judkins' availability for Sunday's Week 7 game vs. Tennessee but stopped short of guaranteeing it. Trending positive; keeping the standard Injury tier until he logs a full practice or a firmer designation posts. CLEARED (10/25): carries no injury designation into today's Week 7 game vs. Tennessee -- the right ankle/fibula-area injury that cost him Week 6 has resolved enough for him to suit up, continuing last week's positive trend (upgraded to limited practice Wed 10/21, with HC Todd Monken 'optimistic'). Upgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Healthy; remains Cleveland's unambiguous RB1. BIG GAME (10/28): Cleared off Friday's injury report (ankle) and ran for 96 yards and 2 TDs on 17 carries in Cleveland's 27-24 win over Tennessee (10/25), continuing to look like the unambiguous RB1 coming off last week's ankle scare.

roster.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
roster.reason: Opened 2026 with 8 catches for 122 yds and the game-winning 45-yard TD (41 YAC) on 4th-and-1 in the 4th quarter of Seattle's 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game win over New England — early sign the regression fears may be overblown. Backup QB Drew Lock (18/22, 187 yds) finished that game after starter Sam Darnold left with a hip injury on the opening drive; Darnold's Thursday (Sept 10) MRI showed no major structural damage ("dodged a bullet," per the team), but he's still expected to miss Week 2 at Arizona with Lock confirmed as the Week 2 starter — worth tracking since it affects who's throwing Smith-Njigba the ball. Led all NFL WRs with 1,793 yds/10 TD in 2025 and won Offensive Player of the Year; now the highest-paid WR in history (4yr/$168.6M). Top-5 overall fantasy asset — the question is regression off a historic year, not upside. NEW (10/14): picked up a minor ankle injury on a 16-yard lateral run in the second quarter of Seattle's 32-29 Week 5 loss at San Francisco (10/11) -- it didn't meaningfully slow him down; he still topped 100 receiving yards for the 5th straight game, pushing his NFL-leading total to 583 yards and 7 TDs through 5 games. Xavier Worthy continues to absorb the added targets. CBS Sports reports he's likely to remain unavailable for the foreseeable future -- this reads as materially more serious than a standard illness designation. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Long-Term Injury given the open-ended, undiagnosed nature of the absence; a situation to keep monitoring closely rather than a standard injury with a known recovery arc. SERIOUS HEALTH SITUATION REVEALED, ESCALATING TO LONG-TERM INJURY (11/6-10): what had been logged here as a routine 'illness' is far more serious -- Henderson said in his own statement (posted to X, 11/6) that he was hospitalized for several days with 'unexplained neurological symptoms' affecting his strength, coordination and other physical functions. He says extensive testing has come back 'positive and reassuring' but doctors have not identified a cause, and he continues working with specialists. Independently verified via Yahoo Sports, CNN, Fox News, CBS Sports and NBC Sports (all 11/6). He was ruled OUT again for Sunday's Week 9 home game vs. Green Bay, and CBS Sports reports he's likely out for the foreseeable future with no timeline. Rhamondre Stevenson (see his note) is New England's clear lead back in his absence. Upgrading from Health Watch/Depth Chart Battle to Long-Term Injury given the open-ended, undiagnosed nature of this absence -- this needs close day-to-day monitoring rather than a standard injury recovery arc. QUESTIONABLE FLIP LOOKS LIKE A PLACEHOLDER, NOT A REAL CLEARANCE (11/11): the roster tracker flipped him from OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Week 10, but no reporting beyond the 11/6 hospitalization statement (unexplained neurological symptoms, tests 'positive and reassuring,' no diagnosis, no timeline) could be found confirming any actual improvement or clearance. Given the serious, open-ended nature disclosed just five days ago, treating this as a likely system placeholder rather than a real recovery signal. J.K. Dobbins led Denver's backfield in carries Sunday (17 att/49 yds, still without a rushing TD this year) but Harvey's role as the clear passing-down/receiving back is intact; Jonah Coleman remains on IR (high ankle sprain, out at least through Week 6). Week 6 TNF (10/15): scored his first rushing TD of the season (1-yard) in Denver's 17-14 OT win over Seattle, finishing with 6 carries for 25 yards plus 3 catches on 4 targets for 31 yards -- led Denver in receiving. J.K. Dobbins also scored on the ground (see his note); Denver's backfield split continues with no clear lead-back resolution. Week 7 (10/25): just 3 carries for 6 yards in Denver's 30-16 win over Arizona, though his lone touch of real fantasy value was a 52-yard TD catch on a screen pass. Newly-activated Jonah Coleman (9 carries/54 yds -- see his note) led the Broncos' three-way backfield committee in touches this week, muddying what was previously viewed as Harvey's clear passing-down role. Keeping Health Watch; monitor next week for whether Coleman's usage holds. RULED OUT, SHORT TERM (10/31): suffered a knee injury at Thursday's practice (10/29), did not practice Friday, and was officially ruled OUT for Sunday's game at Kansas City (11/1) -- Denver's first missed game of the season for him (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Mile High Report, ClutchPoints, 10/30). Multiple reports frame it as not believed to be serious, with a source telling The Denver Post it's not expected to be a long-term absence; his next chance to play is Week 9 at Carolina. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Short-Term Injury given the OUT designation paired with the not-serious, quick-return framing. Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins are expected to split Denver's backfield work in his absence Sunday. REVISED, NOW LONG-TERM (10/31-11/1): further reporting confirms Harvey was placed on injured reserve for the knee injury suffered at Thursday's (10/29) practice -- not just a one-week OUT as his initial designation suggested. Multiple outlets (Yahoo Sports, The Broncos Blitz, Mile High Report) report he's sidelined a minimum of 4 games, with eligibility to return the home game vs. Miami on Dec. 6 (roughly Weeks 9-12 missed). This is a real walk-back from the earlier "not believed to be serious"/quick-return framing -- revising tag from Short-Term Injury to Long-Term Injury per that confirmed IR timeline. Jonah Coleman is now the clear lead back in Denver's backfield (see his note), with J.K. Dobbins as the secondary option and Cody Schrader elevated as depth; this is more a Coleman-led arrangement than the even three-way split in recent weeks. ROSTER FEED CONFIRMS IR (11/2): today's status flip from OUT to INJURY_RESERVE in our roster feed is simply the official confirmation of the IR placement already reported yesterday for the knee injury suffered at practice (10/29) -- no new information beyond the prior update. Keeping Long-Term Injury; Jonah Coleman remains Denver's clear lead back with J.K. Dobbins secondary (see Coleman's note).

Puka Nacua.name: Puka Nacua
bullets: Missed Monday Night Football vs. the Giants (9/21) with a hip/groin issue and stayed OUT all last week; HC Sean McVay confirmed there's no hernia involved.
CONFIRMED: sat out Week 3's 30-26 loss at Denver (9/27) as expected off the DOUBTFUL tag — his second straight missed game with the groin/hip issue.

UPDATE (9/28-29): McVay said the Rams are "hopeful" Nacua can return for Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia, but has since tempered that to "to be determined" and confirmed Nacua will again be limited in practice this week. The team still views it as a short-term issue and believes he's capable of playing now, just not at full explosiveness — no new setback or structural diagnosis, and surgery/IR remain off the table for now (CBS Sports, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, 9/28-29). Keeping Short-Term Injury tag; Davante Adams remains the clear top target in his absence.

UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia. Nothing new medically — this reflects the calendar reaching the week HC Sean McVay has targeted since Week 2. McVay called himself "hopeful" Nacua plays (9/28), described the injury as "almost like pre-hernia" soreness, and said there's "no consideration" of IR; Adam Schefter reports the Rams don't believe surgery will be needed. A follow-up read was more guarded ("to be determined"), so treat this as genuinely 50/50 with a slight lean toward playing, final call likely Friday practice status (NBC Sports, ESPN, CBS Sports, 9/28-29). Davante Adams remains the top target if he sits again.

CLEARED TOWARD PLAYING (10/1-2): logged a full practice Thursday after a limited Wednesday session, with McVay firmly expecting him to play Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia; surgery is not currently expected (SI, NBC Sports, 10/1).

SEPARATE STORYLINE — Personal Conduct Policy: Nacua remains under an active NFL conduct-policy review tied to a civil lawsuit (alleging a bite and an antisemitic remark) and has begun steps toward a diversion program on related misdemeanor charges. He has not been placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List and ESPN's Adam Schefter says there's a real chance he plays out the season with no discipline, but the league can still act at any point since there's no decision deadline — a background risk to monitor, separate from the groin injury (CBS Sports, Fox News/Outkick, 10/1-2).

CLEARED (10/3): officially off the injury-worry list -- full practice participant all week and HC Sean McVay firmly expects him to play Sunday's Week 4 game at Philadelphia with no game-time-decision framing anymore; surgery was never on the table. Downgrading tag from Short-Term Injury to Healthy. Separate conduct-policy review (civil suit) remains unresolved and worth continued background monitoring, but is no longer tied to his on-field availability.

CONFIRMED (10/4-5): played a full workload at Philadelphia in Week 4, posting 14 catches, 199 yards and a rushing TD (our stats database has this at 27.7 fantasy points) despite the Rams' loss (ESPN gameId 401772839). The hip/groin issue (variably described as hip vs. groin, unrelated to his earlier psoas issue) did not limit his role at all -- team-leading target share in the loss, with no lingering concern reported as of 10/5. Upgrading tag from Healthy to include WR1 Lock given the workload. Note: the separate NFL conduct-policy review (civil suit) remains open and unrelated to his on-field availability -- continue monitoring in the background.

UPDATE (10/13): put up a monster line in the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday Night Football (10/12) -- 17 catches (a career-high 24 targets) for 138 yards and a TD. The Rams fell to 2-3 despite the huge game, partly because K Harrison Mevis missed two field goals, including a potential game-winner in overtime (see his note) -- therams.com, Deseret News, AP/Boston Globe.

PLAYED THROUGH IT (10/25): the calf injury that limited practice this week (DNP Friday, feeling better Saturday per sources, with a clean MRI) did not keep him out -- recent recaps have his most current line at 9 catches for 125 yards on 12 targets plus a 2-yard rushing TD in the Rams' Week 7 win over Las Vegas, with no in-game setback reported. Keeping WR1 Lock and Health Watch.

CLEARED, Week 8 (10/27): carries no injury designation entering this week after playing through the calf issue in Week 7 -- officially ACTIVE with no new concern reported. Keeping WR1 Lock and Health Watch; separate NFL conduct-policy review remains open in the background.

NEW QUESTIONABLE TAG (11/10): picked up a fresh QUESTIONABLE designation heading into Week 10 -- specific injury/practice report not independently confirmed via search as of this update. Keeping WR1 Lock and Health Watch pending more detail; flagging now rather than waiting given his workhorse role.

NEW QUESTIONABLE TAG (11/9-10): picked up a QUESTIONABLE designation this week after having no injury concern since clearing a calf issue in Week 7. No specific fresh practice report or injury type could be independently confirmed via search as of this update -- flagging the real uncertainty rather than assuming a placeholder reset, but also not able to confirm a new injury. Keeping Health Watch; will recheck once a practice/injury report surfaces.

MAJOR ESCALATION -- KNEE + TURF TOE, LIKELY IR (11/9-11): suffered MCL and PCL sprains in his right knee plus a turf toe injury on the final offensive snap of the Rams' Week 9 win over Washington (11/9); HC Sean McVay confirmed the MRI results and said there is no ACL tear, but Nacua is expected to miss at least 4 games, with McVay indicating an IR move is likely (the hesitation is only due to the Rams having limited IR-return slots left this year) (AP wire via KIRO7/Boston25, FOX Sports, Forbes, DraftKings Network, The Fantasy Footballers, 11/9-11).
