No change to severity/diagnosis from the 11/9-11 report. Keeping Long-Term Injury.

Jayden Daniels.name: Jayden Daniels
bullets: Dislocated his left (non-throwing) elbow — the same joint's 2nd dislocation within under a year — late in the first half of Washington's 37-20 Week 2 loss to Dallas (Sun 9/20); X-rays showed no fracture. Ruled out for Week 3 vs. Seattle, with Marcus Mariota named starting QB (Dan Quinn, 9/22 presser).

NEW (AP, ~9/23): imaging and multiple specialist opinions found NO ligament damage, and Daniels will NOT need surgery; the Commanders are not placing him on IR "for now" (FOX Sports/AP, NBC Sports/PFT, ProFootballRumors) — a real upgrade from Tuesday's total-uncertainty read.

Still no firm return timetable — HC Dan Quinn has declined to commit to one, with re-evaluation expected to continue toward Washington's Week 7 bye. Mariota remains the starter in the interim, and the recurring nature of the injury (2nd dislocation of the same elbow in <1 year) keeps real season-long variance in play even without surgery.

UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Week 4 (in London vs. Indianapolis). He returned to practice this week and traveled with the team, and per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz told teammates he's foregoing surgery and felt he "owed it to them" to return as fast as possible (RotoWire, Washington Times, Hogs Haven, 9/28). HC Dan Quinn said he isn't sure yet if Daniels plays "in six days" but that he "isn't far off" and will practice "in some form" this week. Read this as soft/early-stage QUESTIONABLE, not a real lean toward playing — nearly every outlet still has Marcus Mariota as the presumptive Week 4 starter pending how practice reps go Wed-Fri.

CONFIRMED OUT (10/2-3): ruled out for Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Colts in London -- ESPN's Adam Schefter does not believe Daniels will be active despite making the trip and practicing in some form. Marcus Mariota remains the favorite to start unless Daniels takes the bulk of first-team reps, which hasn't happened (CBS Sports, RotoBaller, Commanders.com, 10/1-3). No surgery still planned this season; recurring elbow dislocation keeps real multi-week variance in play.

CONFIRMED (10/5): did not play Week 4 vs. the Colts in London; Marcus Mariota started for a second straight game and Washington won 17-16 (Colts.com). Per Adam Schefter, Daniels will "eventually need surgery" on the elbow (this is the THIRD dislocation of the same non-throwing elbow within under a year) but is deferring it to the offseason and will likely play in a brace whenever he returns -- no practice/return timeline has been given as of 10/5 (NBC Sports). Given the recurring nature of the injury and no near-term surgical or return plan, upgrading tag from standard Injury to Long-Term Injury; Mariota remains the starter indefinitely.

IMPROVING, REVISED (10/7): real progress this week -- HC Dan Quinn said Daniels is set for a full Wed-Thu-Fri practice week with the goal of starting Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants, wearing the elbow brace (ESPN, TSN). Added urgency: backup Marcus Mariota suffered his own MCL sprain vs. the Colts, making 7th-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis the emergency option if Daniels can't go. Some practice-report aggregators still show a "limited" tag, so treat this as a real but not fully resolved Questionable rather than a lock. Revising tag down from Long-Term Injury to Health Watch given the firm full-practice/start-Sunday trajectory -- no longer an open-ended absence.

CLEARED (10/8): officially flipped from Questionable to Active ahead of Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants after a full Wednesday practice; per Jay Glazer, Washington plans to start Daniels in the elbow brace, and Tom Pelissero reports the team remains hopeful he returns to the starting role (ESPN, CBS Sports, 10/7-8). Backup situation is in flux -- Marcus Mariota aggravated the same MCL he had surgically repaired in 2022 and is doubtful/out, which only reinforces that Washington needs Daniels back now.

CONFIRMED HEALTHY RETURN (10/12): started Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. the Giants in the elbow brace and delivered a big dual-threat performance in a 27-27 overtime tie -- 17-of-25 passing for 199 yards with no interceptions (despite 5 sacks), plus 103 rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns on 9 carries. No setback to the surgically-pending elbow reported. Washington lost a late chance to win in OT after a Daniels scramble ran out the clock instead of spiking it.

WEEK 10 TNF RESULT (11/12-13): threw two interceptions on back-to-back fourth-quarter possessions in Thursday night's game at the Giants, but engineered a game-winning final drive capped by a 32-yard TD pass to Stefon Diggs with under a minute left, lifting Washington to a 24-21 win and keeping the Commanders' (3-5-1) playoff hopes alive. No injury reported.

NEW (10/8): flipped to QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington after not practicing Wednesday with a knee issue (Giants' official injury report, giants.com, 10/7) -- notable given his 2025 season ended with a torn ACL/meniscus in the same knee, though no beat writer has reported a new tear or setback. Treat as a practice-report flag to watch through Friday, not a confirmed re-injury.

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington -- no setback reported from the knee soreness that had him DNP Wednesday (the knee is the same one that ended his 2025 season with a torn ACL/meniscus, but no new tear or setback has been reported). HC/beat coverage from the Giants was cautiously upbeat all week (bolavip, Newsweek, 10/7-9).

BIG GAME (10/28): Caught 7 passes for 111 yards in the Giants' 27-21 OT win over Houston (10/25), maintaining his role as the clear top target through New York's QB shuffle (Winston/McCarthy). No health concerns reported since his early-October knee scare resolved; upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy and reflecting his locked-in role with WR1 Lock.

NEW (11/6-7): added to the Giants' injury report with a knee issue -- a non-participant Thursday, full participant Friday, and no final game-status designation heading into Sunday's Week 9 game at Philadelphia. New Giants HC John Harbaugh (hired this past offseason, replacing Brian Daboll, who was fired back in November 2025 -- correcting a stale "Daboll" reference in an earlier Giants-related note) called it "an in-season type thing" and said Nabers will be full-go; Nabers told reporters he'd "be good" for Sunday. No outlet has described this as a re-aggravation of his 2025 ACL/meniscus injury (CBS Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, Rotowire, Big Blue View, 11/5-6). Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch out of caution given the knee history, but current reporting points to a minor, managed issue.

CLEARED (11/6-7): missed Thursday's practice with the knee issue but was a full participant Friday and carries no game designation for today's Week 9 home game vs. Philadelphia -- HC John Harbaugh confirmed Nabers will be "full-go" (Heavy.com, SI.com/OnSI, 11/6). Resolves the in-season knee flare with no indication of a new ACL/meniscus setback. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

POST-GAME CONFIRMATION (11/8-10): played Sunday's Week 9 game at Philadelphia as expected after clearing the knee issue -- final stat line not independently confirmable via search as of this update. No setback reported. Remains Healthy.

bullets: Led the NFL with 323 carries in 2025 — 1,585 yds, 18 rush TD, RB1 overall.
New contract extension cements him as the Colts' offensive centerpiece; staff may trim touches slightly to manage wear, but role security is elite.
New extension (announced Aug 6, 2026): 2 years, $44M ($39M guaranteed, up to $47M) — the 2nd-highest-paid RB in the NFL by AAV.

TRADE WATCH (10/28): Speculation around Taylor has intensified after the Colts fired GM Chris Ballard (week of 10/22), with ESPN and Field Level Media reporting Green Bay, Seattle, Denver and Minnesota among potential suitors ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. No deal has been made, and Indianapolis reportedly wants to see more games before deciding; Taylor himself says he hasn't considered it. Monitor closely through the deadline -- a trade would warrant a New Team tag if it happens.

TRADE BUZZ ESCALATING (11/3-5): speculation intensified after Indianapolis traded away G Quenton Nelson and DT DeForest Buckner (week of 10/27), which multiple outlets frame as "opening the door" to also moving Taylor ahead of Tuesday's (11/10) trade deadline -- the Giants and Vikings are now reported as the current frontrunners, with Green Bay and Denver also mentioned. No deal has been made as of this update, and Indianapolis reportedly wants to see more game action before deciding; Taylor himself says he hasn't considered it. Would warrant a New Team tag if a trade is finalized before the deadline.

CONFIRMED: despite HC Andy Reid's talk of "balance" with rookie Emmett Johnson, Walker's Week 3 role barely budged — 78% of the RB snaps and 20 of 23 RB carry opportunities before the final drive, extending his streak to three straight weeks with a 70%+ snap share and 20+ PPR points in a 24-10 win over Miami. Dolphins did hold him to just 16 yards from scrimmage after halftime, worth monitoring, but the workhorse role itself is unchanged (Arrowhead Pride, RotoWire, 9/28).

Ja'Marr Chase (see his note) also cleared concussion protocol and had a big game in the same contest.

Joe Burrow.name: Joe Burrow
bullets: Played through the back tightness as expected — active and started Cincinnati's 20-6 win over Houston (Sun 9/20), going 20/31 for 207 yards and 2 TDs (both to Ja'Marr Chase, from 32 and 18 yards) with no INTs, though he did take 5 sacks.
Confirms the back issue was minor/day-to-day as reported all week — no setback, no in-game re-aggravation reported, and no new limitation entering Week 3 prep.
Elite passing-volume QB1 when right — the profile concern remains price/ADP more than health at this point.

De'Zhaun Stribling.name: De'Zhaun Stribling

Drop-and-stash-if-needed territory in shallow leagues for the next couple of months. Still a real deep-league breakout stash for whenever SF's WR room opens back up.

Sam LaPorta.name: Sam LaPorta
bullets: The hip flare-up was a non-issue once games started — produced in both Week 1 (9.8 fantasy pts, opener vs. New Orleans) and Week 2 (17.2 fantasy pts in Thursday night's win over Buffalo), with no re-aggravation reported.

Jonah Coleman.name: Jonah Coleman
bullets: With both RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins banged up, Coleman led Denver's backfield in Week 2 snap share (42.4%), touches (13) and total yards (58 plus a TD) in the win over Jacksonville — his first career rushing TD. Named a top Week 3 waiver-wire target by NFL.com (9/24).

REVISED (from the earlier "minor, shouldn't affect gameday status" framing, then from last update's "short absence" framing): the ankle is a high ankle sprain, and Denver placed Coleman on injured reserve Saturday (9/26) rather than just ruling him out week-to-week — he's expected back no sooner than Oct. 25 vs. Arizona (first eligible date), meaning at least 4 additional games missed on top of Week 3 (ESPN, NFL.com, Denver Gazette, CBS Sports, 9/26). Upgrading the tag from Short-Term to Long-Term Injury to reflect the real, IR-confirmed absence.

The good news for Denver: both J.K. Dobbins (hip) and RJ Harvey (hamstring) escaped the injury report with no designation and are expected to play Week 3 — the backfield rotation should run through them for the next several weeks with Coleman on IR.

UPDATE (10/5): remains on IR with the Week 2 high-ankle sprain, first eligible to return Week 7 (no change to the previously reported Oct. 25 vs. Arizona target). Denver lost Week 4 to the Chargers; in that game J.K. Dobbins clearly won the early-down split over RJ Harvey -- 11 carries for 83 yards and a TD plus a catch, vs. just 2 carries for 2 yards and 3 catches for 14 yards for Harvey (CBS Sports/RotoWire). Dobbins looks like the stronger side of Denver's committee right now while Coleman remains out.

ACTIVATED & LED BACKFIELD (10/25): activated off IR and immediately out-touched both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey in Denver's 30-16 win over Arizona -- 9 carries for 54 yards plus 2 catches for 15 yards, vs. 6 carries/23 yards+a TD for Dobbins and just 3 carries/6 yards for Harvey (Harvey's fantasy value came via a 52-yard TD catch on a screen pass, not a carry). Dobbins reportedly left the locker room frustrated afterward, telling reporters 'I'm unavailable' and declining interviews (Yahoo Sports, Athlon, PredominantlyOrange, 10/25) -- a real signal Coleman could be climbing the pecking order in a muddled three-way committee. Downgrading tag from Long-Term Injury to reflect the activation; keeping Breakout Watch and Depth Chart Battle given the unsettled backfield hierarchy.

CLEARED, Week 8 (10/27): carries no injury designation this week after Sunday's (10/25) activation and lead-role usage vs. Arizona -- officially ACTIVE with no setback reported. Denver's three-way RB committee (with J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey) remains unsettled; keeping Breakout Watch and Depth Chart Battle.

UPDATE (10/31-11/1): RJ Harvey has been placed on injured reserve (knee, minimum 4 games -- see his note), leaving Denver's backfield as a two-man Coleman/J.K. Dobbins arrangement rather than the muddled three-way committee of recent weeks. Reporting frames Coleman as the lead back in the new arrangement, with Dobbins as the secondary option and Cody Schrader elevated as depth. Keeping Breakout Watch and Depth Chart Battle given Dobbins is still in the mix.

No new setback reported; HC Kevin O'Connell may simply be managing his in-season reps coming off the bye rather than a real flare-up, and he could still upgrade off the report by Friday. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending final Friday designation -- treat as likely-to-play barring a Friday downgrade.

WEEK 7 RESULT (10/30): Minnesota beat Indianapolis 16-10 (10/25) -- Jefferson caught 4 of 7 targets for 44 yards, a quiet game by his standard but with no new injury concern reported (The Fantasy Footballers Week 7 recap). Minnesota's Week 8 opponent is a road trip to Detroit (Sun. 11/1).

HC Kellen Moore said no surgery is needed, but the recovery is expected to run at least 4 weeks — the team's Week 8 bye makes his next realistic game action Sunday, Nov. 8 at Cleveland (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, FantasyPros, 10/1). Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller are the direct backfield beneficiaries in the meantime; treat Etienne as a stash-only dynasty/IR piece for roughly a month.

WEEK 7 ACTUAL (10/22): 4 catches on 5 targets for 69 yards (no TD) in the 30-24 win over New England, including a key 3rd-and-9 conversion late, and also recovered Chicago's game-sealing onside kick. Passing offense is now fully built around a healthy Williams spreading the ball to Loveland/Odunze/Burden rather than running through a stopgap QB -- supersedes the stale Case Keenum-era note.

CONFIRMED: officially ruled OUT for Week 3 vs. Cincinnati after DNP all week, despite the issue being described as "day-to-day" (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/25-26).

NEW: still hasn't practiced — listed DNP again on Monday (9/28) — which is a real concern given Pittsburgh is on a short week for Thursday Night Football at Cleveland in Week 4. He'll need a near-miracle practice ramp-up to play Thursday and enters the week very much questionable (NBC Sports, 9/28). Jaylen Warren is set for another game of workhorse usage should Dowdle sit again.

Treat the QUESTIONABLE tag cautiously — it may reflect today's (Wed 9/30) official report showing him as at least limited, but the stronger prior signal through Tuesday still points toward sitting out. Carried a near-even Monday-night workload alongside Kyren Williams (combined 164 rush yards) in the win over the Giants — the split continues to run closer to 50/50 than a clean Williams-lead role (CBS Sports/RotoWire).

T.J. Hockenson.name: T.J. Hockenson
bullets: CORRECTION + WEEK 7 RESULT (10/30): the previous update's reference to a "home game vs. Philadelphia" was wrong -- Minnesota's actual Week 7 opponent was Indianapolis (16-10 home win, 10/25), not the Eagles. Hockenson caught 4 of 5 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in that win, with no setback reported (NBC Sports). Minnesota's Week 8 opponent is a road trip to Detroit (Sun. 11/1).

NEW -- WRIST/CHEST (11/11-13): picked up wrist and chest issues and did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (an estimated Wednesday report since Minnesota didn't hold a padded practice) ahead of Sunday's Week 10 game at Green Bay -- played 81% of the Week 9 snaps at Buffalo before this surfaced, so it's a new issue rather than an aggravation. No game-status designation attached yet as of Thursday; sources list it as TBD rather than a confirmed Questionable (Vikings.com, Star Tribune, Sharp Football Analysis, 11/11-12). Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending Friday's report.

Kyle Monangai.name: Kyle Monangai
bullets: Was fully healthy through Week 2 — the mid-August hyperextended knee and a hamstring tweak were non-issues, carrying no designation into Week 2's win over Minnesota as Chicago's clear RB2 behind Swift.

CLEARED: returned to a full practice Friday (9/25) after being limited Wed/Thu — reporting is split on the exact body part (SI/Yahoo say hamstring, NBC Sports said knee; the Bears never officially disclosed it), but he carries no designation into Monday night's game at Philadelphia (9/28) (Bleacher Nation, Heavy.com, 9/25).
Bigger Week 3 story for Chicago's offense is elsewhere: starting QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) is expected to sit Monday night, with Case Keenum tabbed to start — see Williams' note.

UPDATE: Chicago beat Philadelphia 27-7 on Monday Night Football in Week 3 (9/28) with Case Keenum starting at QB in place of the injured Caleb Williams (and Tyson Bagent, also unavailable) — Keenum threw for 247 yards and 2 TD. Monangai remains Chicago's clear RB2 behind D'Andre Swift in that game script.

HUGE WEEK 4 (10/4): ran for a reported 146 yards and 2 TDs as Chicago beat the Jets 23-12 with Tyson Bagent starting at QB (Chicago Sun-Times, Yahoo Sports) -- by far his best game of the season. Today's flip from Active to QUESTIONABLE has no confirmed new-injury report behind it as of 10/5; given his August hyperextended-knee history, treat this as a possible post-workload precaution rather than a confirmed new injury until a designation reason is reported. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch out of caution. Still operating in a committee with D'Andre Swift even when fully healthy.

CONFIRMED (10/5): the specific reason behind Friday's Active-to-Questionable flip is now known -- a right thumb injury suffered late in Sunday's 146-yard, 2-TD Week 4 explosion (30 carries, after taking over the bulk of the workload once D'Andre Swift fumbled and exited with knee soreness in the 3rd quarter), which led Chicago to sit him the final ~4 minutes. HC Ben Johnson called it "day-to-day," said imaging showed nothing concerning, and expects him fine for Sunday vs. Green Bay (NBC Sports, Chicago Sun-Times, 10/5). Not knee-related as initially speculated.

WORSENED/CONFIRMED (10/10): flipped from QUESTIONABLE to OUT for Sunday's Week 5 game at Green Bay. HC Ben Johnson had called the thumb injury "not an issue" and expected him to play, but a separate turf-toe issue -- reported mid-week as potentially a 1-2 week issue -- proved to be the bigger factor, and he did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. D'Andre Swift (now cleared, see his note) projects for a bigger workhorse workload Sunday in his absence; Roschon Johnson is next in line. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Short-Term Injury given the reported 1-2 week framing.

REVISED FROM SHORT-TERM TO STANDARD INJURY (10/14): the turf-toe timeline looks worse than last week's 1-2-week framing -- per Chicago Sun-Times reporting around 10/8-9, he was seen in a walking boot and saw a toe specialist, and HC Ben Johnson called it "a bigger deal than initially anticipated." No positive practice-return signal has surfaced since; downgrading tag back from Short-Term Injury to the standard Injury tier given the walked-back timeline, though the team has not put him on IR or attached a new firm number of weeks. D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's clear workhorse in the meantime; Bears play at Atlanta in Week 6 (Sun 10/18).

UPDATE (10/16): estimated as a DNP again Wednesday (10/14) with turf toe (which HC Ben Johnson has called "a bigger deal than we initially anticipated") plus a thumb injury, after already missing Week 5 -- trending toward a second straight missed game Sunday vs. Atlanta (10/18). Not expected to land on IR; D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's clear lead back in the meantime.

CONFIRMED (10/18): ruled out for Sunday's Week 6 game vs. Atlanta per the Chicago Sun-Times -- a second straight missed game with turf toe (plus a lingering thumb injury) after not practicing all week. HC Ben Johnson still calls it 'week-to-week' and said he's 'trending in the right direction,' while ESPN's Jeremy Fowler had floated a possible 1-2 week absence. D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's clear workhorse in the meantime, with Roschon Johnson next in line.

UPDATE (10/22): today's OUT-to-QUESTIONABLE flip matches the start of the new Week 7 practice-report cycle, but no independent beat reporting confirming improved practice participation for the turf toe/thumb issues was found as of this update -- HC Ben Johnson's "week-to-week"/"trending in the right direction" comments from last week remain the most recent confirmed word. Keeping the standard Injury tier rather than reading the flip as a confirmed recovery; D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's clear workhorse regardless.

CONFIRMED OUT, STILL WEEK-TO-WEEK (10/22-23): did not play in Thursday's 30-24 loss to New England -- his third straight missed game (Weeks 5-7) with the turf toe/thumb injuries suffered in Chicago's Week 4 win over the Jets. HC Ben Johnson has kept him off IR and continues to call him 'week-to-week'/'trending in the right direction' rather than giving a firm timeline; SI's Bears site, ProFootballNetwork and Heavy.com (10/21-22) float Week 8 vs. Seattle (11/2) as a plausible but unconfirmed target. Since he's not on IR and no outlet has reported a locked-in 4+ week absence, keeping the standard Injury tier rather than upgrading to Long-Term -- but three straight missed games is a real yellow flag. D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's unquestioned workhorse in the meantime.

NO REAL CHANGE (10/28): Still battling turf toe and a thumb injury -- was again a non-participant through Week 7 (Thursday Night Football vs. New England) practice week and was a "long shot" on short rest (Chicago Sun-Times, 10/19); lost that game 30-24, his third straight missed game. Reports conflict on whether Chicago will place him on IR or keep him week-to-week -- no transaction confirmed either way. Chicago is not on a bye and plays at Seattle on Monday Night Football in Week 8 (11/2), previously floated as a plausible target, but nothing new confirms he's trending toward that game specifically. D'Andre Swift remains the workhorse.

CONFIRMED OUT AGAIN, FOUR STRAIGHT MISSED GAMES (11/1-2): officially OUT for tonight's Week 8 Monday Night game at Seattle (11/2) with the turf toe/thumb injuries -- his fourth consecutive missed game (Weeks 5-8) dating back to Chicago's Week 4 win over the Jets, even though HC Ben Johnson has never placed him on IR and continues to call it 'week-to-week.' Since that stretch now runs roughly a month with no firm return target reported, upgrading the tag from the standard Injury tier to Long-Term Injury to reflect the real accumulated absence, even absent a formal IR move -- revising from the prior 'standard Injury, not yet Long-Term' read now that a fourth game has actually been missed. D'Andre Swift remains Chicago's unquestioned workhorse in the meantime.

STILL UNCONFIRMED FOR WEEK 9 (11/3-4): no official word yet on whether the turf toe/thumb combo clears in time for Sunday's game vs. Tampa Bay -- Chicago's roster feed shows a QUESTIONABLE tag for Week 9, but beat coverage (NBC Chicago, Newsweek) says it's still up in the air whether he suits up or the Bears hold him until after next week's bye. He has not played since Week 4 (four straight missed games), and HC Ben Johnson has reiterated there are no IR plans. Keeping the Long-Term Injury tier pending confirmation either way.

Caleb Williams.name: Caleb Williams
bullets: Had emerged as a fantasy-relevant weekly starter behind an improved Ben Johnson offense before the injury hit — real weekly upside as a rushing/passing dual threat.

CONFIRMED: officially ruled OUT for Week 3 vs. Philadelphia with a Grade 2 hamstring strain and did not play (0 fantasy points). Reporting pegs the expected absence at 3-4 weeks, which would also cost him Weeks 4-5 (NYJ, GB) with a Week 6 return vs. Atlanta as the earliest realistic target (SI/OnSI, Yahoo Sports, 9/27-29).

HC Ben Johnson has called him "week to week" without confirming the Week 4 questionable framing bettors are seeing — with no progress in practice participation this week, Williams should be considered questionable at best, and more likely a second-straight missed game. Keeping the Injury tag (not yet Long-Term) since the reported 3-4 week window sits just under the ~month/4-game long-term threshold, but this bears watching if it slips further.

UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to DOUBTFUL for Week 4 vs. the Jets, but this looks like a procedural downgrade rather than a sign he's rounding into game shape — the operative 3-4 week / Week 6-at-Atlanta timeline from last week's reporting has NOT been revised as of the Wednesday practice cycle (Yahoo Sports, BearGoggleson.com, ProFootballNetwork). HC Ben Johnson continues to call him "week-to-week" without confirming a Week 4 questionable framing. Treat him as unlikely to play Sunday; Case Keenum (not Tyson Bagent, who is also out) remains Chicago's starter after authoring a 247-yard, 2-TD upset of Philadelphia (27-7) on Week 3 Monday Night Football, including an 8-yard TD to Luther Burden III plus a rushing score.

CONFIRMED (10/2-3): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 4 home game vs. the Jets, missing a second straight game with the Grade 2 hamstring strain -- the original 3-4 week / Week 6-at-Atlanta timeline from two weeks ago has NOT been revised. Case Keenum remains Chicago's starter (SI/Betting, PrizePicks, 10/1-3).

CORRECTION + UPDATE (10/5): Chicago's Week 4 starter was Tyson Bagent, not Case Keenum as referenced in last week's note -- Bagent threw for a career-high 268 yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets (Chicago Sun-Times, Yahoo Sports, 10/4), with Kyle Monangai running for 146 yards and 2 TDs behind him (see Monangai's note). Williams (hamstring) missed a second straight game and remains "week to week" per HC Ben Johnson with no firm return date announced as of 10/5; Chicago is in no rush given Bagent's play. The original 3-4 week / Week 6-at-Atlanta timeline has still not been formally revised.

FLAGGING A DISCREPANCY (10/10): ESPN's roster status flipped from OUT to QUESTIONABLE ahead of Sunday's Week 5 game at Green Bay, but this does NOT appear to reflect a real return -- all beat reporting through Thursday (10/8) continued to describe Williams as not practicing and "week-to-week" with the Grade 2 hamstring strain, with Tyson Bagent set to start a third straight game and the Week 6-vs.-Atlanta target still the operative return expectation (RotoBaller, Athletic/Wiederer via RotoBaller, 10/5-8). Treating the QUESTIONABLE tag as a likely data/procedural artifact rather than confirmation he's playing Sunday -- recheck the Bears' actual Friday practice report before trusting it. Keeping the standard Injury tier.

CONFIRMED (10/12): missed a fourth straight game, inactive for Sunday's Week 5 loss at Green Bay (Packers won 31-7). Tyson Bagent started again and struggled (12-of-21, 87 yards, 0 TD, 2 INT, 27.4 rating, 2 sacks) before being benched in the 4th quarter for Case Keenum (11-of-19, 108 yards, 1 INT). No new return timeline reported; Week 6 vs. Atlanta remains the target, keeping the standard Injury tier.

UPDATE (10/13): real progress -- returned to a limited practice Friday (10/9) after resuming throwing drills, and The Athletic's Dan Wiederer reports Chicago never placed him on IR, keeping Week 6 vs. Atlanta (10/18) live as his target. He's still building back to full-speed running, and HC Ben Johnson is calling his return "to be determined"/benchmark-based rather than confirming he plays -- Rapoport/Pelissero flagged Week 6 or the following week (10/22 vs. NE) as the likely activation window, with no hard date set (NBC Sports, Bleacher Nation, 10/9-10).

UPDATE (10/14): trending toward a Week 6 return vs. Atlanta (Sun 10/18) but still unconfirmed by the team itself -- Ian Rapoport reported (10/12) "all signs point" to Williams playing, citing a completed strenuous pregame workout and his first limited practice since the injury (Fri 10/9). HC Ben Johnson has NOT guaranteed it, saying only that Williams would be "close." The Chicago Sun-Times (10/11) floated the team instead targeting the following week (Oct 22 vs. New England) given the short Thu turnaround after a Sunday game, calling the decision "to be determined." Keeping the standard Injury tier until an actual designation/practice grade confirms he's playing.

UPGRADE (10/14): took a full practice Wednesday, per HC Ben Johnson (Yahoo Sports/SI, BleacherNation) -- a real step up from last week's limited/estimated sessions. Johnson still won't commit to naming him the starter until closer to Sunday's game at Atlanta, but a full practice week is a strong signal he plays. Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Health Watch given the clean practice participation.

UPDATE (10/16): a full practice participant Wednesday (10/14) after missing three straight games with a Grade 2 hamstring strain -- NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports "all signs point" to Williams returning Sunday vs. Atlanta (10/18), and the Bears have moved to roughly 3-point favorites, suggesting the market expects him back. HC Ben Johnson hasn't confirmed the start, calling it "still fluid."

RETURNED AND DOMINANT (10/18): made his return from the 3-game hamstring absence in Sunday's 31-23 win at Atlanta with zero lingering effects -- went 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a TD to Colston Loveland, including a 12-of-12 start before his first incompletion. Chicago held off a 24-point Atlanta rally attempt to improve to 4-2; D'Andre Swift ran for 2 TDs (see his note). Williams said afterward his body felt great but that managing it will be "a weekly thing" (ESPN, CBS Chicago, Yahoo Sports, 10/18). Downgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Healthy given the clean, full-workload return; Chicago is back in action Thursday vs. New England on a short week, worth checking his practice reps given the quick turnaround.

WEEK 7 ACTUAL (10/22): backed up his return with another strong outing in the 30-24 TNF win over New England -- 22-of-33 for 308 yards and 2 TD (incl. a 12-yard TD to Colston Loveland), zero interceptions, no hamstring setback through back-to-back full workloads. Also hit Rome Odunze on a key 3rd-and-9 conversion late that set up Odunze's own game-sealing onside-kick recovery (Boston Globe, Bleacher Nation, NFL.com, 10/22-23).

Isaiah Likely.name: Isaiah Likely
bullets: Signed for 3yr/$40M+, now the clear TE1 ahead of Theo Johnson, reunited with HC John Harbaugh — real path to a top-10 fantasy TE role after sharing looks with Mark Andrews in Baltimore.

NEW (10/8): limited at Wednesday's practice with a knee/groin issue and carries a QUESTIONABLE tag into Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington (Giants' official injury report, 10/7) -- first injury concern since signing. No severity or timeline reported yet; check Friday's final designation.

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday night's Week 5 game vs. Atlanta -- no setback from the knee/groin issue that limited him in practice this week. First clean bill of health since signing with Baltimore.

Cam Little.name: Cam Little
bullets: Jacksonville's starting kicker, known for elite leg strength on long attempts — no competition for the job.

Romeo Doubs.name: Romeo Doubs
bullets: Signed in free agency; profiles as a high-volume slot piece similar to Diggs' old role now that Diggs is gone.

PLACED ON IR (10/19-20): dove for a 42-yard go-ahead TD catch from Drake Maye in the 1st quarter of Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets and landed hard on his shoulder, first questionable to return before being ruled out; the Patriots officially placed him on injured reserve Monday (10/19), which rules him out a minimum of four games under NFL IR rules (ESPN, NBC Sports, Boston.com, Heavy.com, 10/19). No surgery has been announced and a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler the injury isn't expected to keep him out long-term -- he's hopeful to return around New England's bye in late November, with one outlet pegging Week 12 vs. the Chargers as an earliest-return target. Upgrading tag from Breakout Watch to Long-Term Injury per the official IR designation (our fixed tiering rule treats any IR stint as Long-Term regardless of the softer verbal outlook); Mack Hollins and DeMario Douglas are set to see expanded roles in New England's receiver room in the meantime.

Nico Collins.name: Nico Collins
bullets: Still a fantasy WR1 when healthy (ESPN ranks him WR10) — three straight 1,000-yard seasons, 21 TDs over that stretch — but the Grade 1 hamstring strain has now cost him back-to-back games.
CONFIRMED: officially ruled OUT for Week 3 vs. the Colts (Sunday) — his second straight missed game with the same hamstring strain (NBC Sports, Last Word on Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/25-26).

NEW: HC DeMeco Ryans said he's "hopeful" Collins is available for Week 4 vs. Dallas, and Adam Schefter reports a "decent chance" he returns, but Collins did not practice Monday and will need to show up as at least a limited participant Wednesday-Friday to have a realistic shot at playing (ESPN/Schefter, CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 9/27-29). Keeping Injury tag until he's actually back on the practice field; Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Jaylin Noel remain Houston's top three WRs in his absence.

UPDATE (9/30): Tracker flips OUT to QUESTIONABLE for Week 4 vs. Dallas. HC DeMeco Ryans said Monday (9/28) he's "hopeful"/there's a "decent chance" Collins plays, calling his rehab progress "really good" (CBS Sports, NBC Sports). The QUESTIONABLE tag implies he returned to practice in at least a limited fashion this week for the first time since the injury — a real, meaningful step, but he'll still need Thu/Fri practice participation to be considered a lock. One aggregator flagged a separate "knee (limited)" note that isn't corroborated elsewhere and should be treated with caution rather than as a new injury. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte continue to lead Houston's WR snaps/targets in his absence.

CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/2-3): officially active for Monday Night Football's Week 4 game at Dallas, ending his absence with the hamstring strain -- he told ESPN Friday "Hell yeah, I'm playing this week" and was not listed on Houston's final injury report. Downgrading tag from Injury to Healthy; this snaps him back in as Houston's clear WR1 over Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte.

Week 4 final (10/4): played in his return from the hamstring strain and caught 4 of his targets for 54 yards as Houston routed Dallas 34-10 (CBS Sports). Modest workload in the first game back -- no new injury reported, worth tracking snap/target share growth as he ramps back toward full volume in Week 5.

VOLUME WATCH (10/28): Managed just 2 catches on 5 targets for 6 yards in Houston's 27-21 OT loss to the Giants (10/25) as C.J. Stroud spread the ball to 9 different targets, including Marvin Harrison Jr., who continues to carve into Houston's target share since the October trade. Houston is on its Week 8 bye; adding Volume Regression Watch tag given the target-diffusion trend.

Cam Skattebo.name: Cam Skattebo
bullets: Fully cleared from last year's gruesome rookie ankle injury (dislocation + open fracture) and confirmed as the Giants' Week 1 starting RB over Tyrone Tracy Jr., hosting Dallas on Sunday Night Football.

Held to just 12 carries for 36 yards, 4 catches for 19 yards, and a lost fumble in Monday night's 28-6 loss at the Rams — the whole Giants game plan was wrecked after QB Jaxson Dart left with a knee injury on the first series (182 total team yards); treat the poor box score as game-script-driven, not a role change (RotoWire, CBS Sports).

NEW (10/8): limited at Wednesday's practice with a shoulder issue, officially QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington (Giants' injury report, 10/7) -- distinct from last year's season-ending ankle fracture/dislocation. No word yet on severity or workload impact pending Friday's report.

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Washington -- cleared the shoulder issue that limited him in back-to-back Wednesday/Thursday practices after opening the week in a non-contact jersey. On track for his usual workhorse workload (bolavip, NBC Sports Fantasy, 10/7-9).

Week 5 final (10/11): played through the shoulder issue with no setback -- 13 carries for 59 yards plus 2 catches for 12 yards (40 of his 71 scrimmage yards came in overtime) in a 27-27 tie at Washington. Costly moment: fumbled at the Washington 24-yard line late in OT with the Giants in range for a potential game-winning field goal. No injury fallout reported from the game; remains the clear starter.

ZERO-TOUCH SCARE (10/26): got no carries or targets on just 6 offensive snaps in Week 6's loss to New Orleans, but HC Brian Daboll (via beat reporting) denied it was a benching, saying "when he was in there, we didn't call any runs" -- a play-calling/game-script explanation, not a demotion. The Giants also released veteran RB Najee Harris and turned to J.J. McCarthy at QB (relieving an inefficient Jameis Winston) for Week 7 vs. Houston, both of which point toward Skattebo keeping the clear lead role rather than losing it (RotoBaller, 10/24-26). Keeping Depth Chart Secured and Healthy.

NEW (10/25-27): felt something in his hamstring on a career-long 42-yard run in overtime of the Giants' Week 7 win over Houston -- the carry that set up the game-winning score. No diagnosis or recovery timetable announced as of Monday (10/26), but NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported "all indications this morning are he should be OK, especially with the team on a bye this weekend." New York is on its Week 8 bye, so there's no game-day decision this week; next real checkpoint is Wednesday's Week 9 practice report. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch; keeping Depth Chart Secured.

UPDATE (11/2): the hamstring tweak from the Week 7 OT win over Houston is still "day-to-day" per Giants HC John Harbaugh (correcting prior notes that misattributed Giants HC comments to Brian Daboll, who was fired back in November 2025 -- Harbaugh took over this past offseason) ahead of Sunday's Week 9 game at Philadelphia. Our roster feed has him Questionable. Devin Singletary (newly added to this roster) is the direct backup if Skattebo sits. Keeping Health Watch; Depth Chart Secured stands as the starter when healthy.

ESCALATES TO DOUBTFUL (11/4-8): missed practice Wednesday and Thursday, was limited Friday, and Giants.com's own headline read "Cam Skattebo doubtful vs. Philadelphia Eagles in Week 9" -- he also skipped his usual Friday media session, which beat writers read as a signal he likely won't play today vs. the Eagles (Giants.com, SI.com/OnSI, Yahoo Sports, 11/6). No specific new diagnosis beyond the hamstring tweak suffered on the Week 7 OT win over Houston. Devin Singletary is the direct next-man-up if Skattebo sits (see his note). Upgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the real doubt; keeping Depth Chart Secured for when he's healthy.

OFFICIALLY OUT, CONFIRMED (11/10): the DOUBTFUL tag resolved to OUT for Sunday's Week 9 game at Philadelphia (11/8) -- the hamstring injury from the Week 7 OT touchdown-setup run (10/25) held him out, with conflicting reports beforehand (NFL Network's Rapoport skeptical, Giants HC John Harbaugh more optimistic) landing on the side of caution. Devin Singletary was the primary back in his place. Keeping standard Injury tier pending a clearer multi-week timeline.

OFFICIALLY INACTIVE FOR WEEK 9 (11/8-10): downgraded from Doubtful to OUT and did not play Sunday's game at Philadelphia with the Week 7 hamstring tweak -- Devin Singletary handled the bulk of the Giants' backfield touches in his absence. Adam Schefter reported pre-game that Skattebo is 'pushing to play' and should be good to go for Week 10, pointing to a short, roughly one-week absence. Moving from the standard Injury tier to Short-Term Injury to reflect the confirmed missed game with a firm near-term return target; keeping Depth Chart Secured for when he's back.

TRENDING STRONGLY TO PLAY, THURSDAY DEADLINE (11/11): the Giants play Washington on Thursday Night Football in Week 10, so a decision is imminent. HC confirmed Monday he's optimistic Skattebo will be a 'full go,' and Skattebo was seen participating in Tuesday's most demanding practice session of the week -- both signals point toward playing (team reporting, 11/10-11). Keeping Short-Term Injury -- this is exactly the roughly one-week return that tag projected after the Week 9 miss.

DATA/REALITY CONFLICT -- ACTUALLY TRENDING TO PLAY (11/12): our roster feed flipped him from QUESTIONABLE to OUT heading into tonight's Week 10 Thursday Night Football game vs. Washington, but that contradicts the real reporting -- ESPN's Adam Schefter reported (11/11) that Skattebo (hamstring) has NO injury designation and is good to go, HC John Harbaugh said he 'should be a full go,' and the Giants' own Week 10 report had him practicing in full Tue/Wed after an opening Monday limited session. Treating the roster feed's OUT as a likely data lag rather than real news given the weight and recency of the reporting; keeping Short-Term Injury since the underlying Week 7 hamstring tweak that cost him Week 9 is the same short-absence injury already tracked. Recheck tomorrow's actual box score/inactives list to resolve the discrepancy.

RESOLVED -- ROSTER FEED WAS WRONG, HE PLAYED (11/12-13): the real reporting from yesterday's note was correct -- Skattebo played Thursday night (no final game-status designation, as Schefter had reported) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to Washington, scoring two rushing touchdowns in the first half as New York led 14-10 before the Commanders rallied behind a late Jayden Daniels TD pass to Stefon Diggs. No setback to the Week 7 hamstring tweak reported; he played his normal workload. Upgrading tag from Short-Term Injury to Healthy now that he's confirmed through a full game with no issue, and the earlier roster-feed OUT flip is confirmed as the data lag it was flagged as being.

D'Andre Swift.name: D'Andre Swift
bullets: Chicago's clear RB1 in Ben Johnson's scheme.

The Sept 3 practice scare was cramping, not a leg injury, and it showed no lingering effect — torched Carolina for 18 carries, 124 yards and 3 TDs (plus a catch) in Sunday's 59-37 win, arguably his best game as a Bear.

The Week 2 knee/ankle concern is resolved — logged a full practice Friday (9/18) and was removed from Chicago's injury report entirely, carrying no designation into Sunday's game at Minnesota (NBC Sports, RotoWire, CBS Sports, 9/18).

NEW (10/1-2): popped up on Chicago's Week 4 injury report as a non-participant Thursday with a knee injury — a new issue, not a recurrence of the earlier cramping/knee-ankle scares. He was off the Wednesday walkthrough report and had just carried 20 times for 84 yards in Chicago's prior game, so beat writers flagged the sudden Thursday DNP as worth watching; no designation confirmed yet pending Friday's report, with hope he's a full go Sunday vs. the Jets (Chicago Sun-Times, Bleacher Nation, 10/1-2).

CLEARED (10/3): the Thursday DNP knee scare did not linger -- Swift practiced fully later in the week and carries no designation into Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Jets, remaining Chicago's unquestioned RB1. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

NEW (10/4): fumbled in the 3rd quarter of Chicago's 23-12 Week 4 win over the Jets and did not return, finishing with 15 carries for 58 yards and 2 catches for 16 yards; was seen limping postgame with soreness in the same knee that had been a minor pregame concern. HC Ben Johnson did not frame it as a benching. Kyle Monangai (see his note) took over and torched the Jets for 146 yards/2 TD on 30 carries in relief. No official injury designation or severity reported yet as of 10/5-6 -- downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending clarity; Chicago's Week 5 backfield split is worth watching since both backs picked up bumps in the same game (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, Bleacher Nation, Heavy.com, 10/4).

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game at Green Bay -- the hip/knee issue that kept him out of Wednesday's practice resolved by Friday. Remains Chicago's lead back; downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

WEEK 6 + WEEK 7 ACTUAL (10/18, 10/22): stayed Chicago's clear lead back through both games. Week 6 at Atlanta (31-23 win, 10/18): 16 carries for 44 yards (2.8 YPC) and 4-of-5 targets for 26 yards -- backup Roschon Johnson actually out-gained him on the ground that day (13 car/51 yds/TD). Week 7 TNF vs. New England (30-24 win, 10/22): bounced back as a true workhorse, 86% of offensive snaps -- 22 carries for 78 yards and Chicago's first TD of the game (4-yard run), per Rotowire's usage breakdown and CBS Sports. Monangai still out; no threat to Swift's role.

Mike Evans.name: Mike Evans
bullets: Monday (9/21) update: Shanahan said the hip "will have to be managed this week" and Evans would likely miss some practice time. Turns 33 in August — an aging watch item independent of any single-week injury.

UPDATE: exited Week 3's loss to Arizona early in the 2nd quarter with a rib injury after a hard hit from S Budda Baker on a middle-of-the-field catch — was carted off and did not return, finishing with 3 catches for 34 yards and a TD before leaving (ESPN, CBS Sports, Yahoo Sports, 9/27-28).

Downgrading tag from Aging-Watch-only injury risk to Health Watch: Evans returned to practice Friday and is officially Questionable for Week 4 vs. Denver, with HC Kyle Shanahan indicating optimism that he'll play (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Last Word on Sports, 9/26-29). Treat as a game-time-decision-caliber Questionable, not a real absence risk at this point.

CLEARED (10/5): the rib strain suffered vs. Arizona in Week 3 is behind him -- today's status flip from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE confirms he's cleared the issue that had him day-to-day. Pleaded no contest Sept 10 in Brown County to the misdemeanor battery charge (found guilty, $1,000 fine + costs) with a 12-month deferred-judgment agreement on the property-damage charge. As of 9/26, the NFL STILL has not announced an official suspension length — reporting indicates the league is navigating legal barriers (a court-ordered bar on releasing video evidence) before finalizing discipline, with the standard 6-game domestic-violence-related baseline still the working estimate (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, ProFootballRumors, 9/24-26).

Green Bay has already hedged, trading a 2028 6th-round pick to Pittsburgh for RB Kaleb Johnson as depth-chart insurance — a real sign the team isn't banking on a quick Jacobs return. Treat him as unplayable/bench for now.

The video-evidence dispute delaying the league's review is still unresolved -- a judge recently declined to permanently seal the incident video on procedural grounds (NBC Sports/PFT, ~10/1-2) -- and Jacobs' next court hearing isn't until Nov. 17, well past several more game weeks. Any time already spent on the Exempt List would count toward an eventual suspension. Green Bay's Kaleb Johnson depth-chart plan is unchanged; still unplayable/bench.

Still unplayable/bench.

Green Bay's backfield without him: MarShawn Lloyd leads with 40 carries/112 yards/2 TD this season, with Kaleb Johnson (27/106) and Chris Brooks also involved -- Green Bay's run game ranks last in the NFL in his absence.

Still unplayable/bench; MarShawn Lloyd remains Green Bay's lead back for Sunday Night Football vs. Dallas (10/18).
