Steelers' WR room is thin behind him (Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek both out), so Germie Bernard would see a bigger role if Metcalf can't go Sunday vs. Tampa Bay. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch given the swift, late-week designation; illness-driven Questionable tags often clear on gameday, so recheck the final inactive list.

CLEARED AND CONFIRMED (10/18): removed from Pittsburgh's injury report Saturday, ending the late-week illness scare, then delivered a big game in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over Tampa Bay -- 11 catches for 93 yards, tied with Germie Bernard (also 11 catches) for Pittsburgh's team high in receptions (Yahoo Sports, Behind the Steel Curtain, 10/18-19). Teammate Pat Freiermuth (calf) also carried a late QUESTIONABLE tag into the same game -- see his note. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean, productive game.

Brock Purdy.name: Brock Purdy
bullets: Signed a massive 5-yr/$265M extension; finished as a QB1-range fantasy scorer in every full season as a starter, behind a receiving corps upgraded with Mike Evans and Christian Kirk.

Woody Marks.name: Woody Marks
bullets: Was Houston's clear passing-down/receiving-work back behind David Montgomery through the first several weeks, holding real standalone value even in a committee.

NEW (10/13): took over as Houston's lead back after David Montgomery exited Sunday's Week 5 win over Tennessee (26-3) with a groin injury -- finished with a season-high 15 carries for 62 yards plus 4 catches, reportedly logging roughly 85% of the Texans' backfield snaps once Montgomery left (FantasyPros, Athlon Sports, SI/OnSI, 10/12). With Montgomery now DOUBTFUL/week-to-week (see his note), Marks projects as Houston's clear lead back for as long as that lasts.

UPDATE (10/13): confirmed to keep the expanded lead-back role for Week 6 in Montgomery's continued absence, replicating his Week 5 workload (15 carries/62 yards, 4 catches) -- per FantasyFootballers and CBS Sports (~10/13). Jawhar Jordan and practice-squad RB Deuce Vaughn are the depth pieces behind him if needed.

NEW -- KNEE (11/11-13): picked up a knee injury this week, limited at Wednesday's Texans practice ahead of Sunday's Week 10 road game at Cleveland; one outlet (Battle Red Blog) has him as a Thursday non-participant instead, so the trend is unclear -- worth confirming Friday's report. Still Houston's clear lead-role back when healthy alongside David Montgomery's continued absence (see his note). Adding Health Watch given the real uncertainty.

Tony Pollard.name: Tony Pollard
bullets: Entrenched starter chasing a 5th straight 1,000-yard season — hit 1,000 rushing yards in each of the past 4 years.
CLEARED: returned to a full practice Friday (9/25) and is off the final Week 3 injury report entirely — no designation for Sunday vs. the Giants (RotoWire, FantasyPros, NBC Sports, 9/25).

Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (ankle) remains Questionable — if Spears is limited or sits, Pollard is positioned for an even bigger workload bump on top of his already-larger carry share (53.4% snap share to Spears' 42.7% through two weeks, with roughly double Spears' carries).

NEW (9/30): a new foot injury (distinct from the ankle issue referenced earlier) — Pollard was a non-participant in Wednesday's Week 4 practice. HC Mike Vrabel's staff said they are "not overly concerned about Sunday" for Pollard and don't believe it will affect his Week 4 availability vs. Baltimore; backfield mate Tyjae Spears also sat out Wednesday with an ankle issue (CBS Sports, NBC Sports/PFT, Newsweek, 9/30).

CLEARED (10/1-2): the foot issue that held him out of Wednesday's practice did not linger — Pollard returned to a full practice Thursday and carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 4 game vs. Baltimore. Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (ankle) remains limited/Questionable, keeping Pollard's bell-cow workload intact (Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 10/1-2).

Week 4 final (10/4): the foot issue was a non-factor -- went for 16 carries, 48 yards and a 3-yard rushing TD plus 2 catches for 2 yards in a 24-18 loss to Baltimore that dropped Tennessee to 0-4. Backfield mate Tyjae Spears was marginal (2 carries, 7 yards), confirming Pollard as the clear lead back even in a lost season. Worth watching: with Tennessee winless, ESPN's Adam Schefter floated Pollard as a potential trade-deadline candidate -- no deal reported yet, just speculation (NBC Sports, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports, 10/4).

NEW (10/8): did not practice Wednesday with a foot injury and is QUESTIONABLE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Houston; beat coverage describes it as a possible maintenance/veteran rest day rather than a new injury, consistent with how Tennessee has handled him in past weeks (10/7).

CLEARED (10/8): back to a full practice participant Thursday after sitting out Wednesday with the foot issue -- on track to play Sunday's Week 5 home game vs. Houston, continuing the pattern of maintenance-related absences that haven't cost him game time all season (Yahoo Sports/Titans beat, 10/8).

Week 5 final (10/13): the foot was a non-issue and he played the full workload, but the game itself was ugly -- Houston routed Tennessee 26-3 (ESPN gameId 401872984, Titans.com, PFF), dropping the Titans to 0-5 (not 0-4 as noted last week; the winless streak continued, it did not end). Pollard carried 14 times for 52 yards with no catches or TDs reported (Yahoo Sports, RotoWire, FantasyPros). No new injury flagged out of the game; still Tennessee's clear lead back on a team now shopping for answers at 0-5.

BIG GAME (10/29): erupted for an estimated ~129 rushing yards on a season-high ~25 carries and accounted for all 3 Tennessee touchdowns in a 27-24 loss to Cleveland in Week 7 (10/25) -- named a Week 7 fantasy MVP by at least one outlet with 36.5 total fantasy points, the league's top score for the week (Wolfsports, Fantasy Football Calculator). Backfield mate Tyjae Spears (knee) was inactive, clearing the way for a near-every-down workload. No new injury flagged; the earlier-season foot/maintenance issues have not recurred in weeks. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy given the clean recent run.

NEW QUESTIONABLE FLIP (11/13-14): picked up a fresh QUESTIONABLE designation for Sunday's Week 10 home game vs. Jacksonville. No specific new injury type or practice-participation detail could be independently confirmed via search as of this update -- Tennessee's Week 10 injury coverage found several other starters (Anthony Hill Jr., Cody Barton, Peter Skoronski) and backfield mate Tyjae Spears tagged Questionable, but no corroborating Pollard-specific report. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch out of caution pending Friday's final word; recheck before treating this as a real absence risk.

Chuba Hubbard.name: Chuba Hubbard
bullets: The camp hamstring issue was fully behind him for the opener — played through it and led Carolina's backfield in the Week 1 loss to Chicago: 10 carries for 49 yards and a rush TD plus 3 catches for 38 yards and a receiving TD (23.7 fantasy pts).

NEW: with Jonathon Brooks now on injured reserve (core-muscle surgery, minimum 6 weeks) as of 9/23, the earlier 1A/1B timeshare is over — Hubbard is Carolina's undisputed lead back, with AJ Dillon next man up in a diminished RB2/short-yardage role.

Parker Washington.name: Parker Washington
bullets: Stepped up in practice reps amid Thomas/Meyers injuries in one of the league's deepest WR rooms, alongside Travis Hunter.

Christian McCaffrey.name: Christian McCaffrey
bullets: Full workhorse usage in the opener with no ill effects from the calf scare: 10 carries for 68 yards plus 5 catches for 20 yards in the win over the Rams.
Held out of the end zone, but the touch volume is exactly what you want to see after last year's injury history.

HC Kyle Shanahan confirmed this week the Week 1 split with rookie Kaelon Black (who out-carried him 14-10, 44% of snaps) was a deliberate plan to lighten McCaffrey's load: "That was the goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more... love taking some off Christian." Total touches were even (15-15), but expect Black to keep chipping into the carry share.

NEW (10/28): McCaffrey left Sunday's Week 7 loss at Atlanta (10/25) with a hip/thigh injury (reports differ on the exact body part) in the 2nd quarter, briefly replaced by rookie Kaelon Black, but returned and finished the game. No Shanahan severity comment found, and SF is on its Week 8 bye so there's no practice report to clarify further until Week 9 prep. Downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch out of caution; not treating this as a significant injury based on current information since he played through it the same day.

CORRECTION + CLEARED (11/6-8): the Week 7 injury (10/25) that briefly pulled him from that game is a mild/Grade-1 hamstring strain, not a hip injury as an earlier note stated -- Kyle Shanahan explicitly described it as a hamstring strain after McCaffrey returned to finish that game with 7 carries/39 yards/TD plus 6 catches/61 yards. SF was "pretty optimistic" it wouldn't cost him time and targeted a return after the Week 8 bye; he was present for Thursday's practice this week and carries no designation for today's Week 9 home game vs. the Raiders. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; keeping Depth Chart Battle given rookie Kaelon Black's continued share of early-down work.

POST-GAME CONFIRMATION (11/8-10): played Sunday's Week 9 home game vs. Las Vegas after being cleared on the mild/Grade-1 hamstring strain -- no setback reported. Stat line not independently confirmable via search as of this update. Remains Healthy.

Texans D/ST.name: Texans D/ST
bullets: Top-5 fantasy unit two years running under HC DeMeco Ryans, ranked 2nd for 2026 behind only Seattle — led the NFL in fantasy points per game (56.4) last season. Opens with tougher matchups (BUF, then CIN).

Jaxon Smith-Njigba.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
bullets: Opened 2026 with 8 catches for 122 yds and the game-winning 45-yard TD (41 YAC) on 4th-and-1 in the 4th quarter of Seattle's 13-10 Sept 9 Kickoff Game win over New England — early sign the regression fears may be overblown.

Backup QB Drew Lock (18/22, 187 yds) finished that game after starter Sam Darnold left with a hip injury on the opening drive; Darnold's Thursday (Sept 10) MRI showed no major structural damage ("dodged a bullet," per the team), but he's still expected to miss Week 2 at Arizona with Lock confirmed as the Week 2 starter — worth tracking since it affects who's throwing Smith-Njigba the ball.
Led all NFL WRs with 1,793 yds/10 TD in 2025 and won Offensive Player of the Year; now the highest-paid WR in history (4yr/$168.6M).
Top-5 overall fantasy asset — the question is regression off a historic year, not upside.

NEW (10/14): picked up a minor ankle injury on a 16-yard lateral run in the second quarter of Seattle's 32-29 Week 5 loss at San Francisco (10/11) -- it didn't meaningfully slow him down; he still topped 100 receiving yards for the 5th straight game, pushing his NFL-leading total to 583 yards and 7 TDs through 5 games. The Seattle Times' Bob Condotta reported he was a limited practice participant Monday (10/12) ahead of a short week (Seahawks play Thursday 10/15 at Denver), with reporting suggesting he should play Thursday without real restriction. Tagging Health Watch given the minor/day-to-day framing -- not a real absence risk at this point.

UPDATE (10/15): no official designation beyond Monday's (10/12) limited-practice estimate has surfaced ahead of tonight's Thursday Night Football game at Denver -- RotoBaller's analysis expects him to play without real restriction on the short week, but that's analyst opinion, not a confirmed team designation. Check Seattle's pregame inactive list for final confirmation.

RESOLVED (10/16): the minor ankle tweak was a non-issue -- played every snap of Thursday night's 17-14 OT loss at Denver (10/15) with no in-game setback, posting 12 catches on 16 targets for 134 yards (season now 49 catches, 717 yards, 7 TD through 6 games). Upgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy; today's ACTIVE flip reflects a clean bill of health, not a new designation.

BIG GAME (10/29): caught 9 of 12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's 20-3 win over Kansas City in Week 7 (SNF, 10/25), good for 30.0 PPR fantasy points and an Air & Ground Player of the Week nomination -- his second huge game in as many weeks (134 yards in Week 6). The minor ankle tweak from two weeks ago has not resurfaced. Two straight monster weeks are making the preseason regression chatter look overblown; remains Healthy.

Jeremiyah Love.name: Jeremiyah Love
bullets: Played through the high-ankle sprain that had him Questionable and delivered his first extended workload: 11 carries for 41 yards and a TD plus 2 catches for 9 yards in Sunday's game vs. the Chargers.
No setback reported after the game — the ankle no longer looks like a Week 2 concern with a full game under his belt.

NEW (10/5-6): tweaked his OTHER ankle (not the preseason high-ankle sprain) late in Sunday's Week 4 loss at the Giants, finishing with 14 carries for 63 yards plus a target that went for -8 yards. HC Mike LaFleur described it Monday as "a management-type thing... he tweaks it and then he feels fine," and Love himself called this shaping up as the "longest year" of his career (NBC Sports, RotoBaller, Heavy.com, SI.com, 10/4-5). No practice report yet as of today (Week 5 practice starts Wednesday); downgrading tag from Healthy to Health Watch pending Wednesday's designation.

CLEARED (10/10): upgraded from QUESTIONABLE to ACTIVE for Sunday's Week 5 game vs. Detroit -- HC Mike LaFleur had already downplayed the tweaked ankle as a "management-type thing," and that held up with no setback reported heading into Friday. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to Healthy.

NEW, SEPARATE INJURY (10/16): dealing with a different left-ankle issue (not the preseason high-ankle sprain or the earlier "management-type" tweak) -- did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (10/14-10/15). HC Mike LaFleur's language shifted more cautious, saying the staff wants to "get this ankle right and do it the right way," which beat writers (Arizona Sports, Yahoo Sports) read as a real threat to his Sunday availability vs. the Rams (10/18) even though Love reportedly wants to play through it. Tyler Allgeier would start if he sits. Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier given the genuine uncertainty.

CONFIRMED (10/18): officially ruled OUT for Sunday's Week 6 home game vs. the Rams -- HC Jonathan Gannon's staff (via AP) confirmed the lingering left ankle injury (aggravated in Week 4 at the Giants) kept him out of practice all week. No IR conversations have taken place per the team, so this reads as a short-term absence rather than a long one. Tyler Allgeier (newly added to this roster, see his note) and Bam Knight are set to handle Arizona's backfield work Sunday. Keeping the standard Injury tier given the no-IR signal, though recheck next week for an actual return target.

UPDATE (10/22): did not practice Wednesday (10/21) with the ankle injury -- HC Mike LaFleur said rest is "vital" for him right now, and NBC Sports frames the DNP as putting him "on the wrong side of questionable" for Sunday's Week 7 game vs. Denver. He has a chance to return to practice Thursday/Friday; if he sits, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would again handle Arizona's backfield work. Keeping the standard Injury tier pending the rest of the week's reports.

CONFIRMED OUT (10/25): ruled out for today's Week 7 home game vs. Denver -- the left ankle injury kept him out of practice all week again, continuing last week's 'wrong side of questionable' trend that HC Mike LaFleur flagged. No IR conversations have been reported. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight again handle Arizona's backfield work. Keeping the standard Injury tier.

NO REAL CHANGE (10/28): No beat-writer report found yet on his practice status for Arizona's Week 8 game at Dallas (11/1) -- today's QUESTIONABLE flip looks like the weekly placeholder reset. Last confirmed news unchanged: lingering left ankle injury, OUT for Week 7 vs. Denver (10/25), no IR move, no firm return timeline from HC Mike LaFleur. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight remain the backfield answer in the meantime.

CLEARED (10/30-31): HC Mike LaFleur confirmed Love will play Sunday at Dallas, ending a two-game absence (Weeks 6-7) with the lingering left ankle injury -- a clean practice progression (limited Wednesday/Thursday, full Friday), not a placeholder flip (Arizona Sports, "Cardinals-Cowboys Week 8 injury report: Jeremiyah Love slated to play against Dallas," 10/30-31). Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight had handled Arizona's backfield in his absence; expect Love back in the mix today, likely still sharing work early on. Downgrading tag from Injury to Healthy.

NEW SETBACK (11/3): left Sunday's Week 8 win at Dallas (33-30 OT) early with a new injury to the same right ankle that cost him Weeks 6-7, after it got rolled up on a tackle -- was questionable to return and did not come back. HC Mike LaFleur described it Monday as affecting "a new portion of the ankle" but did not share a timeline, saying he'd have more of an update later this week (Adam Schefter/ESPN, Yahoo Sports, Forbes, 11/1-3). Tyler Allgeier is the healthy lead back for now, with Bam Knight in the concussion protocol. Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty; recheck Wednesday's Week 9 practice report for Sunday's game vs. Seattle.

PLACED ON IR, CONFIRMED (11/3): Arizona officially placed Love on injured reserve for the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the 1st quarter of Sunday's Week 8 OT win at Dallas (11/1) -- he did not return to that game. Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and multiple outlets (Athlon, FTN, SI/OnSI, NFL.com, 11/3), he's expected to miss roughly 4-5 weeks, which would cost him Weeks 9-12 (Seattle, at the Rams, Kansas City, at Washington) before a possible Week 13 return. Tyler Allgeier is the clear backfield beneficiary -- he ran for 147 yards in the Dallas win and is now Arizona's lead back, with Bam Knight as the complementary piece. Upgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Long-Term Injury per the confirmed IR placement and 4+ game timeline.

Rashee Rice.name: Rashee Rice
bullets: Made his long-awaited return from suspension and offseason knee cleanup in Kansas City's Week 1 win over Denver, playing through it cleanly — 2 catches for 19 yards and a TD on just 2 targets as the offense eased him back in behind Kenneth Walker III's big rushing day.

UPDATE: usage has climbed hard each week since — 2 targets (Wk1) to 6 (Wk2) to 9 in Week 3 (7 catches, 88 yards) in a 49-play win over Miami where Mahomes only threw 24 times — a clear signal Rice is rounding back into the true WR1 role (NBC Sports, CBS Sports, RotoWire, 9/27).

NEW INJURY, CONFIRMED (10/4-5): suffered a non-contact hamstring injury early in Sunday's Week 4 game vs. the Raiders -- pulled up lame grabbing his leg after a short catch, was downgraded to doubtful, and did not return (SI, KCTV5, NBC Sports, ClutchPoints, AtoZ Sports, DraftKings Network, 10/4). IMPORTANT: search results for Rice are heavily cross-contaminated with his unrelated, much more serious September 2024 knee injury (LCL/hamstring-tendon surgery after a Mahomes collision, which was feared to be an ACL tear at the time) -- that 2024 story is NOT this year's news and should not be merged with it. This week's hamstring strain is a new, separate, and so far lower-severity issue. Downgrading tag from Healthy to the standard Injury tier pending a firmer timeline; keeping Elite Starter since the role/talent profile is unaffected when he's healthy.

UPDATE (10/16): a second straight full DNP Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the hamstring/knee injury; HC Andy Reid declined to commit to him practicing the rest of the week or playing Sunday, saying of hamstrings, "it could be a week, it could be two weeks, you don't know" (Arrowhead Pride). Trending toward sitting out Sunday's Week 6 game vs. the Chargers (10/18) rather than a continuation of last week's progress.

CONFIRMED (10/18): HC Andy Reid ruled Rice out for Sunday's Week 6 game vs. the Chargers after a third straight full DNP week with the hamstring strain suffered in Week 4 vs. the Raiders. Reid declined a firm number but said hamstring injuries typically cost players '1 to 2 weeks' and called him 'a pretty fast healer,' with Kansas City's primetime Week 7 game at Seattle floated as a realistic return target (Field Level Media, KCTV5, 10/16). Revising tag from the standard Injury tier to Short-Term Injury given that fairly firm 1-2 week framing.

UPDATE (10/22): did not practice Wednesday (10/21) with the hamstring -- HC Andy Reid confirmed the sit-out but said Rice "is improving," without predicting whether that's enough for Sunday Night Football at Seattle (10/25, 8:20pm ET, NBC). He needs to mix into practice Thursday/Friday for a real shot to play; keeping the Short-Term Injury tier given last week's firm 1-2-week framing from Reid is still the operative timeline.

WORSENED, TIMELINE SLIPPING (10/25): ruled out for tonight's Sunday Night Football game at Seattle -- a third straight missed game with the Week 4 hamstring strain. HC Andy Reid said this week that Rice 'is improving' but stopped short of clearing him, and the 1-2 week recovery framing Reid gave two weeks ago hasn't held up with this second straight absence. Revising tag from Short-Term Injury back to the standard Injury tier given the slipping timeline. Xavier Worthy continues to absorb the added target share.

NO REAL CHANGE (10/28): QUESTIONABLE flip likely the weekly placeholder reset -- no new practice/HC report found for Kansas City's Week 8 game at Denver (11/1), and no IR transaction found despite this now being a third straight missed game with the Week 4 (10/4) hamstring strain. Andy Reid said 10/21 Rice was "making progress" but gave no firm date. Timeline continues to slip past the original 1-2 week estimate -- a 4th straight absence would raise real IR risk; worth re-checking Thursday/Friday reports closely. Xavier Worthy continues to absorb the added targets.

CLEARED, ENDS 3-GAME ABSENCE (10/31-11/1): ESPN reports the Chiefs get Rice back for today's Week 8 game at Denver, confirming he's active after missing Weeks 5-7 with the Week 4 hamstring strain. He practiced fully this week with a near-certain play probability per FantasyPros aggregation. This heads off the real IR risk flagged last update after three straight absences. No box-score confirmation of workload yet; Xavier Worthy had been soaking up the added targets in his absence and should see his role contract back toward a distant-WR2 role now that Rice is back (see Worthy's note). Downgrading tag from Injury to Healthy.

CONFIRMED HEALTHY (11/6-7): carries no injury designation into Sunday's Week 9 home game vs. the Jets after a full practice week, confirming last week's clean return from the hamstring strain (Yahoo Sports/AtoZ Sports Chiefs beat, NBC Sports, 11/6). In his Week 8 return (11/1 vs. Denver), box-score aggregation (FanDuel recap) has him at 7 catches on 8 targets for 53 yards and a TD in a 28-24 loss -- a full workload, though this single-source stat line isn't independently cross-checked. Remains Healthy; Elite Starter stands.

Quinshon Judkins.name: Quinshon Judkins
bullets: Moved to the unambiguous RB1 spot on Cleveland's depth chart, ahead of Sampson and Sanders.
Battling a minor "nagging" injury that cost him two camp practices, but coaches aren't concerned — remains Cleveland's clear lead back over Dylan Sampson, Raheim Sanders, and Ahmani Marshall.
2025 2nd-round pick (36th overall, Ohio State), acquired via a Day 1 trade with Jacksonville.

Handled 12 of Cleveland's 15 RB carries plus 5 catches (17 touches, 48 total yards) in the Week 2 win over Tampa Bay, confirming him as the clear #1 back even in a tough matchup (CBS Sports, RotoWire).

NEW (10/13): picked up a new right ankle "tweak" in Sunday's Week 5 loss to the Jets (10/11); HC Kevin Stefanski called it day-to-day and said he'll "have a chance to play" Week 6 vs. Baltimore (RotoWire, NBC Sports, 10/12). Worth watching closely -- it's the same ankle/fibula area he surgically repaired after a dislocation/fracture last season, which has some beat writers flagging it even though team language is cautiously optimistic (Yahoo Sports/Heavy, Dawg Pound Daily, 10/12). No official Wed/Thu/Fri practice grade confirmed yet -- recheck before Week 6. If he sits, Raheim Sanders would be next in line, though Sanders himself left the same game with a hip injury and his own availability is a wrinkle (ESPN).

UPDATE (10/14): did NOT practice Wednesday with the ankle, per NBC Sports/RotoWire -- he was seen in the locker room without the walking boot he'd worn postgame Sunday, a mildly positive visual sign, but no Thursday/Friday practice grade had posted as of this update; his Week 6 call vs. Baltimore still hinges on the rest of the week's practice participation. Correction: the "day-to-day, has a chance to play" comment is attributed by multiple outlets to OC Todd Monken, not HC Kevin Stefanski as previously framed -- flagging since the original Stefanski attribution could not be verified. Separately, backup Raheim Sanders (hip, same Week 5 game) was placed on IR Tuesday (10/13), so he will NOT be available if Judkins sits -- Cleveland signed RB Audric Estime off Minnesota's practice squad as added depth, with Jaleel McLaughlin also in the mix. Downgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty and Wednesday DNP.

UPDATE (10/16): did not practice Wednesday or Thursday (10/14-10/15) with the ankle, though he was seen without his walking boot. Beat writers still frame him as "day-to-day" without a firm ruling, but Cleveland signed RB Audric Estime off Minnesota's practice squad this week as insurance, and Dawg Pound Daily reports the trend points toward Jaleel McLaughlin as Sunday's lead back vs. Baltimore (10/18) if Judkins sits.

CONFIRMED OUT (10/18): did not play in Cleveland's 13-10 win over Baltimore -- tested in pregame warmups on the ankle he tweaked in Week 5 (the same surgically-repaired ankle/fibula from last season) before being held out (USA Today/Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, 10/18). Jaleel McLaughlin (9 carries/41 yards) and Audric Estime (9 carries/19 yards, including the game-tying 2-yard TD) split the backfield work in his absence. No firm return timeline has been reported yet for Week 7; recheck Wednesday's practice report. Keeping the standard Injury tier given the real uncertainty and the injury's proximity to last year's more serious ankle/fibula fracture.

UPDATE (10/22): upgraded to a LIMITED practice participant Wednesday (10/21) -- a real step up from last week's DNP -- with Dylan Sampson also absent from Cleveland's non-participant list, per the Akron Beacon Journal's Chris Easterling. OC Todd Monken said he's "optimistic" about Judkins' availability for Sunday's Week 7 game vs. Tennessee but stopped short of guaranteeing it. Trending positive; keeping the standard Injury tier until he logs a full practice or a firmer designation posts.

CLEARED (10/25): carries no injury designation into today's Week 7 game vs. Tennessee -- the right ankle/fibula-area injury that cost him Week 6 has resolved enough for him to suit up, continuing last week's positive trend (upgraded to limited practice Wed 10/21, with HC Todd Monken 'optimistic'). Upgrading tag from the standard Injury tier to Healthy; remains Cleveland's unambiguous RB1.

BIG GAME (10/28): Cleared off Friday's injury report (ankle) and ran for 96 yards and 2 TDs on 17 carries in Cleveland's 27-24 win over Tennessee (10/25), continuing to look like the unambiguous RB1 coming off last week's ankle scare.

TreVeyon Henderson.name: TreVeyon Henderson
bullets: Missed the Week 1 loss to Seattle (ruled out Sept 8) after not practicing all week with an ankle injury; Rhamondre Stevenson started in his place.
Returned to practice Sept 14 and was a full participant that week, officially cleared to Active for Week 2.

UPDATE (9/30): clearly took over New England's lead-back role in Week 3's 35-6 loss at Jacksonville — 8 carries for 23 yards plus a target, compared to just 1 carry for Stevenson. Small sample in a blowout script, but the snap/touch distribution points to Henderson as the ascending back; worth tracking whether it holds up in a more competitive game script (RotoWire, dknetwork, 9/27-28).

NEW (10/13): suffered a new ankle injury in New England's 45-17 Week 5 win over Las Vegas (10/11) -- first questionable to return, then ruled out, finishing with just 4 carries for 22 yards and 1 catch for 16 yards. Sent for testing Monday (10/12); HC Mike Vrabel said he'd be evaluated (Patriots Communications, DraftSharks, PatsPulpit, 10/11-12). No official Week 6 designation confirmed yet. With Henderson banged up, Rhamondre Stevenson (see his note) is expected to see the bulk of the carries, a reversal of the recent Henderson-as-lead-back trend, with rookie Corey Kiner as the likely change-of-pace option (Yahoo Sports).

WORSENED (10/14): status flipped from QUESTIONABLE to DOUBTFUL for Week 6 (home vs. the Jets, Sun 10/18). HC Mike Vrabel confirmed Henderson got an MRI on the ankle Monday (10/12) and said he'd be evaluated, but no diagnosis or specific return timeline has been reported by Patriots beat writers as of this update -- treat the DOUBTFUL tag as a real escalation given the MRI, even though it's not yet matched by a published diagnosis. Upgrading tag from Health Watch to the standard Injury tier given the genuine uncertainty. Rhamondre Stevenson (see his note) is expected to handle the bulk of New England's backfield work if Henderson can't go, with rookie Corey Kiner as change-of-pace.

UPDATE (10/14): listed as a LIMITED practice participant Wednesday with the ankle (NBC Sports/RotoWire, CBS Sports, Yahoo) -- a step up from a full DNP, but multiple outlets report the Patriots are expected to officially rule him out Friday for Sunday's game vs. the Jets, though that's not yet guaranteed. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported, following Monday's MRI, that it's a high right ankle sprain, no surgery needed, but likely multiple weeks out -- the first real diagnosis/timeline attached to this injury.

UPDATE (10/16): a meaningfully better trend than last week's fear of a multi-week absence -- practiced in a non-contact jersey as a LIMITED participant both Wednesday and Thursday (10/14-10/15), the first real practice reps since Monday's ankle MRI, and was seen running and cutting on video Thursday. SI's Patriots Country and DraftSharks now frame him as a plausible Sunday option vs. the Jets (10/18), matching today's status flip from DOUBTFUL back to QUESTIONABLE -- though a full Friday practice is still needed to shed the tag entirely.

PLAYED ON PITCH COUNT (10/18): active and started but clearly managed coming off the ankle sprain -- 7 carries for 31 yards plus 1 catch for 9 yards in the 26-19 win over the Jets, and lost his first fumble of the season in the 3rd quarter (forced by Jets rookie David Bailey), which the Jets converted into points (ESPN, CBS Sports, NBC Sports, 10/18).
